short_description.id: Hong atau jiang adalah naga pelangi mitologi Tiongkok yang memiliki kepala pada kedua ujung tubuh.
short_description.en: Hong, or jiang, is a Chinese mythological rainbow dragon with heads at both ends.

long_description.id: Hong atau jiang adalah naga pelangi mitologi Tiongkok yang memiliki kepala pada kedua ujung tubuh. Bahasa Tiongkok membedakan kata hong, didong, dan ni untuk pelangi.
long_description.en: Hong, or jiang, is a Chinese mythological rainbow dragon with heads at both ends. Chinese distinguishes hong, didong, and ni as words related to rainbows.

long_description.id: Aksara pelangi kuno zaman Shang berbentuk naga melengkung berkepala dua. Shuowen Jiezi menggambarkan bentuk aksara hong sebagai mirip makhluk berjenis serangga atau reptil.
long_description.en: Ancient Shang rainbow characters depict an arched two-headed dragon. The Shuowen Jiezi describes the hong character's form as resembling a wug or reptile-like creature.

long_description.id: Hopkins menafsirkan aksara tulang ramalan sebagai pelangi yang berujung dua kepala naga, dan Eberhard mencatat relief awal menggambarkannya sebagai ular atau naga berkepala dua. Menurut Carr, pelangi dipandang sebagai pertanda buruk karena muncul setelah hujan, dan Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Shijing dan Huainanzi mengaitkannya dengan pertanda atau peringatan.
long_description.en: Hopkins reads the oracle-bone character as a rainbow ending in two dragon heads, and Eberhard notes that early reliefs show it as a snake or two-headed dragon. According to Carr, the rainbow was seen as an ill omen because it appears after rain, and Wikipedia notes that the Shijing and Huainanzi link it with omens or warnings.

long_description.id: Teks klasik menyebut hal terkait pelangi: Shijing memuat puisi berjudul 蝃蝀 yang menyebut sesuatu di timur yang tak berani ditunjuk, dan Liji mencatat pelangi mulai tampak pada bulan terakhir musim semi dan tak tampak pada bulan pertama musim dingin. Dalam mitos lain, Nuwa menambal langit dan konon menciptakan pelangi pertama.
long_description.en: Classical texts mention matters related to the rainbow: the Shijing has a poem titled 蝃蝀 that mentions something in the east no one dares point at, and the Liji records the rainbow beginning to appear in the last month of spring and being hidden in the first month of winter. In another myth, Nüwa patches the sky and supposedly creates the first rainbow.

cultural_context.id: Menurut kutipan Carr, orang Tiongkok memandang pelangi berkepala dua sebagai pertanda buruk karena muncul setelah hujan, berbeda dari naga long yang bertuah dan melambangkan hujan yang akan datang.
cultural_context.en: According to the Carr quotation, the Chinese regarded the two-headed rainbow as an ill omen because it appears after rain, unlike the auspicious long dragon symbolizing forthcoming rain.

claims.quote: Hong or jiang (Chinese: 虹; pinyin: hóng or jiàng; Wade–Giles: hung or chiang; lit. 'rainbow') is a Chinese dragon with two heads on each end in Chinese mythology, comparable with Rainbow Serpent legends in various cultures and mythologies.

statement.id: Hong atau jiang adalah naga pelangi mitologi Tiongkok yang memiliki kepala pada kedua ujung tubuh.
statement.en: Hong, or jiang, is a Chinese mythological rainbow dragon with heads at both ends.

claims.quote: Chinese has three "rainbow" words, regular hóng (虹), literary dìdōng (蝃蝀), and ní (蜺; "secondary rainbow").

statement.id: Bahasa Tiongkok membedakan kata hong, didong, dan ni untuk pelangi.
statement.en: Chinese distinguishes hong, didong, and ni as words related to rainbows.

claims.quote: However, the oldest characters for "rainbow" in Shang dynasty oracle bone script were pictographs of an arched dragon or serpent with open-mouthed heads at both ends.

statement.id: Aksara pelangi kuno zaman Shang berbentuk naga melengkung berkepala dua.
statement.en: Ancient Shang rainbow characters depict an arched two-headed dragon.

claims.quote: The 121 CE Shuowen Jiezi dictionary, the first Chinese character dictionary, described the seal character for hong (虹; 'rainbow') as 狀似蟲; 'shaped like a wug'. Over 18 centuries later, Hopkins described the recently discovered oracle character for 虹.

statement.id: Shuowen Jiezi menggambarkan bentuk aksara hong sebagai mirip makhluk berjenis serangga atau reptil.
statement.en: The Shuowen Jiezi describes the hong character's form as resembling a wug or reptile-like creature.

claims.quote: Although many ancient cultures believed rainbows were good omens,"Carr explains, "the Chinese saw them as meteorological disasters. Unlike the auspicious [long] 龍 dragon symbolizing forthcoming rain, the two-headed [hong] 虹 was inauspicious because it appeared after a rain shower."

statement.id: Michael Carr, dikutip Wikipedia, menyatakan bahwa orang Tiongkok melihat pelangi sebagai bencana meteorologis; berbeda dengan naga long (龍) yang membawa hujan dan bertuah, hong (虹) yang berkepala dua dianggap tidak bertuah karena muncul setelah hujan.
statement.en: Carr, as quoted in Wikipedia, states that the Chinese saw rainbows as meteorological disasters; unlike the auspicious long (龍) dragon that symbolizes coming rain, the two-headed hong (虹) was inauspicious because it appeared after a rain shower.

claims.quote: Hopkins described the recently discovered oracle character for 虹 ... We should, I now feel sure, discern a Rainbow terminating in two animal heads. But of what animal? Certainly of the Dragon, must be the answer.

statement.id: Hopkins, dikutip Wikipedia, menafsirkan huruf ramalan tulang kuno untuk pelangi sebagai pelangi yang berujung dua kepala hewan, dan menyimpulkan hewan itu adalah naga.
statement.en: Hopkins, as quoted in Wikipedia, reads the oracle-bone character for the rainbow as a rainbow ending in two animal heads, and concludes the animal must be the dragon.

claims.quote: Eberhard notes, "In early reliefs, the rainbow is shown as a snake or a dragon with two heads. In West China they give it the head of a donkey, and it rates as a lucky symbol."

statement.id: Eberhard, dikutip Wikipedia, mencatat bahwa relief awal menggambarkan pelangi sebagai ular atau naga berkepala dua, dan di Tiongkok Barat diberi kepala keledai serta dianggap lambang keberuntungan.
statement.en: Eberhard, as quoted in Wikipedia, notes that early reliefs show the rainbow as a snake or two-headed dragon, and in West China it is given a donkey's head and counted a lucky symbol.

claims.quote: The Shijing has the oldest known textual usages of hong and didong, and both are bad omens.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, Shijing memuat pemakaian tertulis tertua yang diketahui untuk hong dan didong, dan keduanya pertanda buruk.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, the Shijing has the oldest known textual usages of hong and didong, and both are bad omens.

claims.quote: The Huainanzi says both rainbows and comets were warnings from tian "heaven; god".

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, Huainanzi menyebut pelangi dan komet sebagai peringatan dari tian (langit atau dewa).
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, the Huainanzi says both rainbows and comets were warnings from tian (heaven or god).

claims.quote: Lastly, another Chinese rainbow myth involves the creator Nüwa 女媧 repairing a crack in the sky caused by the water deity Gong Gong 共工 (cf. 虹 ). She supposedly created the first rainbow by melting stones of 5 or 7 different colors to patch the sky.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, mitos pelangi Tiongkok lain menyebut Nuwa (女媧) memperbaiki retakan langit akibat dewa air Gong Gong (共工), dan konon menciptakan pelangi pertama dengan melelehkan batu lima atau tujuh warna untuk menambal langit.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, another Chinese rainbow myth has Nüwa (女媧) repairing a crack in the sky caused by the water deity Gong Gong (共工), and supposedly creating the first rainbow by melting stones of five or seven colors to patch the sky.

short_description.id: Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy") adalah monster air mirip ular dalam cerita rakyat New York yang dilaporkan sejak 1886 [hudson-river-monster-c01].
short_description.en: The Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy") is a serpentine water monster of New York folklore reported since 1886 [hudson-river-monster-c01].

long_description.id: Hudson River Monster, yang populer dengan nama "Kipsy", adalah monster air mirip ular yang dilaporkan di Sungai Hudson dan Pelabuhan New York sejak 1886 [hudson-river-monster-c01]. Nama Kipsy diyakini berasal dari kota Poughkeepsie [hudson-river-monster-c02]. Laporan pertamanya muncul dalam artikel surat kabar tahun 1886 yang menyebutnya "ular laut" [hudson-river-monster-c03].
long_description.en: The Hudson River Monster, popularly "Kipsy", is a serpentine water monster reported along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886 [hudson-river-monster-c01]. The name Kipsy is believed to come from Poughkeepsie [hudson-river-monster-c02]. It was first reported in 1886 newspaper articles calling it "the sea serpent" [hudson-river-monster-c03].

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah ensiklopedia folklor Amerika, legenda setempat bercerita tentang makhluk purba yang dilihat banyak pelaut di Sungai Hudson dan digambarkan sebagai hiu, manatee, ular laut, atau dinosaurus [hudson-river-monster-c05]. Pada 1886, puluhan orang bersikeras telah melihat ular laut sepanjang 100 kaki berkepala besar yang berulang kali menegak setinggi sepuluh kaki dari air [hudson-river-monster-c06]. Ensiklopedia yang sama mencatat bahwa makhluk yang disebut-sebut itu akhirnya diidentifikasi sebagai balok kayu terbakar dari kapal uap Daniel Drew [hudson-river-monster-c07]. Banyak sumber mengaitkan Kipsy dengan legenda pribumi atau awak kapal Henry Hudson, tetapi tidak ada yang menyertakan dokumentasi [hudson-river-monster-c04].
long_description.en: According to an encyclopedia of American folklore, local legends tell of an ancient creature that many sailors spotted on the Hudson River, described as a shark, manatee, sea serpent, or dinosaur [hudson-river-monster-c05]. Dozens of people in 1886 swore they had spotted a sea serpent about 100 feet long with a huge head, which kept rising some ten feet above the river [hudson-river-monster-c06]. The same encyclopedia reports that the supposed monster turned out to be a charred timber from the steamship Daniel Drew [hudson-river-monster-c07]. Many sources link Kipsy to Native American legends or to the crew of Henry Hudson, but none provide documentation [hudson-river-monster-c04].

long_description.id: Kipsy muncul kembali di New York Times pada 2006 ketika saksi di Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, dan Kingsland Point di Sleepy Hollow melaporkan melihat manatee seberat 1.000 pon [hudson-river-monster-c08]. Satu-satunya gambar Kipsy yang ada berupa lukisan, karena belum ada yang berhasil memotretnya [hudson-river-monster-c09]. Sebuah mural di Poughkeepsie karya Margaret dan Richard Crenson tahun 1989 menampilkan Kipsy sebagai ular mitos [hudson-river-monster-c10], dan pada 2009 seniman Carla Goldberg menggambarkannya bermain bola dengan salah satu kepala dewi sungai [hudson-river-monster-c11].
long_description.en: Kipsy turned up in the New York Times again in 2006, after witnesses at Chelsea Piers, in Westchester County and at Kingsland Point in Sleepy Hollow reported a manatee weighing 1,000 pounds [hudson-river-monster-c08]. Every existing picture of Kipsy is a painting, since nobody has managed to photograph it [hudson-river-monster-c09]. A 1989 Poughkeepsie mural by Margaret and Richard Crenson shows Kipsy as a mythical serpent [hudson-river-monster-c10], and in 2009 the artist Carla Goldberg portrayed it playing ball with one of the river goddess's heads [hudson-river-monster-c11].

did_you_know.id: Satu laporan ular laut raksasa di Sungai Hudson akhirnya diidentifikasi sebagai balok kayu terbakar dari kapal uap Daniel Drew [hudson-river-monster-c07].
did_you_know.en: One report of a giant sea serpent in the Hudson River was ultimately identified as a burned timber from the steamship Daniel Drew [hudson-river-monster-c07].

claims.quote: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster, popularly known as "Kipsy" or less commonly "Keepsie" or "Libby" (after the Statue of Liberty) is an aquatic serpentine monster reportedly spotted along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat New York, Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", juga "Keepsie" atau "Libby") adalah monster air mirip ular yang dilaporkan terlihat di Sungai Hudson dan Pelabuhan New York sejak 1886.
statement.en: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", also "Keepsie" or "Libby") is a serpentine water monster reported along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.

claims.quote: The name "Kipsy" is believed to derive from Poughkeepsie, a city located along the river.

statement.id: Nama "Kipsy" diyakini berasal dari Poughkeepsie, kota di tepi sungai itu.
statement.en: The name "Kipsy" is believed to come from Poughkeepsie, a city on the river.

claims.quote: The creature was first reported in a series of newspaper articles published in 1886, in which it is referred to simply as "the sea serpent."

statement.id: Makhluk ini pertama kali dilaporkan dalam serangkaian artikel surat kabar tahun 1886 yang menyebutnya "ular laut".
statement.en: It was first reported in 1886 newspaper articles that called it simply "the sea serpent."

claims.quote: Though many sources allege that "Kipsy" was described in Native American legends or spotted by Henry Hudson's crew as the sailed up the Hudson River on the Halve Maen, none provide any documentation in support of these claims.

statement.id: Banyak sumber menyebut Kipsy ada dalam legenda pribumi atau dilihat awak Henry Hudson, tetapi tidak ada yang menyertakan bukti dokumen.
statement.en: Many sources claim Kipsy appears in Native American legends or was seen by Henry Hudson's crew, but none provide documentation.

claims.quote: Poughkeepsie is the city for which Kipsy is named, and its local legends talk about an ancient creature that many sailors spotted on the Hudson River, describing the creature as a shark, manatee, sea serpent, or dinosaur.

statement.id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, Kipsy dinamai dari kota Poughkeepsie, dan legenda setempat bercerita tentang makhluk purba yang dilihat banyak pelaut di Sungai Hudson, digambarkan sebagai hiu, manatee, ular laut, atau dinosaurus.
statement.en: According to this encyclopedia, Kipsy is named for Poughkeepsie, and its local legends tell of an ancient creature that many sailors spotted on the Hudson River, described as a shark, manatee, sea serpent, or dinosaur.

claims.quote: In 1886 dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.

statement.id: Pada 1886, puluhan orang bersikeras telah melihat ular laut sepanjang 100 kaki berkepala besar di Sungai Hudson yang berulang kali menegak setinggi sepuluh kaki ke udara.
statement.en: In 1886, dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River, repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.

claims.quote: As it turned out, the so-called monster was identified as a burned timber from the steamship Daniel Drew.

statement.id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, makhluk yang disebut-sebut itu akhirnya diidentifikasi sebagai balok kayu terbakar dari kapal uap Daniel Drew.
statement.en: According to this encyclopedia, the so-called monster was identified as a burned timber from the steamship Daniel Drew.

claims.quote: Kipsy reappeared in the New York Times in 2006 when witnesses at Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, and Kingsland Point in Sleepy Hollow reported that they had seen a manatee with a weight of 1,000 pounds.

statement.id: Kipsy muncul kembali di New York Times pada 2006 ketika saksi di Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, dan Kingsland Point di Sleepy Hollow melaporkan telah melihat manatee seberat 1.000 pon.
statement.en: Kipsy reappeared in the New York Times in 2006 when witnesses at Chelsea Piers, Westchester County, and Kingsland Point in Sleepy Hollow reported seeing a manatee weighing 1,000 pounds.

claims.quote: So far, the only images of Kipsy that exist are paintings because no one has been successful in photographing the lake monster.

statement.id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, satu-satunya gambar Kipsy yang ada adalah lukisan, karena belum ada yang berhasil memotret monster danau itu.
statement.en: According to this encyclopedia, the only images of Kipsy that exist are paintings, because no one has succeeded in photographing the lake monster.

claims.quote: a Poughkeepsie mural created by local artists Margaret and Richard Crenson on the Hudson Valley Office Furniture building in 1989 shows Kipsy as a mythical serpent living in the Hudson River.

statement.id: Mural di Poughkeepsie karya seniman lokal Margaret dan Richard Crenson pada gedung Hudson Valley Office Furniture tahun 1989 menampilkan Kipsy sebagai ular mitos yang hidup di Sungai Hudson.
statement.en: A Poughkeepsie mural by local artists Margaret and Richard Crenson on the Hudson Valley Office Furniture building in 1989 shows Kipsy as a mythical serpent living in the Hudson River.

claims.quote: In her 2009 visual artwork series Bodice of the Goddess—The Secret Life of the Hudson River, American artist Carla Goldberg portrayed Kipsy as playing ball with one of the river goddess’s heads.

statement.id: Dalam serial karya seni visualnya tahun 2009, Bodice of the Goddess—The Secret Life of the Hudson River, seniman Amerika Carla Goldberg menggambarkan Kipsy bermain bola dengan salah satu kepala dewi sungai.

short_description.id: Huoshu adalah hewan fantastis Tiongkok yang namanya berarti tikus api, dikatakan hidup di dalam api dan bulunya menjadi kain yang bersih bila dibakar.
short_description.en: Huoshu is a Chinese fantastical beast whose name means fire rat, said to live in fire with hair that makes cloth cleaned by burning.

long_description.id: Huoshu adalah hewan fantastis Tiongkok yang namanya berarti tikus api. Hewan ini dipercaya tinggal dalam api pada pohon yang tidak terbakar. Teks Shenyijing menyebut gunung api tempat pohon-pohon tak habis terbakar tumbuh dan tikus api hidup di dalamnya.
long_description.en: Huoshu is a Chinese fantastical beast whose name means fire rat. The animal is said to dwell in fire within trees that cannot burn. The Shenyijing text mentions a fire mountain where inexhaustible trees grow and the fire rat lives within.

long_description.id: Kain dari bulunya dipercaya menjadi bersih ketika dibakar. Shenyi Jing menggambarkan tikus dalam api dengan rambut putih halus seperti sutra; dalam teks yang dibuka, tikus itu tinggal di dalam api, kadang keluar dengan bulu putih, dan mati bila disiram air, sedangkan bulunya dipintal menjadi kain yang kotornya dibersihkan dengan api. Soushen Ji menghubungkan sumber kain tahan api dengan Gunung Api di Kunlun. Shizhou Ji menyebut hewan mirip tikus bernama huo guang shou di pulau Yan.
long_description.en: Cloth woven from its hair is believed to become clean when burned. The Shenyi Jing describes a fire-dwelling mouse with fine white hair like silk; in the text consulted, the mouse lives in the fire, sometimes comes out with white hair, and dies if drenched with water, while its hair is spun into cloth whose dirt is cleaned away with fire. The Soushen Ji links the source of fireproof cloth with the Mountain of Flame at Kunlun. The Shizhou Ji describes a rat-like huo guang shou on Yan island.

Cloth woven from its hair is said to became clean when burnt, and is thus equated with the item known as huo huan bu (火浣布) or "fire-laundered cloth", which is thought in reality to have been a type of asbestos cloth.

According to this work, the mountain's beast are the source of hair for making the "fire-laundered cloth".

statement.id: Teks Shenyijing menyebut bahwa dalam api pada pohon yang tak habis terbakar ada seekor tikus seberat seribu jin dengan bulu panjang lebih dari dua chi sehalus sutra; ia tinggal di dalam api, tampak merah menyala, kadang keluar dengan bulu putih, dan mati bila diusir dan disiram air.
statement.en: The Shenyijing text says that in the fire among inexhaustible trees there is a mouse weighing a thousand jin with hair over two chi long, fine as silk; it dwells in the fire, glowing red, sometimes comes out with white hair, and dies if chased and drenched with water.

statement.en: The Shenyijing text says its hair is spun and woven into cloth, and when the cloth is soiled, burning it in fire makes it clean.

text.id: Cerita hare bertanduk jauh lebih tua; jackalope Amerika dipopulerkan sejak 1930-an.
text.en: Tales of horned hares are far older; the American jackalope was popularized from the 1930s.

short_description.id: Jackalope adalah hewan mitos Amerika Utara berupa jackrabbit bertanduk antelop, yang dipopulerkan lewat awetan taksidermi di Wyoming pada 1930-an.
short_description.en: The jackalope is a mythical animal of North America, a jackrabbit with antelope horns, popularized through taxidermy mounts in Wyoming in the 1930s.

long_description.id: Jackalope adalah hewan mitos dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Utara yang digambarkan sebagai jackrabbit bertanduk antelop; namanya gabungan jackrabbit dan antelope. Folklorwan memandangnya sebagai salah satu hewan cerita bualan yang disebut fearsome critters.
long_description.en: The jackalope is a mythical animal in North American folklore described as a jackrabbit with antelope horns, and its name blends jackrabbit and antelope. Folklorists regard it as one of the tall-tale animals called fearsome critters.

long_description.id: Pada 1930-an Douglas Herrick dan saudaranya, pemburu yang terampil taksidermi, mempopulerkan jackalope Amerika dengan menempelkan tanduk rusa pada bangkai jackrabbit dan menjualnya kepada sebuah hotel di Douglas, Wyoming. The New York Times mengaitkan asalnya dengan acara berburu tahun 1932, dan awetan pertama dijual seharga $10 kepada Roy Ball, yang memajangnya di La Bonte Hotel; kepalanya dicuri pada 1977.
long_description.en: In the 1930s Douglas Herrick and his brother, hunters skilled in taxidermy, made the American jackalope famous by fixing deer antlers to a jackrabbit carcass and selling the result to a hotel in Douglas, Wyoming. The New York Times traces its origin to a 1932 hunting outing, and the first mount was sold for $10 to Roy Ball, who displayed it in the La Bonte Hotel; its head was stolen in 1977.

long_description.id: Legenda dasarnya mungkin berkaitan dengan cerita serupa dalam budaya lain: sebuah karya Persia abad ke-13 menggambarkan kelinci bertanduk tunggal, wolpertinger muncul di Bavaria, dan legenda Huichol menyebut kelinci bertanduk. Pada akhir abad ke-18 ilmuwan umumnya menolak hare bertanduk sebagai spesies biologis, dan para peneliti menduga sebagian cerita itu terinspirasi oleh kelinci yang terinfeksi virus papiloma Shope, yang menumbuhkan benjolan mirip tanduk.
long_description.en: The underlying legend may be related to similar stories in other cultures: a Persian work of the 13th century shows a one-horned rabbit, the wolpertinger belongs to Bavaria, and Huichol legends speak of a horned rabbit. By the end of the 18th century scientists generally rejected horned hares as a biological species, and researchers suggest some of these tales were inspired by rabbits infected with the Shope papilloma virus, which grows horn-like tumors.

long_description.id: Cerita bualan menyebut jackalope begitu berbahaya sehingga pemburu dianjurkan memakai pipa cerobong di kaki agar tidak ditanduk, dapat menirukan suara manusia, hanya berkembang biak saat kilat menyambar, dan dapat dipikat dengan wiski. Di Douglas, Kamar Dagang menerbitkan lisensi berburu jackalope untuk satu hari musim berburu, 31 Juni.
long_description.en: Tall tales say jackalopes are so dangerous that hunters are told to strap stovepipes to their legs to avoid being gored, that they can imitate human voices, that they breed only during lightning, and that they can be lured with whiskey. In Douglas the Chamber of Commerce issues jackalope hunting licenses for a one-day season on June 31.

cultural_context.id: Folklorwan memandang jackalope sebagai salah satu hewan cerita bualan yang cocok untuk tipuan jenaka oleh pengusaha yang mencari perhatian bagi keuntungan pribadi atau daerahnya. Awetannya kini ada di banyak bar di Amerika Serikat, dan toko wisata menjual kartu pos serta pernak-pernik jackalope.
cultural_context.en: Folklorists see the jackalope as one of the tall-tale animals that suit comic hoaxes by entrepreneurs seeking attention for their own or their region's fortune. Its mounts now hang in many bars in the United States, and tourist stores sell jackalope postcards and trinkets.

literal_meaning.en: A portmanteau of jackrabbit and antelope.

claims.quote: The word jackalope is a portmanteau of jackrabbit and antelope.

statement.id: Kata jackalope adalah gabungan (portmanteau) dari jackrabbit dan antelope.
statement.en: The word jackalope is a portmanteau of jackrabbit and antelope.

claims.quote: In the 1930s, Douglas Herrick and his brother, hunters with taxidermy skills, popularized the American jackalope by grafting deer antlers onto a jackrabbit carcass and selling the combination to a local hotel in Douglas, Wyoming.

statement.id: Pada 1930-an, Douglas Herrick dan saudaranya, pemburu yang terampil membuat awetan taksidermi, mempopulerkan jackalope Amerika dengan menempelkan tanduk rusa pada bangkai jackrabbit dan menjual hasilnya kepada sebuah hotel setempat di Douglas, Wyoming.
statement.en: In the 1930s Douglas Herrick and his brother, hunters with taxidermy skills, popularized the American jackalope by grafting deer antlers onto a jackrabbit carcass and selling it to a local hotel in Douglas, Wyoming.

claims.quote: Researchers suggest that at least some of the tales of horned hares were inspired by sightings of rabbits infected with the Shope papilloma virus.

statement.id: Para peneliti menduga sebagian cerita tentang hare bertanduk terinspirasi oleh penampakan kelinci yang terinfeksi virus papiloma Shope.
statement.en: Researchers suggest that at least some of the tales of horned hares were inspired by sightings of rabbits infected with the Shope papilloma virus.

claims.quote: Folklorists see the jackalope as one of a group of tall tale animals, known as fearsome critters, common to North American culture since the turn of the twentieth century. These fabulous beasts appear in tall tales and lend themselves to comic hoaxes by entrepreneurs who seek attention for their own personal or the region's fortune.

statement.id: Para folklorwan memandang jackalope sebagai salah satu kelompok hewan cerita bualan, yang dikenal sebagai fearsome critters, yang lazim dalam budaya Amerika Utara sejak pergantian abad ke-20. Binatang-binatang ajaib ini muncul dalam cerita bualan dan cocok untuk tipuan jenaka oleh pengusaha yang mencari perhatian bagi keuntungan pribadi atau daerahnya.
statement.en: Folklorists see the jackalope as one of a group of tall-tale animals, known as fearsome critters, common to North American culture since the turn of the twentieth century; these fabulous beasts appear in tall tales and suit comic hoaxes by entrepreneurs seeking attention for their own or the region's fortune.

claims.quote: The jackalope is a mythical animal of North American folklore described as a jackrabbit with antelope horns.

statement.id: Jackalope adalah hewan mitos dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Utara yang digambarkan sebagai jackrabbit bertanduk antelop.
statement.en: The jackalope is a mythical animal of North American folklore described as a jackrabbit with antelope horns.

claims.quote: Stuffed and mounted, jackalopes are found in many bars and other places in the United States; stores catering to tourists sell jackalope postcards and other paraphernalia

statement.id: Dalam bentuk awetan, jackalope ditemukan di banyak bar dan tempat lain di Amerika Serikat; toko untuk wisatawan menjual kartu pos jackalope dan pernak-pernik lain.
statement.en: Stuffed and mounted, jackalopes are found in many bars and other places in the United States, and stores catering to tourists sell jackalope postcards and other paraphernalia.

claims.quote: In 2005, the legislature of Wyoming considered a bill to make the jackalope the state's official mythological creature. It passed the House by a 45–12 margin, but the session ended before the Senate could take up the bill, which died.

statement.id: Pada 2005, legislatur Wyoming mempertimbangkan rancangan undang-undang untuk menjadikan jackalope makhluk mitologis resmi negara bagian. RUU itu lolos di DPR dengan selisih 45–12, tetapi sidang berakhir sebelum Senat membahasnya sehingga RUU itu gugur.
statement.en: In 2005 the Wyoming legislature considered a bill to make the jackalope the state's official mythological creature; it passed the House 45–12 but the session ended before the Senate could take it up, and it died.

claims.quote: A 13th-century Persian work depicts a rabbit with a single horn, like a unicorn. In Europe, the horned rabbit appeared in Medieval and Renaissance folklore in Bavaria (the wolpertinger) and elsewhere.

statement.id: Sebuah karya Persia abad ke-13 menggambarkan kelinci bertanduk tunggal seperti unicorn. Di Eropa, kelinci bertanduk muncul dalam cerita rakyat Abad Pertengahan dan Renaisans di Bavaria (wolpertinger) dan tempat lain.
statement.en: A 13th-century Persian work depicts a rabbit with a single horn, like a unicorn, and in Europe the horned rabbit appeared in Medieval and Renaissance folklore in Bavaria (the wolpertinger) and elsewhere.

claims.quote: These early scientific texts described and illustrated the hybrids as though they were real creatures, but by the end of the 18th century scientists generally rejected the idea of horned hares as a biological species.

statement.id: Teks-teks ilmiah awal itu menguraikan dan menggambarkan hibrida tersebut seolah makhluk nyata, tetapi pada akhir abad ke-18 para ilmuwan umumnya menolak gagasan hare bertanduk sebagai spesies biologis.
statement.en: These early scientific texts described and illustrated the hybrids as though they were real creatures, but by the end of the 18th century scientists generally rejected the idea of horned hares as a biological species.

claims.quote: In Central America, mythological references to a horned rabbit creature can be found in Huichol legends. The Huichol oral tradition has passed down tales of a horned rabbit and of the deer getting horns from the rabbit.

statement.id: Di Amerika Tengah, rujukan mitologis pada makhluk kelinci bertanduk terdapat dalam legenda Huichol. Tradisi lisan Huichol mewariskan kisah tentang kelinci bertanduk dan tentang rusa yang mendapat tanduk dari kelinci itu.
statement.en: In Central America mythological references to a horned rabbit creature are found in Huichol legends, whose oral tradition has passed down tales of a horned rabbit and of the deer getting horns from the rabbit.

claims.quote: The New York Times attributes the American jackalope's origin to a 1932 hunting outing involving Douglas Herrick (1920–2003) of Douglas, Wyoming.

statement.id: The New York Times mengaitkan asal jackalope Amerika dengan sebuah acara berburu tahun 1932 yang melibatkan Douglas Herrick (1920–2003) dari Douglas, Wyoming.
statement.en: The New York Times attributes the American jackalope's origin to a 1932 hunting outing involving Douglas Herrick (1920–2003) of Douglas, Wyoming.

claims.quote: The first jackalope the brothers put together was sold for $10 to Roy Ball, who displayed it in Douglas' La Bonte Hotel. The mounted head was stolen in 1977.

statement.id: Jackalope pertama yang dirakit kedua bersaudara itu dijual seharga $10 kepada Roy Ball, yang memajangnya di La Bonte Hotel di Douglas. Kepala awetan itu dicuri pada 1977.
statement.en: The first jackalope the brothers put together was sold for $10 to Roy Ball, who displayed it in Douglas' La Bonte Hotel; the mounted head was stolen in 1977.

claims.quote: The jackalope became a popular local attraction in Douglas, where the Chamber of Commerce issues Jackalope Hunting Licenses to tourists. The tags are good for hunting during official jackalope season, which occurs for only one day: June 31 (a nonexistent date as June has 30 days), from midnight to 2 a.m.

statement.id: Jackalope menjadi atraksi lokal populer di Douglas, tempat Kamar Dagang menerbitkan Lisensi Berburu Jackalope bagi wisatawan. Tanda itu berlaku untuk berburu pada musim jackalope resmi yang hanya satu hari: 31 Juni (tanggal yang tidak ada karena Juni hanya 30 hari), dari tengah malam hingga pukul 2 pagi.
statement.en: The jackalope became a popular local attraction in Douglas, where the Chamber of Commerce issues Jackalope Hunting Licenses to tourists, good for the one-day official jackalope season on June 31 (a nonexistent date), from midnight to 2 a.m.

claims.quote: Jackalopes are said to be so dangerous that hunters are advised to wear stovepipes on their legs to keep from being gored.

statement.id: Jackalope dikatakan begitu berbahaya sehingga pemburu dianjurkan memakai pipa cerobong di kaki agar tidak ditanduk.
statement.en: Jackalopes are said to be so dangerous that hunters are advised to wear stovepipes on their legs to keep from being gored.

claims.quote: The jackalope can imitate the human voice, according to legend. During the days of the Old West, when cowboys gathered by the campfires singing at night, jackalopes could be heard mimicking their voices or singing along, usually as a tenor.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, jackalope dapat menirukan suara manusia. Pada masa Wild West, ketika koboi berkumpul di api unggun dan bernyanyi di malam hari, jackalope terdengar menirukan suara mereka atau ikut bernyanyi, biasanya sebagai tenor.
statement.en: According to legend the jackalope can imitate the human voice; in the Old West, when cowboys sang around campfires at night, jackalopes could be heard mimicking them or singing along, usually as a tenor.

claims.quote: One of the ways to catch a jackalope is to entice it with whiskey, the jackalope's beverage of choice.

statement.id: Salah satu cara menangkap jackalope adalah memikatnya dengan wiski, minuman favoritnya.
statement.en: One of the ways to catch a jackalope is to entice it with whiskey, the jackalope's beverage of choice.

claims.quote: It is said that jackalopes, the rare Lepus antilocapra, breed only during lightning flashes and that their antlers make the act difficult despite the hare's reputation for fertility.

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa jackalope, Lepus antilocapra yang langka, hanya berkembang biak saat kilat menyambar dan bahwa tanduknya mempersulit hal itu meskipun hare terkenal subur.
statement.en: It is said that jackalopes, the rare Lepus antilocapra, breed only during lightning flashes and that their antlers make the act difficult despite the hare's reputation for fertility.

claims.quote: According to Dorson, in Mythical Creatures of the North Country (1969), historian Walker D. Wyman acknowledged the existence of what he called the Alkali Area Jackalope of the western United States. However, he expressed doubt that it predated the Jack-pine Jackalope of Minnesota and Wisconsin

statement.id: Menurut Dorson, dalam Mythical Creatures of the North Country (1969), sejarawan Walker D. Wyman mengakui adanya apa yang ia sebut Jackalope Area Alkali di Amerika Serikat bagian barat, tetapi meragukan bahwa ia lebih tua daripada Jackalope Jack-pine di Minnesota dan Wisconsin.
statement.en: According to Dorson, in Mythical Creatures of the North Country (1969), historian Walker D. Wyman acknowledged the Alkali Area Jackalope of the western United States but doubted it predated the Jack-pine Jackalope of Minnesota and Wisconsin.

claims.quote: The underlying legend of the jackalope, upon which the Wyoming taxidermists were building, may be related to similar stories in other cultures and other historical times.

statement.id: Legenda dasar jackalope, yang dikembangkan para taksidermis Wyoming, mungkin berkaitan dengan cerita serupa dalam budaya dan masa sejarah lain.
statement.en: The underlying legend of the jackalope, which the Wyoming taxidermists were building on, may be related to similar stories in other cultures and other historical times.

claims.quote: Among them is Juan and the Jackalope: A Children's Book in Verse by Rudolfo Anaya.

statement.id: Salah satunya adalah Juan and the Jackalope: A Children's Book in Verse karya Rudolfo Anaya.
statement.en: Among the books featuring the jackalope is Juan and the Jackalope: A Children's Book in Verse by Rudolfo Anaya.

statement.id: Cerpen "Jackalope Wives" karya Ursula Vernon dinominasikan untuk Nebula Award 2014.
statement.en: A short story, "Jackalope Wives" by Ursula Vernon, has been nominated for a 2014 Nebula Award.

claims.quote: Ralph and Douglas Herrick, taxidermists in Douglas, Wyoming, admitted to conjuring up the American jackalope that we know today. After returning from a hunting trip, the Herrick Brothers serendipitously noticed a dead jackrabbit lying next to a pair of antlers on the floor of their taxidermy shop.

statement.en: Ralph and Douglas Herrick, taxidermists in Douglas, Wyoming, admitted to conjuring up the American jackalope we know today; after a hunting trip they happened to notice a dead jackrabbit lying next to a pair of antlers on the floor of their taxidermy shop.

claims.quote: Over time, Douglas, Wyoming, became known as the Jackalope Capital of the World, and eventually put up an 8-foot jackalope statue in the city center.

statement.id: Seiring waktu, Douglas, Wyoming, dikenal sebagai Ibu Kota Jackalope Dunia dan akhirnya memasang patung jackalope setinggi 8 kaki di pusat kota.

claims.quote: We see jackalopes in art, gas stations, and occasionally even featured in bills brought up by state legislatures.

statement.id: Jackalope terlihat dalam seni, di pom bensin, dan kadang bahkan menjadi bahan rancangan undang-undang yang diajukan legislatur negara bagian.

short_description.id: Jiaotu (椒図) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga menurut sumber berbahasa Jepang dan sebuah teks klasik. Ia digambarkan menyerupai siput atau kerang, gemar menutup, dan dikaitkan dengan pintu.
short_description.en: Jiaotu (椒図) is one of the nine sons of the dragon according to a Japanese-language source and a classical text. It is pictured as snail- or shell-like, fond of closing things, and associated with doors.

long_description.id: Jiaotu (椒図, juga ditulis 椒圖, dibaca しょうず dalam bahasa Jepang) adalah salah satu dari 竜生九子, "sembilan putra naga". Sembilan putra naga adalah sebutan tradisional bagi sekelompok makhluk mitos yang gambarnya muncul pada jenis dekorasi tertentu. Sumber berbahasa Jepang menyamakan wujud Jiaotu dengan katak dan hewan bercangkang.
long_description.en: Jiaotu (椒図, also written 椒圖, read しょうず in Japanese) is one of the 竜生九子, the "nine sons of the dragon". "Nine sons of the dragon" is a traditional label for a group of mythical creatures whose images appear in certain kinds of decoration. The Japanese source compares Jiaotu's form with frogs and shelled creatures.

long_description.id: Menurut entri 椒圖 dalam 升菴集, sembilan putra naga tidak menjadi naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran sendiri; 椒圖 berbentuk seperti siput, gemar menutup, sehingga ditempatkan di atas pintu. Sumber berbahasa Jepang menyebut ia menyukai tempat tertutup, menolak orang asing masuk ke tempat tinggalnya, dan karena itu digambarkan menggigit cincin pegangan pintu.
long_description.en: According to the 椒圖 entry in the 升菴集, the nine sons of the dragon do not become dragons and each has its own liking; 椒圖 is shaped like a snail, likes to close things, and so is set above doors. The Japanese-language source says it likes closed places, dislikes strangers entering its den, and is therefore pictured holding a door's grip ring in its mouth.

long_description.id: Catatan tertua yang diketahui tentang daftar anak naga ada dalam 菽園雜記 karya Lu Rong (1436–1494), yang mencatat bahwa daftar itu hanya memuat sinonim benda-benda kuno, bukan anak naga. Daftar Yang Shen (楊慎, 1488–1559) memuat sembilan makhluk dan merupakan versi yang paling banyak ditemukan.
long_description.en: The oldest known attestation of the list of the dragon's children is in Lu Rong's 菽園雜記 (1436–1494), who noted that the list merely enumerates synonyms of various antiques, not children of a dragon. Yang Shen's (楊慎, 1488–1559) list includes nine creatures and is the most widely found version.

short_description.id: Ular sambung (joint snake) adalah makhluk legendaris dari Amerika Serikat bagian selatan yang konon dapat memecah diri, atau dipotong, menjadi potongan-potongan lalu menyambung kembali.
short_description.en: The joint snake is a legendary creature of the Southern United States that supposedly can break itself, or be cut, into pieces and then reassemble itself.

long_description.id: Ular sambung (joint snake) adalah makhluk legendaris di Amerika Serikat bagian selatan, dan mitosnya diperkirakan menyebar ke tempat lain. Konon ular ini dapat memecah diri (atau dipotong) menjadi beberapa bagian lalu menyambung kembali. Dikatakan pula bahwa jika sepotong ular itu diambil dan pisau lipat yang dipakai memotongnya diletakkan di tempat potongan tersebut, pisau itu akan menyatu dengan seluruh tubuh ular.
long_description.en: The joint snake is a legendary creature of the Southern United States, and the myth is thought to have spread elsewhere. The snake is supposed to be able to break itself, or be cut, into several pieces and then put itself back together. It is also said that if a piece is taken away and the pocket knife that cut it is put where that piece lay, the knife will join up with the rest of the snake.

long_description.id: Menurut catatan para pelancong, kulit ular ini sekeras perkamen dan selicin kaca, serta begitu kaku sehingga hampir tak dapat menekuk. Jika dipukul, ia pecah; dengan cambuk orang dapat memecahnya dari ekor sampai usus menjadi potongan yang panjangnya kurang dari satu inci, tanpa setetes darah pun keluar.
long_description.en: Travelers' accounts describe skin as hard as parchment and as smooth as glass, and a body so stiff it can scarcely bend. When struck it shatters; a whip is said to break it from tail to bowels into pieces under an inch long with no blood at all.

long_description.id: Penjelasan yang diajukan menyebut kekeliruan identitas: mustahil bagi ular mana pun melakukannya dan tetap hidup, tetapi kadal tak berkaki dapat melepas bagian ekornya untuk lolos dari bahaya lalu menumbuhkannya kembali. Kadal tak berkaki ini lazim disebut "glass snakes" atau "joint snakes" padahal bukan ular, dan sumber lain menegaskan bahwa kadal tidak pernah dapat menyambungkan kembali bagian tubuh yang telah lepas.
long_description.en: The explanation offered is mistaken identity: no snake could do this and live, but legless lizards can shed part of the tail to escape danger and then regrow it. These legless lizards are commonly called "glass snakes" or "joint snakes" though they are not snakes, and another source stresses that a lizard can never reattach a lost body part.

long_description.id: Sebuah majalah sains lama melaporkan sebuah spesimen hidup "joint- or glass-snake" dari Starke County, Indiana, yang dikirim untuk diperiksa kepada Dr. W. A. Conklin, Direktur Central Park Menagerie di New York. Sebuah surat dalam majalah itu menyebut teori bahwa hewan bertulang belakang utuh dapat melepas dan menyambung dirinya hampir tak layak dibahas, dan laporan pembedahan menyatakan hal itu tidak mungkin, sama seperti kepala manusia tak dapat dilepas dari batang tubuhnya.
long_description.en: An old science magazine reported a living specimen of a "joint- or glass-snake" from Starke County, Indiana, passed to Dr. W. A. Conklin, who directed the Central Park Menagerie in New York, for examination. A letter in the magazine called the theory that an intact vertebrate could unjoint and rejoint itself hardly worth discussing, and the dissection report said it was impossible, as impossible as detaching a person's head from the trunk.

short_description.id: Monster Danau Kanas adalah makhluk yang dilaporkan hidup di Danau Kanas, Xinjiang; keberadaannya belum dipastikan.
short_description.en: The Kanas Lake Monster is a creature reportedly living in Kanas Lake, Xinjiang; its existence remains unconfirmed.

long_description.id: Monster Danau Kanas adalah makhluk yang dilaporkan hidup di Danau Kanas, Xinjiang; keberadaannya belum dipastikan. Laporan CERNET menyebut taimen raksasa sebagai penjelasan yang diajukan untuk monster itu.
long_description.en: The Kanas Lake Monster is a creature reportedly living in Kanas Lake, Xinjiang; its existence remains unconfirmed. The CERNET report presents giant taimen as a proposed explanation for the monster.

long_description.id: Laporan itu menyatakan bahwa objek penampakan masih membutuhkan penyelidikan untuk disebut monster danau. China Today juga mencantumkan ikan merah raksasa Siberian taimen di antara hipotesis yang dibahas.
long_description.en: The report states that the sighted objects require further investigation before being identified as lake monsters. China Today also lists a giant red fish, the Siberian taimen, among the hypotheses discussed.

long_description.id: Sejak 1980 sebagian orang mengaku memotret "monster danau raksasa" di Danau Kanas, dan laporan menyinggung sapi, kuda, dan domba yang hilang di tepi danau. Pada 1985 sebuah koran melaporkan "Ikan Merah" raksasa sepanjang 10 sampai 15 meter, sedangkan tim peneliti 1987 hanya menemukan kawanan ikan sepanjang tiga atau empat meter dan menyimpulkan bahwa itu taimen raksasa. Pada 2005 tujuh wisatawan melaporkan dua objek gelap raksasa yang melompat dari air, dan China Today menyebut dua hipotesis lain: spesies baru atau reptil purba yang bertahan.
long_description.en: Since 1980 some people have claimed to photograph a "giant lake monster" in Kanas Lake, and reports mention bulls, horses and sheep that disappeared along the shore. In 1985 a newspaper reported giant "Red Fish" 10 to 15 metres long, while a 1987 research team found only a school of fish three or four metres long and concluded they were giant taimen. In 2005 seven tourists reported two huge dark objects springing from the water, and China Today lists two further hypotheses: a new species or a surviving ancient reptile.

claims.quote: 喀纳斯湖水怪（英语：Kanas Lake Monster），是据传生活在中国新疆维吾尔自治区喀纳斯湖中的不明生物。与世界各地的其它湖怪不同，喀纳斯湖水怪并非传说的爬虫类或哺乳类，而类似于鱼类的生物。

statement.id: Monster Danau Kanas adalah makhluk yang dilaporkan hidup di Danau Kanas, Xinjiang; keberadaannya belum dipastikan.
statement.en: The Kanas Lake Monster is a creature reportedly living in Kanas Lake, Xinjiang; its existence remains unconfirmed.

claims.quote: The "lake monster" is thought to be giant taimen.

statement.id: Laporan CERNET menyebut taimen raksasa sebagai penjelasan yang diajukan untuk monster itu.
statement.en: The CERNET report presents giant taimen as a proposed explanation for the monster.

claims.quote: Whether the two objects are legendary "lake monsters" requires further investigation.

statement.id: Laporan itu menyatakan bahwa objek penampakan masih membutuhkan penyelidikan untuk disebut monster danau.
statement.en: The report states that the sighted objects require further investigation before being identified as lake monsters.

claims.quote: first, it is a giant red fish, called Siberian taimen.

statement.id: China Today juga mencantumkan ikan merah raksasa Siberian taimen di antara hipotesis yang dibahas.
statement.en: China Today also lists a giant red fish, the Siberian taimen, among the hypotheses discussed.

claims.quote: Since some claimed that they had discovered and photographed a “giant lake monster” in the Kanas Lake in 1980, Kanas Lake monster has remained a well-known, unsolved “mystery.”

statement.id: China Today mencatat bahwa sejak sebagian orang mengaku menemukan dan memotret "monster danau raksasa" di Danau Kanas pada 1980, monster Danau Kanas tetap menjadi "misteri" terkenal yang belum terpecahkan.
statement.en: China Today notes that since some claimed to have discovered and photographed a "giant lake monster" in Kanas Lake in 1980, the Kanas Lake monster has remained a well-known, unsolved "mystery".

claims.quote: For those bulls, horses and sheep disappeared along the lake, were they really swallowed up by the "monsters"?

statement.id: Laporan CERNET menyinggung sapi, kuda, dan domba yang hilang di sekitar danau dan mempertanyakan apakah hewan-hewan itu benar-benar ditelan "monster" tersebut.
statement.en: The CERNET report mentions bulls, horses and sheep that disappeared along the lake and asks whether they were really swallowed up by the "monsters".

claims.quote: In 1985, Xinjiang Daily carried a headline announcing discovery of giant Red Fish in the lake, saying they were 10 to 15 meters long, weighing more than 4 tons and each having a head over one meter wide.

statement.id: Pada 1985 harian Xinjiang Daily memuat berita penemuan "Ikan Merah" raksasa di danau itu, yang disebut panjangnya 10 sampai 15 meter, berbobot lebih dari 4 ton, dengan kepala selebar lebih dari satu meter.
statement.en: In 1985 the Xinjiang Daily carried a headline announcing the discovery of giant "Red Fish" in the lake, said to be 10 to 15 metres long, weighing over 4 tons, with heads over a metre wide.

claims.quote: In 1987, a well-equipped scientific research team formed by local and domestic experts discovered a sizeable school of Giant Red Fish, each of them three or four meters long. The team thus announced that the mystery was solved--the "lake monsters" were giant taimen, called Giant Red Fish locally.

statement.id: Pada 1987 sebuah tim peneliti menemukan kawanan besar Ikan Merah Raksasa yang masing-masing panjangnya tiga atau empat meter, dan tim itu mengumumkan bahwa misteri terpecahkan: "monster danau" adalah taimen raksasa yang disebut Ikan Merah Raksasa oleh warga setempat.
statement.en: In 1987 a research team found a sizeable school of Giant Red Fish, each three or four metres long, and announced the mystery solved: the "lake monsters" were giant taimen, locally called Giant Red Fish.

claims.quote: they suddenly spotted two dark objects, very large in size, springing out of the water, breaking a wave one meter high. They leapt forward one following the other, headed swiftly towards the middle of the lake and disappeared from sight in about two minutes.

statement.id: Menurut laporan CERNET tahun 2005, tujuh wisatawan dari Beijing yang berperahu di danau tiba-tiba melihat dua objek gelap yang sangat besar melompat dari air dan memecah ombak setinggi satu meter, melaju ke tengah danau, dan menghilang dalam sekitar dua menit.
statement.en: According to the 2005 CERNET report, seven Beijing tourists sailing on the lake suddenly saw two very large dark objects spring out of the water, breaking a one-metre wave, rush toward the middle of the lake and vanish within about two minutes.

claims.quote: The second explanation is that it is a new species that has not yet been catalogued and studied. Third, it is a huge reptilian creature that survived from very ancient times.

statement.id: China Today menyebut dua hipotesis lain tentang monster itu: spesies baru yang belum dikatalogkan dan diteliti, atau makhluk reptil raksasa yang bertahan sejak zaman purba.
statement.en: China Today lists two further hypotheses about the monster: a new species not yet catalogued and studied, or a huge reptilian creature that survived from very ancient times.

topic.en: Size and identity of the creature

summary.id: Berita 1985 menyebut ikan merah sepanjang 10 sampai 15 meter.
summary.en: The 1985 report gives red fish 10 to 15 metres long.

summary.id: Tim 1987 menemukan ikan sepanjang tiga atau empat meter dan menyimpulkan taimen raksasa.
summary.en: The 1987 team found fish three or four metres long and concluded giant taimen.

summary.id: Hipotesis lain: spesies baru atau reptil purba.
summary.en: Other hypotheses: a new species or an ancient reptile.

short_description.id: Kanbari-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan toilet.
short_description.en: Kanbari-nyūdō is a yōkai associated with toilets.

long_description.id: Kanbari-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan toilet. Sekien menggambarkan sosok seperti biksu yang mengeluarkan burung dari mulut.
long_description.en: Kanbari-nyūdō is a yōkai associated with toilets. Sekien depicts a monk-like figure expelling a bird from its mouth.

long_description.id: Satu kebiasaan memakai mantra malam tahun baru untuk mencegah kemunculannya. Kisah lain menganggap mengingat mantra itu sebagai kesialan.
long_description.en: One custom uses a New Year’s Eve chant to avert its appearance. Another account regards recalling that chant as unlucky.

long_description.id: Dalam tradisi Himeji, mantra tahun baru di toilet konon membuat kepala manusia jatuh yang berubah menjadi emas, sedangkan di Wakayama ia disebut "setchinbō" dan bersuara seperti burung. Di sebagian Okayama ia bercampur dengan Mikoshi-nyūdō. Kiyū Shōran mengaitkan asal mantranya dengan kepercayaan bahwa mendengar hototogisu di toilet membawa kejadian buruk.
long_description.en: In the Himeji tradition the New Year's Eve chant in the toilet is said to make a human head fall that turns to gold, while in Wakayama it is called "setchinbō" and makes a bird-like sound. In parts of Okayama it is confused with Mikoshi-nyūdō. The Kiyū Shōran traces the chant to the belief that hearing a hototogisu in a toilet brings misfortune.

long_description.id: Kamus Daijisen Plus mencatat adanya dua pendapat: mantra itu membuat orang tidak bertemu yōkai tersebut, atau justru mendatangkan malapetaka. Dalam kisah Jippensha Ikku, nyūdō itu digigit anjing sampai mati dan yang ditemukan adalah rubah berpakaian putih.
long_description.en: The Daijisen Plus dictionary records two views: that the chant lets one avoid the yōkai, or that it brings disaster instead. In Jippensha Ikku's tale the nyūdō is bitten to death by a dog and what is found is a fox in a white robe.

sources.title: 加牟波理入道 | コトバンク (Shogakukan デジタル大辞泉プラス)
sources.publisher: Kotobank (entries from Shogakukan デジタル大辞泉プラス)

claims.quote: 加牟波理入道（がんばりにゅうどう）は、鳥山石燕の妖怪画集『今昔画図続百鬼』にある日本の妖怪、および日本各地の厠（便所）の俗信に見られる妖怪。

statement.id: Kanbari-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan toilet.
statement.en: Kanbari-nyūdō is a yōkai associated with toilets.

claims.quote: 『今昔画図続百鬼』では、厠に現れる妖怪として口から鳥を吐く入道姿で描かれ、解説文には以下のようにあり、大晦日に「がんばり入道郭公（がんばりにゅうどうほととぎす）」と唱えると、この妖怪が現れないと述べられている。

statement.id: Sekien menggambarkan sosok seperti biksu yang mengeluarkan burung dari mulut.
statement.en: Sekien depicts a monk-like figure expelling a bird from its mouth.

claims.quote: 『今昔画図続百鬼』では、厠に現れる妖怪として口から鳥を吐く入道姿で描かれ、解説文には以下のようにあり、大晦日に「がんばり入道郭公（がんばりにゅうどうほととぎす）」と唱えると、この妖怪が現れないと述べられている。

statement.id: Satu kebiasaan memakai mantra malam tahun baru untuk mencegah kemunculannya.
statement.en: One custom uses a New Year’s Eve chant to avert its appearance.

claims.quote: 一方で、この呪文が禍をもたらすこともあるといい、江戸時代の辞書『諺苑』では、大晦日に「がんばり入道ほととぎす」の言葉を思い出すのは不吉とされる。

statement.id: Kisah lain menganggap mengingat mantra itu sebagai kesialan.
statement.en: Another account regards recalling that chant as unlucky.

claims.quote: 兵庫県姫路地方では、大晦日に厠で「頑張り入道時鳥（がんばりにゅうどうほととぎす）」と3回唱えると、人間の生首が落ちてくるといい、これを褄に包んで部屋に持ち帰って灯りにかざして見ると、黄金になっていたという話もある。
claims.locator: 俗信における加牟波理入道

statement.id: Di daerah Himeji, Prefektur Hyōgo, konon bila pada malam tahun baru seseorang mengucapkan mantra "Ganbari nyūdō hototogisu" tiga kali di toilet, sebuah kepala manusia jatuh; kepala itu dibungkus ujung kimono dan dibawa pulang, dan ketika diperiksa di bawah lampu ternyata menjadi emas.
statement.en: In the Himeji area of Hyōgo Prefecture, it is said that if one chants "Ganbari nyūdō hototogisu" three times in the toilet on New Year's Eve, a human head falls; wrapped in a kimono hem and carried back, it was found under a lamp to have turned to gold.

claims.quote: 和歌山県の伝承では「雪隠坊」（せっちんぼう）と呼ばれ、鳥のような声を出すという。
claims.locator: 俗信における加牟波理入道

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Prefektur Wakayama ia disebut "setchinbō" (雪隠坊) dan konon mengeluarkan suara seperti burung.
statement.en: In Wakayama Prefecture tradition it is called "setchinbō" (雪隠坊) and is said to make a bird-like sound.

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。年の暮れに厠に現れるとされ、全国に伝わる。「加牟波理入道ホトトギス」と唱えれば妖怪にあわずにすむという説と、逆に災厄をもたらすという説がある。
claims.locator: 加牟波理(がんばり)入道

statement.id: Kamus Daijisen Plus mencatatnya sebagai yōkai Jepang yang dikatakan muncul di toilet pada akhir tahun dan dikenal di seluruh negeri; ada pendapat bahwa mantra "Kanbari nyūdō hototogisu" membuat orang tidak bertemu dengannya, dan pendapat sebaliknya bahwa mantra itu mendatangkan malapetaka.
statement.en: The Daijisen Plus dictionary records it as a Japanese yōkai said to appear in toilets at year's end and known across the country; one view holds that chanting "Kanbari nyūdō hototogisu" lets one avoid it, while another holds that it brings disaster.

claims.quote: 岡山県の一部では、加牟波理入道の俗信が見越し入道と混同されており、厠で見越し入道が人を脅かすといい、大晦日の夜に厠で「見越し入道、ホトトギス」と唱えると見越し入道が現れるなどといわれている。
claims.locator: 俗信における加牟波理入道

statement.id: Di sebagian Prefektur Okayama kepercayaan tentang Kanbari-nyūdō bercampur dengan Mikoshi-nyūdō: konon Mikoshi-nyūdō menakuti orang di toilet, dan bila malam tahun baru orang mengucapkan "Mikoshi nyūdō, hototogisu" di toilet, Mikoshi-nyūdō muncul.
statement.en: In parts of Okayama Prefecture the belief about Kanbari-nyūdō is confused with Mikoshi-nyūdō: Mikoshi-nyūdō is said to frighten people in toilets, and chanting "Mikoshi nyūdō, hototogisu" in a toilet on New Year's Eve is said to make Mikoshi-nyūdō appear.

claims.quote: 文政時代の風俗百科事典『喜遊笑覧』に、厠でホトトギスの鳴き声を聞くと不祥事が起きるとの俗信が由来で、子供が大晦日に厠で「がつはり入道ほととぎす」とまじないを唱えるとの記述があり
claims.locator: 俗信における加牟波理入道

statement.id: Encyclopedia adat Era Bunsei, Kiyū Shōran, menyebut asalnya dari kepercayaan bahwa mendengar kicau hototogisu di toilet membawa kejadian buruk, dan mencatat anak-anak mengucapkan mantra "gatsuhari nyūdō hototogisu" di toilet pada malam tahun baru.
statement.en: The Bunsei-era encyclopedia of customs Kiyū Shōran traces it to a belief that hearing the hototogisu's call in a toilet brings misfortune, and records children chanting the charm "gatsuhari nyūdō hototogisu" in a toilet on New Year's Eve.

claims.quote: しかしある晩、入道は犬に噛み殺されてしまった。夜が明けると、そこには白い着物をまとったキツネが死んでいた。人々は笑い、キツネが入道を真似た挙句に呆気ない最期を遂げたと言い合ったという。
claims.locator: 古典上の加牟波理入道

statement.id: Dalam kisah "Ganbari nyūdō" karya Jippensha Ikku, pada suatu malam sang nyūdō digigit anjing sampai mati; ketika fajar menyingsing yang tergeletak adalah seekor rubah berpakaian putih, dan orang-orang menertawakan rubah yang menirunya itu.
statement.en: In Jippensha Ikku's tale "Ganbari nyūdō", the nyūdō is bitten to death by a dog one night; at dawn a dead fox in a white robe lay there, and people laughed, saying the fox had imitated the nyūdō and met an abrupt end.

short_description.id: Kao adalah banteng ilahi dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei yang ditangkap Khuman Khamba dalam legenda Kao Phaba, bagian dari epos Khamba Thoibi.
short_description.en: Kao is a divine bull in Meitei mythology and folklore captured by Khuman Khamba in the legend of Kao Phaba, part of the Khamba Thoibi epic.

long_description.id: Kao adalah banteng ilahi legendaris dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di wilayah Moirang kuno, yang ditangkap oleh Khuman Khamba. Ia muncul dalam legenda Kao Phaba, juga disebut Khambana Kao Phaba, dari epos Khamba Thoibi. Menurut kisahnya, banteng berbahaya itu telah membunuh banyak orang di dekat air sehingga perempuan Khuman tidak dapat memancing.
long_description.en: Kao is a legendary divine bull in the Meitei mythology and folklore of the ancient Moirang realm, captured by Khuman Khamba. It appears in the legend of Kao Phaba, also called Khambana Kao Phaba, of the Khamba Thoibi epic. In the tale the dangerous bull had killed many people near the water, so the women of Khuman could not fish.

long_description.id: Kongyamba, bangsawan kaya klan Angom, menipu pelayannya, Khamba, agar menangkap banteng itu dengan berpura-pura dirasuki roh ilahi dan menuntut dagingnya atas nama dewa Thangjing. Utusan mengusulkan olahraga besar menangkap banteng liar, raja Khuman setuju, dan sebuah koloseum megah dibangun. Khamnu memberi tahu Khamba bahwa banteng itu pernah milik ayah mereka; Khamba menyebut nama ayahnya, dan banteng liar itu menjadi jinak dan lembut.
long_description.en: Kongyamba, a rich nobleman of the Angom clan, tricked his servant Khamba into catching the bull by pretending to be possessed by a divine spirit and demanding its flesh in the name of the god Thangjing. Envoys suggested staging a grand contest to catch the wild bull, the king of Khuman consented, and a large arena was constructed. Khamnu told Khamba that the bull had once belonged to their father; Khamba told the bull his father's name, and the wild bull became tame and gentle.

long_description.id: Sebuah ringkasan lama epos itu menggambarkan Khamba berdiri di tanah kokoh, menangkap banteng pada tanduknya, dan dibawa ke dalam hutan (menurut ringkasan lain, banteng yang kuat itu membawanya ke hutan lebat); di sana ia membisikkan nama ayahnya sehingga banteng mengenali tali sutera dan mengikatkannya sendiri di lehernya. Dalam uraian itu, keesokan harinya Khamba membunuh banteng untuk menghormati dewa Thangjing. Kongyamba mengaku telah menangkap banteng itu, tetapi ia takut dan memanjat tempat tinggi ketika diminta melawannya, sementara Khamba menghadapinya dengan berani.
long_description.en: An older summary of the epic shows Khamba standing on firm ground, catching the bull by the horns and being carried into the jungle, where he whispers his father's name so that the bull knows the silken rope and ties it round its own neck. In that account, on the next day Khamba kills the bull in honour of the god Thangjing. Kongyamba claims to have captured the bull but is afraid and climbs to safety when asked to fight it, while Khamba faces it bravely.

long_description.id: Pada 2001 lukisan Khambana Kao Phaba disimpan dalam koleksi tetap sebuah museum di Bhopal, dan pada 2011 pertunjukan teater tentang banteng Kao diproduksi oleh Laihui Ensemble.
long_description.en: In 2001 the painting Khambana Kao Phaba was kept in the permanent collection of a museum in Bhopal, and in 2011 a theatre show about the bull Kao was produced by the Laihui Ensemble.

summary.id: Kongyamba menipu Khamba agar menangkap banteng yang meneror rakyat Khuman. Khamnu memberi tahu Khamba bahwa banteng itu pernah milik ayah mereka; setelah Khamba menyebut nama ayahnya, banteng menjadi jinak. Kongyamba lalu mengaku sebagai penangkapnya, tetapi gagal ketika diminta melawan banteng itu, sedangkan Khamba menangkapnya sekali lagi.
summary.en: Kongyamba tricks Khamba into catching the bull that terrorizes the people of Khuman. Khamnu tells Khamba that the bull once belonged to their father; after Khamba tells the bull his father's name it becomes tame. Kongyamba then claims to be its captor but fails when asked to fight it, while Khamba captures it once again.

description.id: Pertunjukan teater yang diproduksi Laihui Ensemble berdasarkan kisah banteng Kao.
description.en: A theatre show produced by the Laihui Ensemble based on the story of the bull Kao.

claims.quote: Kao (Meitei pronunciation: /káo/) is a legendary divine bull captured by Khuman Khamba in Meitei mythology and folklore of ancient Moirang realm.

statement.id: Kao adalah banteng ilahi dalam mitologi Meitei yang ditangkap Khuman Khamba.
statement.en: Kao is a divine bull in Meitei mythology captured by Khuman Khamba.

claims.quote: It appears in the legend of Kao Phaba (Old Manipuri: Kau Phaapa), also known as Khambana Kao Phaba (Old Manipuri: Khampana Kao Phaapa) of the Khamba Thoibi epic.

statement.id: Kisah penangkapannya merupakan bagian dari epos Khamba Thoibi.
statement.en: The tale of its capture forms part of the Khamba Thoibi epic.

claims.quote: Kongyamba then tricked his servant Khamba into catching the bull, by pretending, before the king, that he was possessed by a divine spirit, and claimed that the god Thangjing spoke through him. Saying he was "sated with offerings of flesh and fish", he demanded to be given the flesh of the bull that was terrorizing the people of Khuman.

statement.id: Kongyamba menipu pelayannya, Khamba, agar menangkap banteng itu dengan berpura-pura di hadapan raja bahwa ia dirasuki roh ilahi dan mengaku dewa Thangjing berbicara melaluinya; ia menuntut daging banteng yang meneror rakyat Khuman karena 'bosan dengan persembahan daging dan ikan'.
statement.en: Kongyamba tricked his servant Khamba into catching the bull by pretending before the king that he was possessed by a divine spirit and claiming the god Thangjing spoke through him; he demanded the flesh of the bull terrorizing the people of Khuman, saying he was 'sated with offerings of flesh and fish'.

claims.quote: Khamnu revealed a secret to Khamba. She said that the bull had once belonged to their father.  She told him that if Khamba told the bull their father's name, it would be tame and gentle:

statement.id: Khamnu memberi tahu Khamba bahwa banteng itu pernah milik ayah mereka.
statement.en: Khamnu tells Khamba that the bull once belonged to their father.

claims.quote: Khamba did everything as his sister had told him to do. Immediately, the wild bull became tame and gentle. Khamba brought the bull back.

statement.id: Setelah Khamba menjalankan petunjuk kakaknya, banteng menjadi jinak dan dibawa kembali.
statement.en: After Khamba follows his sister's instructions, the bull becomes tame and is brought back.

claims.quote: Kongyamba, a rich nobleman of the Angom clan, met a group of women from the Khuman kingdom in a place called Moirang, and asked them why they were fishing there. They told him that a dangerous bull had killed many people near the water, so they could not fish.

statement.id: Kongyamba, bangsawan kaya dari klan Angom, bertemu sekelompok perempuan dari kerajaan Khuman di Moirang; mereka mengatakan seekor banteng berbahaya telah membunuh banyak orang di dekat air sehingga mereka tidak dapat memancing.
statement.en: Kongyamba, a rich nobleman of the Angom clan, met women from the Khuman kingdom in Moirang, who told him that a dangerous bull had killed many people near the water so they could not fish.

claims.quote: Khamba answered that he was waiting for a good position. Then, he stood on firm ground and caught the bull. The strong bull carried him away into the thick woods.

statement.id: Khamba berdiri di tanah yang kokoh lalu menangkap banteng itu, dan banteng yang kuat itu membawanya pergi ke dalam hutan lebat.
statement.en: Khamba stood on firm ground and caught the bull, and the strong bull carried him away into the thick woods.

claims.quote: On the way back, Kongyamba came to him before anyone saw them. Kongyamba pretended to help Khamba to hold the bull. Kongyamba held the rope. When everyone saw, Kongyamba claimed that he had captured the bull.

statement.id: Dalam perjalanan pulang, Kongyamba mendatangi Khamba sebelum ada yang melihat, berpura-pura membantu memegang banteng dan memegang tali, lalu mengaku dialah yang menangkap banteng itu.
statement.en: On the way back Kongyamba came to Khamba before anyone saw them, pretended to help hold the bull and held the rope, then claimed that he had captured the bull.

claims.quote: But Kongyamba was afraid of the bull. He climbed up on the heights to save himself. Khamba faced the bull bravely. He once again captured the bull.

statement.id: Kongyamba takut pada banteng dan memanjat tempat tinggi untuk menyelamatkan diri, sedangkan Khamba menghadapi banteng dengan berani dan menangkapnya sekali lagi.
statement.en: Kongyamba was afraid of the bull and climbed up to the heights to save himself, while Khamba faced the bull bravely and captured it once again.

claims.quote: The embassy proposed to organize the great sport of capturing the wild bull. The Khuman king agreed. A grand colosseum was built for the event.

statement.id: Utusan mengusulkan penyelenggaraan olahraga besar menangkap banteng liar; raja Khuman setuju, dan sebuah koloseum megah dibangun untuk acara itu.
statement.en: The embassy proposed organizing the great sport of capturing the wild bull; the Khuman king agreed, and a grand colosseum was built for the event.

claims.quote: In 2001, Khambana Kao Phaba (painting) was kept in the permanent collection of the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) Museum, Bhopal, India.

statement.id: Pada 2001, lukisan Khambana Kao Phaba disimpan dalam koleksi tetap Museum Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) di Bhopal, India.
statement.en: In 2001 the painting Khambana Kao Phaba was kept in the permanent collection of the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS) Museum in Bhopal, India.

claims.quote: In 2011, "Kao, the sacred bull" was produced by the Laihui Ensemble. This theatrical show was based on the story of the bull Kao.

statement.id: Pada 2011, pertunjukan teater 'Kao, the sacred bull' diproduksi oleh Laihui Ensemble berdasarkan kisah banteng Kao.
statement.en: In 2011 the theatre show 'Kao, the sacred bull' was produced by the Laihui Ensemble, based on the story of the bull Kao.

claims.quote: There is a great bull that lurks among the reeds that border the waters of Waithou, and already he has killed a man. So we dare not fish there.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, para perempuan Khumal berkata bahwa seekor banteng besar mengintai di antara alang-alang di tepi perairan Waithou dan sudah membunuh seorang laki-laki, sehingga mereka tidak berani memancing di sana.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, the Khumal women say that a great bull lurks among the reeds bordering the waters of Waithou and has already killed a man, so they dare not fish there.

claims.quote: Then Khamnu, who had treasured many things in her heart, was ill at ease for Khamba, and said, “ This great bull was once the Lord of thy father’s herd.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamnu, yang gelisah memikirkan Khamba, berkata bahwa banteng besar itu dahulu adalah pemimpin kawanan ternak ayah Khamba.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, Khamnu, ill at ease for Khamba, says that this great bull was once the Lord of Khamba's father's herd.

claims.quote: Then he stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, and they swayed together as they strove for the mastery. Then Khamba rested on the neck of the bull, who carried him into the jungle.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba berdiri di tanah kokoh dan menangkap banteng pada tanduknya; mereka saling mendorong memperebutkan kekuasaan, lalu Khamba bertumpu di leher banteng yang membawanya ke dalam hutan.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, Khamba stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, they swayed together striving for mastery, and then Khamba rested on the bull's neck as it carried him into the jungle.

claims.quote: And Khamba spake his Father’s name softly into the ear of the bull, and showed him the silken rope. Then the bull remembered the name of his Master and knew the rope, and himself tied it round his own neck.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba membisikkan nama ayahnya ke telinga banteng dan menunjukkan tali suteranya; banteng teringat nama majikannya, mengenali tali itu, dan mengikatkannya sendiri di lehernya.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, Khamba softly spoke his father's name into the bull's ear and showed it the silken rope; the bull remembered the name of its Master, knew the rope and tied it round its own neck.

claims.quote: but the Moirang King would not, and on the morrow Khamba killed the bull in honour of the God Thangjing.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, keesokan harinya Khamba membunuh banteng itu untuk menghormati dewa Thangjing.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, on the next day Khamba killed the bull in honour of the God Thangjing.

claims.quote: Then Khamba fought the bull bravely ; he caught it by the tail suddenly, and then on a sudden let it go so that it fell on its knees.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba melawan banteng dengan berani; ia tiba-tiba memegang ekornya lalu melepaskannya sehingga banteng jatuh berlutut.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, Khamba fought the bull bravely; he suddenly caught it by the tail and then let go so that it fell on its knees.

summary.id: Menurut sebuah ringkasan lama epos itu, keesokan harinya Khamba membunuh banteng itu untuk menghormati dewa Thangjing.
summary.en: In an older summary of the epic, on the next day Khamba killed the bull in honour of the god Thangjing.

summary.id: Ringkasan lain hanya menyebut bahwa Khamba membawa banteng yang sudah jinak itu kembali.
summary.en: Another summary says only that Khamba brought the tamed bull back.
