short_description.id: Kerakera-onna adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa berkimono yang digambar Toriyama Sekien tertawa dari balik pagar; tawanya digambarkan hanya terdengar oleh satu orang.
short_description.en: Kerakera-onna is a giant woman yōkai in a kimono pictured by Toriyama Sekien laughing over a wall; its laughter is described as audible only to one person.

long_description.id: Kerakera-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien dalam buku bergambar yōkai zaman Edo, Konjaku Hyakki Shūi. Ilustrasinya menampilkan perempuan raksasa berkimono yang tertawa dengan mulut terbuka dari balik pagar. Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan paruh baya raksasa.
long_description.en: Kerakera-onna is a Japanese yōkai pictured by Toriyama Sekien in the Edo-period illustrated yōkai book Konjaku Hyakki Shūi. The illustration shows a giant woman in a kimono laughing with her mouth open over a wall. A dictionary describes her as a giant middle-aged woman.

long_description.id: Sekien membandingkan sosoknya dengan kisah perempuan yang mengintip dari pagar dan menduga ia roh perempuan cabul yang mempermainkan banyak orang. Menurut ensiklopedia daring berbahasa Jepang, perempuan yang tertawa kerakera sudah beberapa kali muncul dalam buku cetak zaman Edo sebelum Sekien, jadi ia bukan semata ciptaan Sekien.
long_description.en: Sekien compared her figure with the story of a woman peeking over a wall and suggested she might be the spirit of a lewd woman who toyed with many people. According to an online encyclopedia in Japanese, a woman laughing "kerakera" had already appeared several times in Edo-period printed books before Sekien, so she is not purely Sekien's invention.

long_description.id: Pustaka yōkai sejak era Shōwa dan Heisei menjelaskan bahwa ia menakuti orang di jalan sepi dengan tawa yang hanya terdengar oleh satu orang, dan orang berhati lemah pingsan karenanya. Yokai.com juga menyebut tawa itu hanya terdengar oleh lelaki yang lewat. Penjelasan Fujisawa Morihiko tahun 1929 melukiskan perempuan buruk rupa yang lebih tinggi dari pagar, sehingga ia sering dikenal sebagai yōkai raksasa.
long_description.en: Yōkai literature since the Shōwa and Heisei eras explains that it frightens people on deserted roads with a laugh that only one person can hear, and the faint-hearted faint from it. Yokai.com likewise says the laugh can be heard only by the man who passes. Fujisawa Morihiko's 1929 explanation pictures an ugly woman taller than the fence, so it is often known as a giant yōkai.

etymology.original_form: 倩兮女 (けらけらおんな)

note.id: Yōkai perempuan dari Provinsi Tosa yang sama-sama tertawa.
note.en: A laughing woman yōkai from Tosa Province with a shared trait of laughing.

sources.title: 倩兮女
sources.publisher: コトバンク（デジタル大辞泉プラス）

claims.quote: 倩兮女（けらけらおんな）、けらけら女は、鳥山石燕による江戸時代の妖怪画集『今昔百鬼拾遺』に描かれている日本の妖怪。

statement.id: Kerakera-onna adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Kerakera-onna is a Japanese yōkai pictured by Toriyama Sekien.

claims.quote: 倩兮女（けらけらおんな）、けらけら女は、鳥山石燕による江戸時代の妖怪画集『今昔百鬼拾遺』に描かれている日本の妖怪。

statement.id: Gambarnya muncul dalam buku yōkai dari zaman Edo.
statement.en: The picture appears in an Edo-period illustrated yōkai book.

claims.quote: 着物姿の巨大な女性が、塀越しに口をひらいて笑う姿が描かれており、石燕による解説文は以下の通り添えられている。

statement.id: Ilustrasi itu menampilkan perempuan raksasa berkimono.
statement.en: The image shows a giant woman in a kimono.

claims.quote: 着物姿の巨大な女性が、塀越しに口をひらいて笑う姿が描かれており、石燕による解説文は以下の通り添えられている。

statement.id: Ia tampak tertawa dari balik dinding.
statement.en: She is drawn laughing over a wall.

claims.quote: 塀（墻・牆）からのぞき込んでいる姿をその故事中の美女に比しており、石燕はこれをもって「倩兮女」を多くの人を弄んだ淫婦の霊ではなかろうかと述べている。

statement.id: Toriyama Sekien membandingkan sosok yang mengintip dari balik pagar dengan perempuan cantik dalam sebuah kisah lama, dan menduga "kerakera-onna" adalah roh perempuan cabul yang mempermainkan banyak orang.
statement.en: Toriyama Sekien likened the figure peering over a wall to the beauty in an old tale, and suggested the "kerakera-onna" might be the spirit of a lewd woman who toyed with many people.

claims.quote: 石燕の「倩兮女」以前にも、江戸時代の版本には黒本や絵草紙『平家化物たいぢ』などにはけらけらと笑う女の首がたびたび登場している。

statement.id: Sebelum Sekien, buku cetak zaman Edo seperti kurohon dan ezōshi Heike Bakemono Taiji berulang kali memuat kepala perempuan yang tertawa kerakera.
statement.en: Before Sekien, Edo-period printed books such as kurohon and the ezōshi Heike Bakemono Taiji often featured the head of a woman laughing "kerakera".

claims.quote: 『今昔百鬼拾遺』には詳細な特徴などは述べられていないが、昭和・平成以降の妖怪関連の文献では、人通りのない道を歩いている者に笑いかけて脅かす者で、笑い声によって人の不安をかきたてるもの、また笑い声はその1人だけにしか聞こえず、気が弱い人は笑い声を聞いただけで気を失ってしまうという解説がなされている。

statement.id: Konkon Hyakki Shūi tidak memerinci ciri-cirinya, tetapi pustaka yōkai sejak era Shōwa dan Heisei menjelaskan bahwa ia menakuti orang yang berjalan di jalan sepi dengan tawa; tawa itu hanya terdengar oleh satu orang dan orang berhati lemah pingsan mendengarnya.
statement.en: The Konjaku Hyakki Shūi gives no detailed features, but yōkai literature from the Shōwa and Heisei eras explains that it frightens people on deserted roads with its laughter, which only that one person can hear, and the faint-hearted faint on hearing it.

claims.quote: 民俗学者・藤沢衛彦の著書『妖怪画談全集 日本篇』（1929年）では「見上ぐれば垣より高く大面相の醜女現はれてげらげらげらと笑ふ」と解説されており、しばしば巨大な女性の妖怪と解説されていることがある。

statement.id: Folklorist Fujisawa Morihiko dalam Yōkai Gadan Zenshū Nihon-hen (1929) menjelaskannya sebagai perempuan buruk rupa bermuka besar yang tampak lebih tinggi dari pagar dan tertawa; karena itu ia sering dijelaskan sebagai yōkai perempuan raksasa.
statement.en: The folklorist Fujisawa Morihiko, in Yōkai Gadan Zenshū Nihon-hen (1929), describes a big-faced ugly woman appearing taller than the fence and laughing; hence it is often explained as a giant female yōkai.

claims.quote: 土佐国（高知県）には「笑い女」という妖怪が伝承されており、これは笑い声をたてる女の妖怪であるという点で共通している。

statement.id: Di Provinsi Tosa (Prefektur Kōchi) diwariskan yōkai "Warai-onna" (perempuan tertawa), yang sama-sama yōkai perempuan yang mengeluarkan tawa.
statement.en: In Tosa Province (Kōchi Prefecture) a yōkai called "Warai-onna" ("laughing woman") is handed down, which shares the trait of being a woman yōkai that laughs.

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。巨大な中年女の姿で、塀越しにけらけらと笑うとされる。江戸時代の画家、鳥山石燕(せきえん)の画集「今昔百鬼拾遺」などに記述がある。
claims.locator: デジタル大辞泉プラス「倩兮女」

statement.id: Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berwujud perempuan paruh baya raksasa yang tertawa kerakera dari balik pagar, dengan catatan dalam kumpulan gambar Toriyama Sekien, Konjaku Hyakki Shūi, antara lain.
statement.en: The dictionary describes a yōkai in the form of a giant middle-aged woman who is said to laugh "kerakera" over a wall, recorded in works such as Edo-period painter Toriyama Sekien's Konjaku Hyakki Shūi.

claims.quote: When a man passes a lonely street or alley haunted by a kerakera onna, she unleashes a horrible, shrill cackle that can only be heard by him.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, ketika seorang lelaki melewati jalan atau lorong sepi yang dihantui kerakera onna, ia melepaskan tawa melengking mengerikan yang hanya terdengar olehnya.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, when a man passes a lonely street or alley haunted by a kerakera onna, she unleashes a horrible shrill cackle that only he can hear.

claims.quote: Their name comes from the cackling sound of their laughter.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyebut namanya berasal dari bunyi tawa terkekeh mereka.
statement.en: Yokai.com says their name comes from the cackling sound of their laughter.

short_description.id: Khambrangchak adalah burung yang disebut dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Kangleipak.
short_description.en: Khambrangchak is a bird featured in Meitei mythology and folklore of Kangleipak.

long_description.id: Khambrangchak adalah burung yang disebut dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei di Kangleipak. Kisah Lady Khambrangchak menceritakan serangkaian kecelakaan saat ia bersiap mengunjungi keluarga asal.
long_description.en: Khambrangchak is a bird featured in Meitei mythology and folklore of Kangleipak. Lady Khambrangchak's tale concerns a series of mishaps while preparing to visit her birth family.

long_description.id: Nama lainnya adalah Khambrangchak Pidonnu dan Khambrangchak Tonsenu. Para sarjana berbeda dalam identifikasi burung, antara yellow wagtail dan white pied wagtail.
long_description.en: Alternative names include Khambrangchak Pidonnu and Khambrangchak Tonsenu. Scholars differ in identifying the bird as a yellow wagtail or white pied wagtail.

long_description.id: Dalam versi dari sebuah kumpulan kisah rakyat Manipur, Khambraangchak Tonsenu adalah burung yang suka selalu rapi dan sering mencuci bulunya. Ketika bersiap mengunjungi orang tuanya, ia menginjak seekor kepiting di sungai yang menggigit kakinya. Putusan raja dalam versi ini menyalahkan pasangan pemilik sapi, berbeda dengan versi lain.
long_description.en: In the version from a collection of Manipuri folktales, Khambraangchak Tonsenu is a bird who loves to be neat and often washes her plumes. While getting ready to visit her parents she steps on a crab at the river, which bites her foot. The king's judgement in this version blames the couple who owned the cows, unlike another version.

role.id: Burung betina yang gigitannya oleh kepiting memicu rangkaian kejadian.
role.en: The bird whose crab-bite sets off a chain of events.

summary.id: Dalam versi dari sebuah kumpulan kisah rakyat Manipur, ia bersiap mengunjungi orang tuanya dan menginjak kepiting di sungai. Kepiting itu menggigit kakinya, dan rangkaian kejadian berakhir dengan putusan raja bahwa pasangan pemilik sapi harus mengikat sapi mereka.
summary.en: In the version from a collection of Manipuri folktales, she prepares to visit her parents and steps on a crab at the river. The crab bites her foot, and the chain of events ends with the king's judgement that the couple who owned the cows must keep them bound.

claims.quote: One day she was getting ready to visit her parents. She wanted to wash her feet, so she went to the river.

short_description.id: Kinie Ger adalah monster separuh manusia dan separuh quoll dari tradisi Southeastern Australia [kinie-ger-c01].
short_description.en: Kinie Ger is a half-man, half-quoll monster from traditional stories of Southeastern Australia [kinie-ger-c01].

long_description.id: Dalam kisah tradisional di Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger adalah makhluk buas separuh manusia dan separuh quoll yang berburu mangsa menggunakan tombak [kinie-ger-c01]. Tubuhnya digambarkan memiliki kepala dan badan seekor quoll namun dengan anggota badan menyerupai manusia [kinie-ger-c02].
long_description.en: In the folklore of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is remembered as a half-human, half-quoll predator hunting with a spear [kinie-ger-c01]. He possessed the head and torso of a quoll matched with humanoid limbs [kinie-ger-c02].

long_description.id: Monster kejam ini akhirnya disergap dan dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak saat datang meminum air [kinie-ger-c03]. Setelah dikalahkan, tubuhnya menyusut dan menjadi quoll pertama yang menjadi leluhur bangsa hewan tersebut [kinie-ger-c04].
long_description.en: The ruthless beast was eventually ambushed and slain by an owl and a crow while drinking at a pool [kinie-ger-c03]. Upon his downfall, his form shrank to establish the ancestral lineage of the first quoll [kinie-ger-c04].

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah karya referensi biografi, Unaipon mempelajari mitologi Aborigin sejak awal 1920-an dan menyusun versi-versinya atas legenda; Kinie Ger—The Native Cat termasuk terbitan yang didanai pada 1928.
long_description.en: According to a biographical reference work, Unaipon studied Aboriginal mythology from the early 1920s and compiled his own versions of legends; Kinie Ger—The Native Cat was among the publications funded in 1928.

long_description.id: Sebuah ensiklopedia lama menggambarkan Kinie Ger sebagai makhluk kejam dan haus darah berkepala dan bertubuh kucing tetapi berkaki tangan manusia, yang membunuh orang tak bersalah, hewan, dan burung, lalu dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak yang menyergapnya di lubang air.
long_description.en: An older reference entry pictures Kinie Ger as a cruel, bloodthirsty creature with a cat's head and body but human limbs, which killed innocent people, animals and birds until the owl and the crow ambushed and killed it at a water hole.

who.id: Makhluk hibrida manusia dan quoll pemburu bersenjata tombak.
who.en: A spear-wielding hybrid of man and predatory quoll.

origin.id: Tradisi lisan masyarakat pribumi di Southeastern Australia.

role.en: A forest menace transformed upon defeat into the first quoll.

famous_for.id: Wujud perpaduannya yang unik serta penyusutan tubuhnya menjadi hewan quoll pertama.
famous_for.en: Shrinking into the founding progenitor of all modern quolls.

did_you_know.id: Setelah dikalahkan, tubuh Kinie Ger dipercaya menyusut dan menjelma menjadi quoll pertama di dunia [kinie-ger-c04].
did_you_know.en: Following his defeat, Kinie Ger shrank to become the legendary founding ancestor of all quolls [kinie-ger-c04].

statement.en: In traditional stories of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is an evil half-man, half-quoll beast.

claims.quote: It was a ruthless killer with the head and body of a quoll but the limbs of a man.

claims.quote: In Australian Aborigine mythology, Kinie Ger was a ruthless and murderous beast with the head and body of a cat but the limbs of a man who went around killing innocent people, animals and birds. He was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him when he came to drink at a water hole.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Aborigin, Kinie Ger adalah makhluk kejam dan haus darah berkepala dan bertubuh kucing tetapi berkaki tangan manusia, yang membunuh orang tak bersalah, hewan, dan burung; ia dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak yang menyergapnya saat ia datang minum di lubang air.
statement.en: In Aboriginal mythology, Kinie Ger was a ruthless and murderous beast with the head and body of a cat but the limbs of a man, who killed innocent people, animals and birds; he was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him as he came to drink at a water hole.

short_description.id: Klu adalah dewa naga atau roh air dalam tradisi Tibet.
short_description.en: Klu are dragon deities or water spirits in Tibetan tradition.

long_description.id: Klu (ཀླུ), juga disebut Lu atau, dengan terjemahan setengah bunyi setengah makna, 鲁龙, adalah dewa naga atau roh air dalam tradisi Tibet. Dalam Bon, sebagian membawa panen dan kebahagiaan, sedangkan sebagian membawa penyakit dan bencana. Setelah agama Buddha masuk ke Tibet, klu disamakan dengan naga India.
long_description.en: Klu (ཀླུ), also called Lu or, in a part-phonetic, part-semantic rendering, 鲁龙, are dragon deities or water spirits in Tibetan tradition. In Bon, some bring harvests and happiness while others bring disease and disaster. After Buddhism reached Tibet, klu were equated with the Indian naga.

long_description.id: Bentuk awal klu tidak tetap dan dapat berupa beragam hewan air. Teks Bon menggambarkan bentuk gabungan dengan tubuh manusia, berbagai kepala hewan, dan ekor ular atau ikan.
long_description.en: Early klu forms are variable and can include different aquatic animals. Bon texts describe composite forms with human bodies, various animal heads, and snake or fish tails.

long_description.id: Di Ladakh, lu dipandang sebagai roh air pengubah wujud yang mudah tersinggung. Mereka mendiami berbagai sudut alam, dapat memberi kekayaan besar, dan terkenal mampu mengendalikan air. Mereka juga lekat dengan mata air alami; mencemarinya dikatakan membuat lu marah dan dapat menimbulkan penyakit bagi orang atau komunitas.
long_description.en: In Ladakh, lu are regarded as temperamental shape-shifting water spirits. They inhabit various corners of the natural world, can bestow great wealth, and are well known for being able to control water. They are also closely tied to natural springs; contaminating one is said to upset the lu and can bring illness to a person or community.

long_description.id: Menurut esai yang dirujuk, menjaga hubungan baik dengan lu dinilai penting untuk menjaga keseimbangan lingkungan di Ladakh.
long_description.en: According to the essay cited, keeping good relations with the lu is regarded as essential to sustaining environmental balance in Ladakh.

description.id: Di Ladakh, lu digambarkan sebagai roh air pengubah wujud.
description.en: In Ladakh, lu are described as shape-shifting water spirits.

description.id: Lu terkenal mampu mengendalikan air dan memberi kekayaan besar.
description.en: Lu are well known for being able to control water and can bestow great wealth.

description.id: Lu yang terusik dikatakan dapat mendatangkan penyakit dan kemalangan; Bon menyebut sebagian klu membawa penyakit dan bencana.
description.en: Disturbed lu are said to bring illness and misfortune; Bon accounts say some klu bring disease and disaster.

note.id: Setelah agama Buddha masuk ke Tibet, klu disamakan dengan naga India.
note.en: After Buddhism reached Tibet, klu were equated with the Indian naga.

statement.id: Dalam Bon, sebagian membawa panen dan kebahagiaan, sedangkan sebagian membawa penyakit dan bencana.
statement.en: In Bon, some bring harvests and happiness while others bring disease and disaster.

claims.quote: 根據對遺跡、壁畫和史料記載等的考古研究，推断“魯”龍神崇拜起源於吐蕃以前的原始社會。早期的鲁龙形象复杂多变，可以附身或化身爲水生動物，沒有固定的形象，甚至可以泛指魚、蝦、蛙、蛇、蝎、蟹等。牠們能帶來420多種疾病，如瘟疫、梅毒、傷寒、天花、麻風等，藏人稱之為“龍病”。在近代的川西南藏区仍流传着“亵渎了水中的神灵，身上就会起水泡、长脓疮”的说法，是“龙病”观点的遗留。

statement.id: Bentuk awal Klu tidak tetap dan dapat berupa beragam hewan air.
statement.en: Early Klu forms are variable and can include different aquatic animals.

claims.quote: 在苯教经过辛饶米沃祖师的改革而进入恰苯时期後，鲁龙被作为重要的神祇加以供奉，其形象演變為多種動物的綜合。苯教《大品黑白花濟龍經》（《十万龙经》）記載，龍神有人身、馬頭，或蛇頭、虎頭、熊頭、鼠頭、羊頭、牛頭、豹頭、豕頭、鹿頭、狼頭、孔雀頭等等不同形象，且都有蛇尾或魚尾。這與漢地龍形象的演變頗有相近之處，即“九擬”理論——角似鹿（最初漢地龍沒有角）、頭似駝、眼似兔、項似蛇、腹似蜃、鱗似魚、爪似鷹、掌似虎、身如牛。此時期，魯龍的故事也在原始傳說基礎上豐富而具體起來。如苯教经典《花黑白十万龙经》（简称《十万龙经》，也稱《十二萬龍經》）中寫道，魯龍是世界誕生之母，故稱“龍母”，它們居住在水域中，或山林中，也說住在海底龍宮，守护着无数财宝。藏学家海爾姆特·霍夫曼在《西藏的宗教》一书中写道：“这些龙的最初的住所是河和湖，甚至是些井；他们在水底有家，守卫着秘密的财富。

statement.id: Teks Bon menggambarkan bentuk gabungan dengan tubuh manusia, berbagai kepala hewan, dan ekor ular atau ikan.
statement.en: Bon texts describe composite forms with human bodies, various animal heads, and snake or fish tails.

claims.quote: These spirits, known locally as lu (klu in Tibetan and Ladakhi)—commonly translated as naga (semi-divine hybrid beings from Indian Mythology who have human torsos with serpent tails), remind us of their contribution to Buddhist practice and role in navigating human relationships with the environment.

statement.id: Roh air yang dikenal di Ladakh sebagai lu (klu dalam bahasa Tibet dan Ladakh) umumnya diterjemahkan sebagai naga; esai ini menggambarkan naga sebagai makhluk hibrida semi-ilahi dari mitologi India dengan batang tubuh manusia dan ekor ular.
statement.en: Water spirits known in Ladakh as lu (klu in Tibetan and Ladakhi) are commonly translated as naga, which the essay describes as semi-divine hybrid beings of Indian mythology with human torsos and serpent tails.

claims.quote: In Ladakh, nagas are temperamental shape-shifting water spirits known as lu, who inhabit various corners of the natural world and can bestow great wealth. From streams and soil to trees and stones, lu are well-known for their abilities to both control water and wreck misfortune when perturbed.

statement.id: Di Ladakh, naga dipandang sebagai roh air pengubah wujud yang mudah tersinggung, disebut lu; mereka mendiami berbagai sudut alam dan dapat memberi kekayaan besar. Dari aliran air dan tanah hingga pohon dan batu, lu terkenal mampu mengendalikan air sekaligus mendatangkan kemalangan bila diusik.
statement.en: In Ladakh, nagas are described as temperamental shape-shifting water spirits called lu, who inhabit various corners of the natural world and can bestow great wealth. From streams and soil to trees and stones, lu are well known for being able both to control water and to bring misfortune when disturbed.

claims.quote: lu are known for their affinity for natural springs and contaminating a spring, even washing one’s hands in the spring, will disrupt the lu and can result in bodily afflictions, such as skin maladies, gastrointestinal discomfort, and joint pain. An unhappy lu can bring illness, hardship, and unending tragedy to an individual, family, or community.

statement.id: Lu dikenal lekat dengan mata air alami; mencemari mata air, bahkan mencuci tangan di sana, dikatakan mengganggu lu dan dapat menimbulkan penyakit kulit, gangguan pencernaan, dan nyeri sendi. short_description.id: Koolakamba adalah kera besar yang diduga merupakan hibrida simpanse dan gorila, dilaporkan dari wilayah yang kini menjadi Gabon sejak abad ke-19, tetapi keberadaannya tidak pernah terbukti.
short_description.en: The Koolakamba is a great ape once claimed to be a chimpanzee-gorilla cross, reported from what is now Gabon since the 19th century, though its existence has never been proven.

long_description.id: Koolakamba, juga ditulis Kooloo-Kamba, adalah kera yang diduga merupakan hibrida antara simpanse dan gorila. Laporannya dari Afrika sudah ada sejak pertengahan abad ke-19, dan dokter Franquet mendeskripsikannya pada 1852 dalam laporan tentang kera besar Gabon. Namun, tidak ada bukti empiris yang pernah menguatkan keberadaannya.
long_description.en: The Koolakamba, also written Kooloo-Kamba, is an ape suggested to be a cross between chimpanzee and gorilla. Reports of it from Africa reach back to the middle of the 19th century, and Doctor Franquet described it in 1852 in a report on the great apes of Gabon. Still, no empirical proof of the animal has ever been found.

long_description.id: Nama itu dipakai Du Chaillu berdasarkan kata-kata orang Nkomi dan Bakalai di wilayah Sungai Ovenga, kini Gabon. Menurut catatannya, orang Goumbi menamai hewan ini dari bunyi panggilannya ditambah kata Camma kamba yang berarti berbicara, sedangkan orang Bakalai cukup menyebutnya Koola.
long_description.en: Du Chaillu took the name from words of the Nkomi and Bakalai people around the Ovenga River, in present-day Gabon. In his account the Goumbi people named the animal after its call plus the Camma word kamba, meaning to speak, while the Bakalai simply called it Koola.

long_description.id: Hewan yang ditembak Du Chaillu adalah jantan dewasa setinggi empat kaki tiga inci, berkepala sangat bulat, bercambang melingkari wajah, bertulang pipi menonjol, dan berambut hitam. Ia menilai kera ini paling menyerupai manusia dalam struktur kepalanya, sementara penduduk setempat hanya tahu bahwa hewan ini pemalu, sulit didekati, dan lebih sering dijumpai jauh di pedalaman. Sumber lain menyebutnya lebih besar, berwajah lebih datar, dan lebih bipedal daripada simpanse.
long_description.en: The animal Du Chaillu shot was a full-grown male four feet three inches tall, with a very round head, whiskers ringing the face, prominent cheek-bones and black hair. He judged it the ape closest to man in head structure, while local people could say only that it was shy, hard to approach and met more often deeper inland. Another source calls it bigger, flatter-faced and more upright than the chimpanzee.

long_description.id: Pada November 1996, foto seekor kera tak biasa dari Kebun Binatang Yaounde, Kamerun, dimuat dalam buletin perlindungan primata dan memunculkan lagi pembicaraan tentangnya. Secara ilmiah belum diketahui apakah Koolakamba subspesies simpanse, hibrida, atau sekadar variasi individu; satu sumber menilai gagasan hibrida itu lebih mencerminkan kurangnya pemahaman para zoolog masa itu tentang variasi kera besar.
long_description.en: In November 1996 a photo of an odd-looking ape at the Yaounde Zoo, Cameroon, appeared in a primate-protection newsletter. Science has not settled whether the Koolakamba is a chimpanzee subspecies, a hybrid or merely individual variation; one source argues the hybrid idea mostly reveals how little zoologists of the time understood variation among great apes.

short_description.id: Kui adalah nama bermakna majemuk dalam mitologi Tiongkok, termasuk binatang gunung berkaki satu yang keluar masuk air disertai angin dan hujan.
short_description.en: Kui is a name with multiple senses in Chinese mythology, including a one-legged mountain beast whose passage in and out of water brings wind and rain.

long_description.id: Kui adalah nama bermakna majemuk dalam mitologi Tiongkok, termasuk makhluk gunung berkaki satu. Nama yang sama juga digunakan untuk musisi legenda pencipta musik dan tarian.
long_description.en: Kui is a name with multiple senses in Chinese mythology, including a one-legged mountain being. The same name also denotes a legendary musician credited with music and dance.

long_description.id: Menurut teks klasik bagian timur wilayah liar, Kui adalah binatang di gunung di tengah Laut Timur yang berbentuk seperti lembu, bertubuh biru kehijauan, tanpa tanduk, dan berkaki satu. Setiap kali ia keluar masuk air turun angin dan hujan, sinarnya seperti matahari dan bulan, dan suaranya seperti guntur.
long_description.en: According to the classical text on the eastern wilds, Kui is a beast on a mountain in the East Sea, shaped like an ox, with a blue-green body, no horns, and one foot. Whenever it goes in or out of the water there is wind and rain, its glare is like the sun and moon, and its voice is like thunder.

long_description.id: Kaisar Kuning disebut memperoleh Kui lalu membuat kulitnya menjadi gendang yang bunyinya terdengar sejauh lima ratus li. Tradisi lain menggambarkan kekuatan gunung berbentuk gendang, merah, berkaki satu yang bernama Hui, serta makhluk berwajah manusia dan bertubuh kera yang dapat berbicara.
long_description.en: The Yellow Emperor is said to have obtained Kui and made its hide into a drum whose sound carried five hundred li. Other accounts describe a drum-shaped, red, one-footed mountain power named Hui, and a being with a human face and ape-like body that can speak.

long_description.id: Motif kuilong dan kuiwen muncul pada perunggu zaman Zhou. Sebuah kutipan dalam artikel memberi nama khwei, bersama wang-liang, kepada penampakan di antara pohon dan batu, dan lung (naga) kepada yang berada di air. Penerjemahan Kui sebagai walrus dijelaskan sebagai kekeliruan kamus, bukan makna Tiongkok aslinya. Tafsir Konfusianis membaca ungkapan "Kui berkaki satu" sebagai "satu orang seperti Kui sudah cukup".
long_description.en: A passage quoted in the article gives the name khwei, together with wang-liang, to apparitions found between trees and rocks, and lung (dragons) to those found in water. Kuilong and kuiwen motifs appear on Zhou bronzes. Translating Kui as walrus is explained as a dictionary error rather than its Chinese meaning. Confucianist revisionism reads the phrase "Kui had one foot" as "one person like Kui was enough".

claims.quote: Kui (Chinese: 夔; pinyin:  kuí; Wade–Giles: k'uei) is a polysemous figure in ancient Chinese mythology. Classic texts use this name for the legendary musician Kui who invented music and dancing; for the one-legged mountain demon or rain-god Kui variously said to resemble a Chinese dragon, a drum, or a monkey with a human face; and for the Kuiniu wild yak or buffalo.

claims.quote: While Kui (夔) originally named a mythic being, Modern Standard Chinese uses it in several other expressions. The reduplication kuíkuí (夔夔) means "awe-struck; fearful; grave" (see the Shujing below). The compounds kuílóng (夔龍) (with "dragon") and kuíwén (夔紋) (with "pattern; design") name common motifs on Zhou dynasty Chinese bronzes.

statement.en: An ancient commentary quoted in the article says some hold that the khwei have one leg, and that they have a human face, an ape-like body, and can speak.

claims.quote: There is another mountain power, this one in the shape of a drum, colored red, and also with only one foot. Its name is Hui.

statement.en: A text quoted in the article describes another mountain power shaped like a drum, red, and one-footed, named Hui, which the article notes as a variant name of Kui.

claims.quote: as "Kui [had] one foot", Confucianist revisionism construes it as "Kui, one [person like him] was enough."

summary.id: Teks klasik menggambarkan Kui sebagai binatang atau makhluk gunung berkaki satu.

short_description.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu-lagu rakyat Nordik, yang terkenal karena duelnya dengan pahlawan Vidrik Verlandsson.
short_description.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) of Nordic folk ballads, best known for his duel with the hero Vidrik Verlandsson.

long_description.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu-lagu rakyat (folkvisor) Nordik. Menurut tradisi, ia tinggal di Skottfjället dekat Brattön di paroki Bro, Bohuslän. Ia paling dikenal karena duelnya dengan pahlawan cerita Denmark (danska) Vidrik Verlandsson, yang berakhir dengan kemenangan Vidrik dan dipenggalnya kepala sang raksasa. Dalam Didrikssagan, raksasa ini disebut Etgeir.
long_description.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) of Nordic folk ballads (folkvisor). According to tradition he lived at Skottfjället near Brattön in Bro parish, Bohuslän. He is best known for his duel with the Danish (danska) saga hero Vidrik Verlandsson, which ended with Vidrik winning and cutting off the giant's head. In the Didrikssagan the giant is called Etgeir.

long_description.id: Konon, setelah dipenggal, raksasa itu berlari tanpa kepala ke pertanian Bjälkebräcka di Hallinden, dan di sana tubuhnya dikuburkan dalam susunan batu berbentuk tiga cabang. Kepalanya dikatakan dikubur di sebuah ladang batu bulat zaman es yang di daerah itu disebut "Långbene rös". Vidrik Verlandsson sendiri adalah pahlawan dalam beberapa lagu rakyat Nordik, salah satu pejuang Didrik av Bern, yang menjadi termasyhur berkat kemenangannya atas raksasa ini.
long_description.en: After the beheading, the giant is said to have run headless to the farm Bjälkebräcka in Hallinden, where his headless body was buried in a three-pointed stone setting. His head is said to lie in an ice-age field of rounded stones known locally as "Långbene rös". Vidrik Verlandsson himself is the hero of several Nordic ballads, one of the warriors of Didrik av Bern, who became famous for his victory over this giant.

short_description.id: Luduan adalah makhluk bertuah legenda Tiongkok dengan kepala singa dan tanduk badak.
short_description.en: Luduan is an auspicious Chinese legendary creature with a lion head and rhino horn.

long_description.id: Luduan adalah makhluk bertuah legenda Tiongkok dengan kepala singa dan tanduk badak. Tubuhnya menggabungkan tubuh naga, telapak beruang, sisik ikan, dan ekor sapi.
long_description.en: Luduan is an auspicious Chinese legendary creature with a lion head and rhino horn. Its anatomy combines a dragon body, bear paws, fish scales, and an ox tail.

long_description.id: Luduan dipercaya dapat menempuh 18.000 li sehari dan berbicara dalam semua bahasa. Kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan pemerintahan penguasa yang tercerahkan. Museum Istana Nasional menyimpan pedupaan perunggu berbentuk Luduan dengan tatahan emas dan perak, dan singgasana Kaisar di Aula Keharmonisan Tertinggi dilengkapi dua pedupaan berbentuk luduan sebagai lambang keberuntungan.
long_description.en: Luduan is credited with traveling 18,000 li in a day and speaking every language. Its appearance is associated with enlightened rulers. The National Palace Museum holds a Luduan-shaped bronze incense burner with gold and silver inlay, and the Emperor's throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony is furnished with two luduan-shaped incense burners as a lucky emblem.

long_description.id: Sebuah legenda menyebut luduan pernah menampakkan diri kepada Genghis Khan dan meyakinkannya untuk membatalkan upayanya menaklukkan India. Sebuah teks sejarah Tiongkok mencatat peristiwa serupa: makhluk bertanduk satu berwarna hijau yang berbicara seperti manusia menyuruh kaisar segera kembali, lalu penasihatnya menyebutnya binatang pertanda baik bernama 角端 yang menyukai kehidupan dan membenci pembunuhan, dan sang kaisar menarik pasukannya hari itu juga.
long_description.en: A legend says a luduan once appeared to Genghis Khan and persuaded him to abandon his efforts to conquer India. A Chinese history text records a similar episode: a green one-horned beast that spoke like a human told the emperor to return soon, his adviser called it an auspicious beast named 角端 that loves life and hates killing, and the emperor withdrew his army that very day.

short_description.id: Maushop (Moshup) adalah pahlawan mitos dan raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Wampanoag yang menurut kepercayaan suku Aquinnah membentuk pulau-pulau dan mengajari orang menangkap ikan dan paus.
short_description.en: Maushop (Moshup) is a mythical hero and giant of Wampanoag folklore who, in the Aquinnah tribe's belief, shaped the islands and taught people to fish and catch whales.

long_description.id: Maushop atau Moshup adalah pahlawan mitos dan raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Wampanoag. Menurut legenda, ia berasal dari Aquinnah di Martha's Vineyard dan tinggal di sana sejak sebelum orang Wampanoag. Suku Wampanoag Aquinnah menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk baik hati bertubuh raksasa dan berkekuatan gaib, yang kadang dianggap iblis oleh orang yang tidak memahaminya.
long_description.en: Maushop, also called Moshup, is a mythical hero and giant of Wampanoag folklore. Legend has him coming from Aquinnah on Martha's Vineyard, where he dwelt before the Wampanoag arrived. The Aquinnah Wampanoag tribe describes him as a benevolent being of gigantic frame and supernatural power, whom those who did not understand him sometimes took for the devil.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah yang dituturkan suku itu, Moshup berkelana di tanah tersebut dan suatu hari menyeret kakinya yang lelah di lumpur menuju tanjung Tebing Aquinnah; angin dan pasang laut kemudian melebarkan alur jejak itu menjadi pulau bernama Noepe. Suku itu percaya Moshup bertanggung jawab atas bentuk Martha's Vineyard, Kepulauan Elizabeth, Noman's Land, dan Nantucket.
long_description.en: In the tribe's telling, Moshup roamed the land and one day dragged his weary foot through the mud on the way to the headlands of the Aquinnah Cliffs; wind and tides then widened the track into an island called Noepe. The tribe holds that Moshup shaped Martha's Vineyard, the Elizabeth Islands, Noman's Land and Nantucket as they are today.

long_description.id: Makanan harian kesukaan Moshup adalah paus panggang. Dari dekat pintu sarangnya di Tebing Aquinnah ia berjalan ke laut, mengangkat paus, membantingnya ke tebing, lalu memasaknya di atas api yang tak pernah padam. Bara pohon-pohon yang ia cabut hingga akarnya, tulang paus, gigi hiu, dan kerang quahog membatu yang masih ditemukan di tebing disebut sisa dari meja makannya. Versi lain menyebut ia melempar batu besar ke air sebagai pijakan untuk menangkap paus dan membuang abu pipanya ke laut hingga menjadi Nantucket.
long_description.en: Moshup's favorite daily food was broiled whale. From near the entrance to his den on the Aquinnah Cliffs he waded into the sea, lifted a whale, flung it against the Cliffs and cooked it over a fire that never went out. The coals of the trees he pulled up by the roots, the whale bones, shark's teeth and petrified quahogs still found in the Cliffs are called the refuse from his table. Another version says he threw boulders into the water as stepping stones to catch whales and emptied his pipe ashes into the ocean, where they became Nantucket.

long_description.id: Maushop dipandang sebagai penyedia kebutuhan orang Wampanoag. Ia melemparkan banyak paus ke pantai untuk santapan mereka dan mengajari mereka berburu dan memancing. Menurut satu versi, orang Wampanoag menjadi terlalu bergantung padanya sehingga ia pergi agar mereka belajar bertahan sendiri, sedangkan suku Aquinnah meyakini Moshup masih menjaga nasib mereka. Ia dikatakan memiliki beberapa pendamping, termasuk katak raksasa dan istrinya, Granny Squannit. Seorang anggota suku yang dikutip situs resmi suku menyebut Moshup guru sekolah pertama yang mengajarkan rasa hormat kepada orang-orang.
long_description.en: Maushop was seen as a provider for the Wampanoag. He threw many whales onto the coast for their supper and taught them to hunt and fish. In one version the Wampanoag grew too dependent on him and he departed so they would learn to fend for themselves, whereas the Aquinnah tribe believes Moshup still presides over their destinies. Among his companions are said to be a giant frog and his wife, Granny Squannit. A tribal member quoted on the tribe's official site calls Moshup the first schoolmaster, who taught the people respect.

short_description.id: Mikoshi-nyūdō adalah yōkai mirip biksu botak yang makin tinggi dan makin panjang lehernya saat orang menengadah kepadanya.
short_description.en: Mikoshi-nyūdō is a bald, monk-like yōkai that grows taller, with a longer neck, the more a person looks up at it.

long_description.id: Mikoshi-nyūdō adalah yōkai "goblin" berkepala botak dengan leher yang terus memanjang. Dalam cerita rakyat Jepang dan teks kaidan zaman Edo, ia menakuti orang yang mengintip dari atas benda seperti layar lipat byōbu. Namanya menggabungkan mikoshi, yang berarti melihat ke seberang atau mengantisipasi, dan nyūdō, yang berarti pendeta Buddha. Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berleher panjang dan bertubuh tinggi dalam rupa nyūdō.
long_description.en: The mikoshi-nyūdō is a bald-headed "goblin" yōkai with an ever-extending neck. In Japanese folklore and in kaidan texts of the Edo period, it scares people who peer over objects like byōbu folding screens. Its name joins mikoshi, meaning to see over or to anticipate, and nyūdō, meaning a Buddhist priest. A dictionary describes it as a tall, long-necked yōkai in the form of a nyūdō.

long_description.id: Ketika orang berjalan di ujung jalan malam atau jalan perbukitan, sosok berbentuk biksu muncul tiba-tiba dan makin tinggi jika orang menengadah. Dikatakan orang yang dilewati atau jatuh terlentang karena menengadah dapat mati dicekik atau digigit lehernya. Makhluk ini dapat dibuat lenyap dengan mengucapkan "mikoshita", dan Yokai.com menyebut cara lolosnya adalah mengantisipasinya dan menghadapinya tanpa rasa takut.
long_description.en: When someone walks to the end of a night road or hill road, a monk-shaped figure suddenly appears and grows taller if one looks up. It is said that being flown over or falling backward from looking up can end in death by strangling or having the throat bitten. It can be made to vanish by saying "mikoshita", and Yokai.com says the way to escape is to anticipate it and face it without fear.

long_description.id: Wujud aslinya sering tidak jelas, tetapi di beberapa daerah ia dianggap hewan penjelma, seperti tanuki, rubah, atau mujina. Dalam esai Enka Kidan, ia disebut dewa wabah yang menjangkitkan demam. Pada akhir zaman Edo, lehernya yang panjang dan kurus serta wajah bermata tiga menjadi gambaran baku, dan sebagian orang menganggapnya berkaitan dengan rokurokubi.
long_description.en: Its true identity is often unclear, but in some regions it is a transforming animal such as a tanuki, fox or mujina. In the essay Enka Kidan it is a plague deity that inflicts fever. By the late Edo period a long, thin neck and a three-eyed face became its standard image, and some people think it is related to the rokurokubi.

description.id: Dikatakan makhluk ini dapat dibuat lenyap dengan mengucapkan "mikoshita" ("aku sudah melihat melewatimu").
description.en: It is said it can be made to disappear by saying "mikoshita" ("I've seen past you").

description.id: Kamus menyebut yōkai serupa seperti miage-nyūdō, shidaidaka, taka-nyūdō, dan nyūdō-bōzu.
description.en: The dictionary lists similar yōkai such as the miage-nyūdō, shidaidaka, taka-nyūdō and nyūdō-bōzu.

statement.id: Nama ini menggabungkan mikoshi 見越し ("melihat ke seberang"; mengintip dari atas pagar, antisipasi) dan nyūdō 入道 ("memasuki Jalan"; pendeta Buddha atau makhluk gundul).
statement.en: The name combines mikoshi 見越し ("see over"; looking over the top of a fence, anticipation) and nyūdō 入道 ("enter the Way"; a Buddhist priest or a tonsured monster).

claims.quote: but they can be made to disappear by saying "mikoshita (見こした, I've seen past you)."

statement.id: Dikatakan makhluk ini dapat dibuat lenyap dengan mengucapkan "mikoshita" ("aku sudah melihat melewatimu").
statement.en: It is said it can be made to disappear by saying "mikoshita" ("I've seen past you").

claims.quote: There are many where the true identity of mikoshi-nyūdō is unclear, but there are regions where they are animals that possess the ability to transform.

statement.id: Wujud asli mikoshi-nyūdō sering tidak jelas, tetapi di beberapa daerah ia dianggap hewan yang dapat berubah wujud.
statement.en: The true identity of the mikoshi-nyūdō is often unclear, but in some regions it is an animal that can transform.

claims.quote: In the "Tonoigusa," they are shapeshifted tanuki, and there are also some regions where they are shapeshifted foxes (kitsune). In the Shinano Province (now Nagano Prefecture), they are said to be shapeshifted mujina.

statement.id: Dalam Tonoigusa ia adalah tanuki yang berubah wujud; di beberapa daerah rubah (kitsune), dan di Provinsi Shinano (kini Prefektur Nagano) mujina.
statement.en: In the Tonoigusa it is a shapeshifted tanuki; in some regions a fox (kitsune), and in Shinano Province (now Nagano Prefecture) a mujina.

claims.quote: In the essay Enka Kidan (煙霞綺談) by Hakuchō Nishimura from the Edo period, the mikoshi-nyūdō is a yakubyōgami that inflicts people with fever

statement.id: Dalam esai zaman Edo Enka Kidan karya Hakuchō Nishimura, mikoshi-nyūdō adalah yakubyōgami (dewa wabah) yang menjangkitkan demam pada orang.
statement.en: In the Edo-period essay Enka Kidan by Hakuchō Nishimura, the mikoshi-nyūdō is a yakubyōgami (plague deity) that afflicts people with fever.

claims.quote: The length of its neck has been exaggerated over the passage of eras, and in the late Edo period, it has become standard for its neck to be long and thin, and for its face to have three eyes.

statement.id: Panjang lehernya dilebih-lebihkan dari zaman ke zaman; pada akhir zaman Edo menjadi baku bahwa lehernya panjang dan kurus serta wajahnya bermata tiga.
statement.en: The length of its neck was exaggerated over the eras, and by the late Edo period it became standard for the neck to be long and thin and the face to have three eyes.

claims.quote: 首が長く、背の高い入道姿で、金棒などを持っている妖怪。人が見上げれば見上げるほど背が高くなり、また首が長くなるという。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典「見越入道」

statement.id: Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berwujud nyūdō berleher panjang dan bertubuh tinggi yang membawa tongkat besi dan sebagainya; semakin orang menengadah, semakin tinggi tubuhnya dan semakin panjang lehernya.
statement.en: The dictionary describes a long-necked, tall yōkai in the form of a nyūdō, carrying an iron rod and the like, that grows taller and its neck longer the more a person looks up.

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。路上に現れ、出会ったものが目線を上げるほど巨大化するとされる。中国地方に伝わる。類似した特徴のものに「見上げ入道」「次第高」「高入道」「入道坊主」などがある。
claims.locator: デジタル大辞泉プラス「見越入道」

statement.id: Kamus menyebutnya yōkai yang muncul di jalan dan dikatakan membesar seiring orang mengangkat pandangan; diwariskan di wilayah Chūgoku, dengan yōkai serupa seperti miage-nyūdō, shidaidaka, taka-nyūdō, dan nyūdō-bōzu.
statement.en: The dictionary calls it a yōkai that appears on roads and is said to grow as the person raises their eyes; handed down in the Chūgoku region, with similar yōkai such as the miage-nyūdō, shidaidaka, taka-nyūdō and nyūdō-bōzu.

claims.quote: The only possible escape is to anticipate the mikoshi nyūdō (thus its name). Meet it face-to-face, eye-to-eye, and show no fear.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, satu-satunya jalan lolos adalah mengantisipasi mikoshi nyūdō (dari situlah namanya): hadapi ia mata ke mata dan jangan menunjukkan rasa takut.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, the only escape is to anticipate the mikoshi nyūdō (hence its name): meet it eye to eye and show no fear.

claims.quote: Mikoshi nyūdō is a popular form of some shape-shifting animals. In particular, itachi and tanuki transform into these giants in order to hunt humans.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, mikoshi nyūdō adalah wujud yang populer bagi beberapa hewan penjelma; terutama itachi (musang) dan tanuki berubah menjadi raksasa ini untuk memburu manusia.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, mikoshi nyūdō is a popular form for some shape-shifting animals; in particular itachi and tanuki transform into these giants to hunt humans.

claims.quote: 見越し入道、見越入道（みこしにゅうどう）とは、日本の妖怪のひとつ。『宿直草』『煙霞奇談』『古今百物語評判』などの江戸時代の怪談本や随筆、及び日本各地の民俗資料に見られる。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebut mikoshi-nyūdō terlihat dalam buku kaidan dan esai zaman Edo seperti Tonoigusa, Enka Kidan, dan Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, serta dalam bahan folklor di berbagai daerah Jepang.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia says the mikoshi-nyūdō appears in Edo-period kaidan books and essays such as Tonoigusa, Enka Kidan and Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, and in folklore materials from across Japan.

claims.quote: There are those who think that they are related to the rokurokubi, and since the rokurokubi of legends are frequently female, they are sometimes pointed out as examples of male rokurokubi.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menganggapnya berkaitan dengan rokurokubi, dan karena rokurokubi dalam legenda sering perempuan, ia kadang disebut contoh rokurokubi lelaki.
statement.en: Some think it is related to the rokurokubi, and since legendary rokurokubi are often female, it is sometimes pointed out as an example of a male rokurokubi.

short_description.id: Mino-waraji adalah yōkai tsukumogami dari kumpulan gambar Toriyama Sekien: jas hujan jerami dan sandal jerami yang menjelma menjadi makhluk pemikul cangkul.
short_description.en: Mino-waraji is a tsukumogami yōkai from Toriyama Sekien’s picture collection: a straw raincoat and straw sandals turned into a hoe-carrying creature.

long_description.id: Mino-waraji adalah yōkai dalam kumpulan gambar Hyakki Tsurezure-bukuro karya Toriyama Sekien. Dalam gambar itu ia berdiri di rumpun bambu yang tertutup salju: jas hujan jerami (mino) menjadi tubuhnya, sandal jerami (waraji) menjadi kedua kakinya, dan ia memanggul cangkul. Nama 蓑草鞋 secara harfiah berarti mantel jerami dan sepatu jerami, dan ia digolongkan sebagai tsukumogami.
long_description.en: Mino-waraji is a yōkai in Toriyama Sekien’s picture collection Hyakki Tsurezure-bukuro. In the picture it stands in a snow-covered bamboo grove: a straw raincoat (mino) forms its body, straw sandals (waraji) form its two legs, and it carries a hoe on its shoulder. The name 蓑草鞋 literally means straw coat and straw shoe, and it is classed as a tsukumogami.

long_description.id: Diperkirakan Sekien terinspirasi oleh yōkai bermotif sandal dan jas hujan jerami yang sudah ada dalam gulungan Hyakki Yagyō Emaki dan Tsukumogami Emaki. Basis data gambar Nichibunken juga mencatat satu gambar dari gulungan yōkai dengan nama 蓑草鞋: sosok yang seluruh tubuhnya tertutup jerami kuning dan berwajah sandal jerami, dengan rupa yang berbeda dari gambar Sekien.
long_description.en: It is thought that Sekien drew inspiration from yōkai with sandal and raincoat motifs already present in the Hyakki Yagyō Emaki and Tsukumogami Emaki scrolls. The Nichibunken image database also records one picture from a yōkai scroll under the name 蓑草鞋: a figure covered in yellow straw with a straw sandal for a face, in a form that differs from Sekien’s picture.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jerman menggambarkan sosok ini sebagai mantel jerami tegak dengan dua sandal sebagai kaki dan satu sandal sebagai kepala, yang konon berdiam di tepi sawah atau di rumpun bambu dan dianggap pemurung tetapi tidak berbahaya. Penjelasan tentang asalnya berbeda-beda: dendam petani yang dipajaki berat, roh petani yang menderita, atau roh yang terlalu rajin bekerja di ladang.
long_description.en: German Wikipedia describes the figure as an upright straw coat with two sandals as feet and one as a head, said to stay at the edge of rice fields or in bamboo groves and regarded as grumpy but harmless. Explanations of its origin differ: the resentment of heavily taxed farmers, the soul of a suffering farmer, or a soul too eager to keep working in the fields.

long_description.id: Penjelasan sejak era Heisei menambahkan bahwa jas hujan jerami dianggap memiliki daya magis seperti yang dikenakan banyak dewa pengunjung, dan sandal jerami sering dipakai sebagai benda bertuah penangkal yōkai, sehingga keduanya dianggap mudah menjadi yōkai.
long_description.en: Explanations from the Heisei era onward add that the straw raincoat was thought to hold magical power, as many visiting deities wear one, and straw sandals were often used as protective charms against yōkai, so both were thought to turn easily into yōkai.

sources.title: 草履；ゾウリ，蓑草鞋；ミノワラジ
sources.publisher: International Research Center for Japanese Studies (Nichibunken), 怪異・妖怪画像データベース

claims.quote: 蓑草鞋（みのわらじ）は、鳥山石燕の妖怪画集『百器徒然袋』にある日本の妖怪。

statement.id: Mino-waraji adalah yōkai dalam kumpulan gambar yōkai Hyakki Tsurezure-bukuro karya Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Mino-waraji is a yōkai in Toriyama Sekien’s yōkai picture collection Hyakki Tsurezure-bukuro.

claims.quote: 雪のつもっている竹林の中を蓑（みの）が胴体、草鞋（わらじ）が両脚となり、鍬（くわ）をかついだ姿で描かれている。

statement.id: Tubuhnya berupa jas hujan jerami, kakinya sandal, dan ia membawa cangkul.
statement.en: Its body is a straw raincoat, its legs are sandals and it carries a hoe.

claims.quote: 『百鬼夜行絵巻』や『付喪神絵巻』に草鞋や蓑をモチーフとして描かれた妖怪は存在しているので、それらから石燕が着想を得て描いたものであろうと考えられている。

statement.id: Diperkirakan Sekien terinspirasi oleh yōkai bermotif sandal jerami dan jas hujan jerami yang sudah ada dalam gulungan Hyakki Yagyō Emaki dan Tsukumogami Emaki.
statement.en: It is thought that Sekien drew inspiration from yōkai with sandal and raincoat motifs already present in the Hyakki Yagyō Emaki and Tsukumogami Emaki scrolls.

claims.quote: 凶作が続いた時期に年貢を厳しく取り立てられた農民の怨みの念が、古い蓑や草鞋に乗り移って付喪神と化したものと解説されることもある。蓑は来訪神の多くが身に纏っているように呪力があるものとされ、また草鞋も妖怪を避けるためによく呪物として使用されており、そのような器物は呪力によって妖怪化しやすいと考えられていたともされる。

statement.id: Dalam penjelasan sejak era Heisei, ia kadang diterangkan sebagai tsukumogami yang lahir ketika dendam petani yang dipajaki berat pada masa gagal panen berturut-turut merasuki jas hujan dan sandal jerami tua. Jas hujan jerami dianggap memiliki daya magis seperti yang dikenakan banyak dewa pengunjung (raihōjin), dan sandal jerami sering dipakai sebagai benda bertuah penangkal yōkai, sehingga benda-benda itu dianggap mudah menjadi yōkai.
statement.en: In explanations from the Heisei era onward, it is sometimes described as a tsukumogami born when the resentment of farmers harshly taxed during successive crop failures possessed old straw raincoats and sandals. The straw raincoat was thought to hold magical power, as many visiting deities (raihōjin) wear one, and straw sandals were often used as protective charms against yōkai, so such objects were thought to turn easily into yōkai.

claims.quote: 草履の化物。全身黄色い藁で覆われており、顔が草鞋である。馬頭の杖にまたがり、裾下から動物のような腕脚を覗かせている。
claims.locator: 内容記述 (record "草履；ゾウリ，蓑草鞋；ミノワラジ", parent bibliography: 妖怪絵巻)

statement.id: Basis data Gambar Kaii-Yōkai milik Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) mencatat satu gambar dari gulungan yōkai (妖怪絵巻) dengan subjek ganda 草履 (zōri) dan 蓑草鞋 (ミノワラジ), dan menerangkannya sebagai monster sandal yang seluruh tubuhnya tertutup jerami kuning, berwajah sandal jerami, menunggangi tongkat berkepala kuda, dengan lengan dan kaki seperti hewan yang tampak dari bawah ujung pakaian.
statement.en: The Kaii-Yōkai Image Database of Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) records an image from a yōkai picture scroll (妖怪絵巻) under the double subject 草履 (zōri) and 蓑草鞋 (ミノワラジ), described as a sandal monster whose whole body is covered in yellow straw and whose face is a straw sandal, riding a staff topped with a horse head, with animal-like arms and legs showing below its hem.

claims.quote: (蓑草鞋; wörtlich „Strohmantel und Strohschuh“) ist ein fiktives Wesen aus der japanischen Folklore und gehört zur Yōkai-Gruppe der Tsukumogami.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jerman mengartikan 蓑草鞋 secara harfiah sebagai "mantel jerami dan sepatu jerami" dan menggolongkannya ke kelompok yōkai tsukumogami.
statement.en: German Wikipedia glosses 蓑草鞋 literally as "straw coat and straw shoe" and places it in the yōkai group of tsukumogami.

claims.quote: Der Mino-waraji soll als großer, aufrecht gehender Mino-Strohmantel erscheinen, der zwei Waraji als Füße benutzt, ein dritter Waraji dient ihm als Kopf. Er soll sich am Rande hoher Reisfelder oder in Bambushainen aufhalten.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jerman, ia konon tampil sebagai mantel jerami (mino) besar yang berjalan tegak dengan dua sandal jerami (waraji) sebagai kaki dan sandal ketiga sebagai kepala, dan konon berdiam di tepi sawah padi yang tinggi atau di rumpun bambu.
statement.en: According to German Wikipedia, it is said to appear as a large upright-walking straw coat (mino) using two straw sandals (waraji) as feet and a third as its head, and to stay at the edge of tall rice fields or in bamboo groves.

claims.quote: Ein Mino-waraji soll dann entstehen, wenn dessen ehemaliger Besitzer, meist ein bescheidener Reisbauer, unglücklich starb und zu Lebzeiten viel Leid hatte erdulden müssen. Nun sei dessen Seele in seiner Staffur gefangen.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jerman, Mino-waraji konon muncul ketika bekas pemiliknya, biasanya petani padi yang sederhana, meninggal dalam keadaan tidak bahagia setelah banyak menderita, dan rohnya terperangkap dalam pakaiannya.
statement.en: According to German Wikipedia, a Mino-waraji is said to arise when its former owner, usually a humble rice farmer, died unhappily after much suffering in life, and the soul is trapped in his garb.

claims.quote: Abweichende Anekdoten erzählen das krasse Gegenteil: In dem Mino-waraji hause eine übereifrige Seele, die auch nach dem Tod nicht von der Feldarbeit lassen könne.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jerman menambahkan bahwa anekdot lain menceritakan hal yang sangat berlawanan: di dalam Mino-waraji berdiam roh yang terlalu rajin dan tidak bisa berhenti mengerjakan ladang bahkan setelah mati.
statement.en: German Wikipedia adds that other anecdotes tell the opposite: an over-eager soul dwells in the Mino-waraji and cannot give up field work even after death.

claims.quote: Er gilt als mürrisch, aber harmlos.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jerman, ia dianggap pemurung tetapi tidak berbahaya.
statement.en: According to German Wikipedia, it is regarded as grumpy but harmless.

topic.en: Origin or cause of the Mino-waraji

summary.id: Penjelasan sejak era Heisei: dendam petani yang dipajaki berat merasuki jas hujan dan sandal jerami tua.
summary.en: Heisei-era explanation: the resentment of heavily taxed farmers possessed old straw raincoats and sandals.

summary.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jerman: roh bekas pemilik, petani padi yang meninggal dalam penderitaan, terperangkap dalam pakaiannya.
summary.en: German Wikipedia: the soul of the former owner, a rice farmer who died in suffering, trapped in his garb.

summary.id: Anekdot lain menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jerman: roh yang terlalu rajin dan tak mau berhenti bekerja di ladang.
summary.en: Other anecdotes per German Wikipedia: an over-eager soul that cannot stop field work.

short_description.id: Mintuci adalah roh air dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Ainu, digambarkan setengah manusia setengah hewan; ada yang jahat, ada pula yang membantu manusia.
short_description.en: The mintuci is a water spirit in Ainu mythology and folklore, described as half human and half animal; some are said to be dangerous and others to help people.

long_description.id: Mintuci adalah roh air dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Ainu. Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk setengah manusia dan setengah hewan. Sebagian kisah menghubungkannya dengan kappa, tetapi ada pula yang menunjukkan legenda yang khas bagi Ainu tentang mintuci yang tidak terlihat pada legenda kappa.
long_description.en: The mintuci is a water spirit in Ainu mythology and folklore. It is described as partly human and partly animal. Some accounts relate it to the kappa, while others point to legends peculiar to the Ainu about the mintuci that are not seen in kappa legends.

long_description.id: Mintuci dikabarkan setinggi dan sebesar anak berumur 3 hingga 12 atau 13 tahun. Kulitnya digambarkan keunguan atau kemerahan dengan tekstur seperti kulit penyu laut, dan kakinya seperti kaki burung atau berupa empat set kuku. Kamus awal menempatkan makhluk ini di danau dan sungai.
long_description.en: The mintuci are reputed to be the height and build of a child aged 3 to 12 or 13. Their skin is described as purplish or reddish with a sea turtle-like texture, and their feet as bird-like or as four sets of hooves. An early dictionary locates the creature in lakes and rivers.

long_description.id: Mintuci umumnya dianggap berwatak jahat dan konon memburu manusia serta ternak dengan menyeretnya ke dalam air. Namun ada jenis baik bernama pirika mintuci yang menghuni pegunungan. Mintuci juga disebut dapat memberi keberuntungan kepada nelayan, dengan harga berupa bertambahnya kematian akibat tenggelam, dan memberkati pemburu dengan hasil buruan yang melimpah.
long_description.en: The mintuci is generally considered evil-dispositioned and is said to hunt people and livestock by dragging them underwater. There are also benevolent types called pirika mintuci that inhabit the mountains. The mintuci is also said to bring luck to fishermen, at the price of more deaths by drowning, and to bless hunters with plentiful game.

long_description.id: Nama mintuci dianggap dipinjam dari kata Jepang mizuchi, sedangkan Batchelor memberi etimologi Ainu murni. Kajian cerita rakyat berbahasa Jepang juga memakai ejaan mintsuchi, dan namanya bervariasi menurut daerah.
long_description.en: The name mintuci is considered to be borrowed from the Japanese word mizuchi, whereas Batchelor gave a purely Ainu etymology. Japanese folklore studies also use the spelling mintsuchi, and the name varies by region.

literal_meaning.id: Dianggap dipinjam dari kata Jepang mizuchi; Batchelor menjelaskannya sebagai gabungan mimi 'daging' dan tumunci 'setan'.
literal_meaning.en: Considered borrowed from the Japanese word mizuchi; Batchelor explained it as a compound of mimi 'flesh' and tumunci 'devil'.

claims.quote: The mintuci (Ainu ミントゥチ; also mintuci kamuy, also transliterated into Japanese as mintsuchi (ミンツチ)) is a water sprite or an aquatic supernatural creature, a half-man-half-beast, told in stories of Ainu mythology and folklore.

statement.id: Mintuci adalah roh air dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Ainu.
statement.en: Mintuci is a water spirit in Ainu mythology and folklore.

claims.quote: a water sprite or an aquatic supernatural creature, a half-man-half-beast, told in stories of Ainu mythology and folklore.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk setengah manusia setengah hewan (half-man-half-beast).
statement.en: It is described as a half-man-half-beast creature.

claims.quote: It is also considered a variant of the kappa and, therefore, a type of yōkai.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah menghubungkannya dengan kappa.
statement.en: Some accounts relate it to the kappa.

claims.quote: The name is mintuci (Ainu: ミントゥチ) according to modern Ainu orthography, but it is also commonly spelled mintsuchi (ミンツチ) in folkloric study literature written in Japanese.

statement.id: Kajian cerita rakyat berbahasa Jepang juga memakai ejaan mintsuchi.
statement.en: Japanese folklore studies also use the spelling mintsuchi.

claims.quote: The mintuci has been defined as "fabulous animal", purported to be "half human and half animal and to inhabit lakes and rivers" in the Ainu dictionary c. 1900 compiled by British missionary John Batchelor.

statement.id: Kamus awal menempatkan makhluk ini di danau dan sungai.
statement.en: An early dictionary locates the creature in lakes and rivers.

claims.quote: The Ainu word mintuci is considered to be borrowed from the Japanese word mizuchi (or variants thereof), that are local appellations for the kappa, ultimately deriving from the term mizuchi, which signifies a type of dragon.

statement.id: Satu penjelasan menghubungkan namanya dengan istilah Jepang mizuchi.
statement.en: One explanation links its name with the Japanese term mizuchi.

claims.quote: The mintuci are said to hunt people and livestock by dragging them underwater, but this prankishness is also a trait frequently ascribed to the kappa

statement.id: Mintuci konon memburu manusia dan ternak dengan menyeretnya ke dalam air, sifat yang juga sering dikaitkan dengan kappa.
statement.en: The mintuci are said to hunt people and livestock by dragging them underwater, a trait also often ascribed to the kappa.

claims.quote: The mintuci are reputed to be of the height and stature of a 3-year-old to a 12-year-old or 13-year-old human.

statement.id: Mintuci dikabarkan setinggi dan sebesar anak manusia berumur 3 hingga 12 atau 13 tahun.
statement.en: The mintuci are reputed to be of the height and stature of a human child of 3 to 12 or 13 years.

claims.quote: The mintuci ... Its skin is purplish or reddish, with sea turtle-like texture, and they have either bird-like feet or four sets of hooves, with one supposed witness discovering sickle-like footprints.

statement.id: Kulit mintuci digambarkan keunguan atau kemerahan dengan tekstur seperti kulit penyu laut, dan kakinya seperti kaki burung atau berupa empat set kuku.
statement.en: The mintuci's skin is described as purplish or reddish with a sea turtle-like texture, and it has either bird-like feet or four sets of hooves.

claims.quote: Although the mintuci is generally considered an "evil dispositioned" type of fabulous aquatic creature, reputed to "disembowel and devour human beings when they catch them", there are also benevolent types called pirika mintuci (lit. "good mintuci") which inhabit the mountains according to John Batchelor.

statement.id: Mintuci umumnya dianggap makhluk air yang berwatak jahat, tetapi ada pula jenis baik bernama pirika mintuci yang menghuni pegunungan.
statement.en: The mintuci is generally considered an evil-dispositioned aquatic creature, but there are also benevolent types called pirika mintuci that inhabit the mountains.

claims.quote: As the mintuci is a deity which controls the fish, it may bring luck to fishermen, but at a price, because as long as it is present, it will be responsible for an increase in deaths by drowning.

statement.id: Karena mintuci dianggap dewa yang menguasai ikan, ia dapat membawa keberuntungan bagi nelayan, tetapi dengan harga berupa bertambahnya kematian akibat tenggelam.
statement.en: Because the mintuci is regarded as a deity controlling fish, it may bring luck to fishermen, but at the price of more deaths by drowning.

claims.quote: The mintuci also blesses the hunter, rewarding him with game in plenitude according to folk tradition.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi rakyat, mintuci juga memberkati pemburu dengan hasil buruan yang melimpah.
statement.en: According to folk tradition, the mintuci also blesses hunters with plentiful game.

claims.quote: The mintuci is thought capable of transforming into a youth and becoming an adopted husband at a home with only daughters, bringing about fortune and luck of the hunt, but once the village incurs his wrath, he will depart, absconding with the community's food spirit, causing famine.

statement.id: Mintuci diyakini dapat berubah menjadi pemuda dan menjadi menantu angkat di rumah yang hanya punya anak perempuan serta membawa keberuntungan berburu, tetapi bila desa membangkitkan amarahnya ia pergi membawa roh pangan komunitas sehingga terjadi kelaparan.
statement.en: The mintuci is thought capable of turning into a youth and becoming an adopted husband in a home with only daughters, bringing hunting luck, but if the village incurs his wrath he leaves with the community's food spirit, causing famine.

claims.quote: All but one of the puppets drowned, and the grand general who remained managed to defeat the smallpox demon. The puppets that drowned thereafter became the mintuci kamuy, helping people in case of illness or adversity.

statement.id: Menurut satu mitos asal-usul, boneka-boneka yang tenggelam setelah melawan setan cacar kemudian menjadi mintuci kamuy yang menolong manusia saat sakit atau kesulitan.
statement.en: According to one origin myth, the puppets that drowned in the fight against the smallpox demon thereafter became the mintuci kamuy, who help people in illness or adversity.

claims.quote: According to some Ainu elders, mintuci was a name that people on the Japanese mainland used to refer to kappa, and the correct Ainu term was Shiri-sham-ainu (シリシャマイヌ), literally denoting a "mountain-side-person".

statement.id: Menurut sebagian tetua Ainu, mintuci adalah nama yang dipakai orang di daratan utama Jepang untuk kappa, dan istilah Ainu yang tepat adalah Shiri-sham-ainu, secara harfiah "orang di lereng gunung".
statement.en: According to some Ainu elders, mintuci was a name people on the Japanese mainland used for the kappa, and the correct Ainu term was Shiri-sham-ainu, literally a "mountain-side-person".

claims.quote: The name manifests local variation, and the creature is called mimtuci (ミムトゥチ) in the Chitose dialect and mintoci (ミントチ) in the Ishikari region.

statement.id: Namanya bervariasi menurut daerah: mimtuci dalam dialek Chitose dan mintoci di wilayah Ishikari.
statement.en: The name varies by locality: mimtuci in the Chitose dialect and mintoci in the Ishikari region.

claims.quote: The creature is known by the name hundoci (フンドチ) or slight variants thereof in the Tokachi and Kurshiro regions.

statement.id: Di wilayah Tokachi dan "Kurshiro" (ejaan sumber), makhluk ini dikenal dengan nama hundoci atau variannya.
statement.en: In the Tokachi and "Kurshiro" (the source's spelling) regions the creature is known as hundoci or slight variants of it.

claims.quote: People may also become possessed by the mintuci, and women possessed by one may attempt to seduce men.

statement.id: Orang dapat dirasuki mintuci, dan perempuan yang dirasuki konon dapat mencoba menggoda laki-laki.
statement.en: People may become possessed by the mintuci, and women possessed by one may try to seduce men.

claims.quote: However, Batchelor has given a strictly Ainu etymology for mintuci, explaining it as a compound of mimi (or mim) meaning 'flesh' and tumunci (トゥームーンチー) meaning 'devil'.

statement.id: Batchelor memberi etimologi yang murni Ainu: gabungan mimi (atau mim) 'daging' dan tumunci 'setan'.
statement.en: Batchelor gave a strictly Ainu etymology: a compound of mimi (or mim) 'flesh' and tumunci 'devil'.

claims.quote: Others characterize it as a yōkai, closely akin to the kappa, but others point out that there are legends peculiar to the Ainu attached to the mintuci, not seen in kappa legends.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menggolongkannya sebagai yōkai yang dekat dengan kappa, sedangkan yang lain menunjukkan adanya legenda yang khas bagi Ainu tentang mintuci yang tidak terlihat pada legenda kappa.
statement.en: Some characterize it as a yōkai closely akin to the kappa, while others point out legends peculiar to the Ainu about the mintuci that are not seen in kappa legends.

claims.quote: Mintuchi ... A kind of fabulous animal said to be half human and half animal and to inhabit lakes and rivers.

statement.id: Kamus Batchelor menulis mintuchi sebagai sejenis hewan fantastis yang konon setengah manusia dan setengah hewan serta menghuni danau dan sungai.
statement.en: Batchelor's dictionary defines mintuchi as a kind of fabulous animal said to be half human and half animal and to inhabit lakes and rivers.

claims.quote: Mintuchi ... These mermaids are said to have bodies like those of human beings while they have hoofs instead of hands or feet. They are also said to disembowel and devour human beings when they catch them.

statement.id: Entri kamus itu menyebut makhluk ini "putri duyung" yang konon bertubuh seperti manusia tetapi berkuku, bukan bertangan atau berkaki, dan membelah perut lalu memakan manusia yang ditangkap.
statement.en: The dictionary entry calls these creatures "mermaids" said to have human-like bodies but hoofs instead of hands or feet, and to disembowel and devour humans they catch.

claims.quote: There are also said to be good mermaids or pirika mintuchi, really faries inhabiting the mountains, and these are said to benefit people with their help.

statement.id: Kamus itu juga menyebut ada pirika mintuci yang baik, peri yang menghuni pegunungan dan konon menguntungkan manusia dengan bantuannya.
statement.en: The dictionary also mentions good ones, pirika mintuci, described as fairies inhabiting the mountains and said to benefit people with their help.

short_description.id: Mo memiliki sejarah sebagai nama panda sekaligus penggambaran makhluk campuran dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Mo has a history as a name for the panda and as a composite creature depicted in Chinese tradition.

long_description.id: Mo memiliki sejarah sebagai nama panda sekaligus penggambaran makhluk campuran dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Dalam uraian Bai Juyi, Mo menggabungkan belalai gajah, mata badak, ekor sapi, dan kaki harimau.
long_description.en: Mo has a history as a name for the panda and as a composite creature depicted in Chinese tradition. Bai Juyi describes Mo with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, a cow tail, and tiger paws.

long_description.id: Bai Juyi mengaitkan gambar Mo dengan penolakan pengaruh jahat dan kulitnya dengan perlindungan dari wabah. Baku Jepang mengembangkan motif gambar pelindung kesehatan menjadi makhluk pemakan mimpi buruk. Uraian pemakan logam berasal dari komentar Guo Pu, bukan langsung dari teks awal Shan Hai Jing. Hingga akhir Qing, nama Mo masih mencakup panda dan makhluk campuran, sebelum dikaitkan dengan tapir melalui kekeliruan identifikasi.
long_description.en: Bai Juyi associates images of Mo with warding off evil and its pelt with protection from contagion. The Japanese baku develops the protective image motif into dream devouring to prevent nightmares. The metal eating description comes from Guo Pu's commentary rather than the early Shan Hai Jing text itself. Until the late Qing, Mo could refer to both the panda and the composite creature, before a mistaken identification associated it with the tapir.

long_description.id: Teks utama dari penyair Tang Bai Juyi menyebut Mo hidup di lembah-lembah pegunungan di selatan dan memuji binatang itu sebagai makhluk ajaib yang tidak makan selain besi. Menurut pengantarnya, kulit Mo dipercaya menolak wabah dan gambarnya menolak kejahatan; ia juga menulis bahwa menurut Shanhaijing binatang ini memakan besi dan tembaga.
long_description.en: The primary text by the Tang poet Bai Juyi says the mo lives in the mountain valleys of the south and praises it as a marvellous beast that eats nothing but iron. According to his preface, the skin of the mo was believed to avert pestilence and its picture to avert evil; he also writes that, according to the Shanhaijing, the beast eats iron and copper.

claims.quote: Mo (Chinese: 貘) was the Chinese name for the giant panda from the 3rd century BCE to the 19th century CE. ... Chinese woodblocks depict the mò (貘) as having an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail and tiger paws, following the description of 9th-century Tang poet Bai/Bo Juyi.

statement.id: Mo memiliki sejarah sebagai nama panda sekaligus penggambaran makhluk campuran dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Mo has a history as a name for the panda and as a composite creature depicted in Chinese tradition.

claims.quote: The mò has elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws [貘者象鼻犀目牛尾虎足]. It inhabits the mountains and valleys of the south. To sleep on its pelt repels contagion [寢其皮辟瘟]. To draw its form repels evil [圖其形辟邪]. In the past I suffered from wind-ailment of the head [病頭風], and whenever I slept I always protected my head with a small screen.

statement.en: Bai Juyi describes Mo with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, a cow tail, and tiger paws.

claims.quote: The mò has elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws [貘者象鼻犀目牛尾虎足]. It inhabits the mountains and valleys of the south. To sleep on its pelt repels contagion [寢其皮辟瘟]. To draw its form repels evil [圖其形辟邪]. In the past I suffered from wind-ailment of the head [病頭風], and whenever I slept I always protected my head with a small screen.

claims.quote: Bai's "eats iron and copper, and eats nothing else" reference comes from Guo Pu's 4th century commentary to the Shanhai jing and not the pre-Han classic text. The Shanhai jing proper mentions the mengbao "ferocious leopard" on South Mountain, which Guo notes as a metal-eating beast similar to the mò, and mentions Lai Mountain, which he glosses as a mò habitat.

statement.en: The metal eating description comes from Guo Pu's commentary rather than the early Shan Hai Jing text itself.

claims.quote: Up until the late Qing dynasty (1644–1912), the Chinese name mo (貘) continued referring to both "giant panda" and "chimera with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, cow tail, and tiger paws", and owing to Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat's mix-up in the 1820s, mò was misidentified as the recently discovered "Malayan tapir".

statement.id: Hingga akhir Qing, nama Mo masih mencakup panda dan makhluk campuran, sebelum dikaitkan dengan tapir melalui kekeliruan identifikasi.
statement.en: Until the late Qing, Mo could refer to both the panda and the composite creature, before a mistaken identification associated it with the tapir.

claims.quote: 貘者，象鼻犀目，牛尾虎足，生南方山谷中。寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。

statement.id: Dalam pengantar Bai Juyi, Mo digambarkan berbelalai gajah, bermata badak, berekor sapi, dan berkaki harimau, hidup di lembah-lembah pegunungan di selatan; tidur di atas kulitnya menolak wabah dan menggambar rupanya menolak kejahatan.
statement.en: In Bai Juyi's preface the mo has an elephant's nose, rhinoceros eyes, an ox tail and tiger feet, and lives in the mountain valleys of the south; sleeping on its skin averts pestilence and drawing its form averts evil.

claims.quote: 寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。予舊病頭風，每寢息，常以小屏衛其首，適遇畫工，偶令寫之。按《山海經》，此獸食鐵與銅，不食他物。

statement.id: Bai Juyi menulis bahwa menurut Shanhaijing binatang ini memakan besi dan tembaga dan tidak makan hal lain.
statement.en: Bai Juyi writes that, according to the Shanhaijing, this beast eats iron and copper and nothing else.

claims.quote: 邈哉奇獸，生於南國。其名曰貘，非鐵不食。昔在上古，人心忠質。

statement.id: Dalam baris pujiannya, Bai Juyi menyebut Mo sebagai binatang ajaib dari negeri selatan yang tidak makan selain besi.
statement.en: In the hymn itself, Bai Juyi calls the mo a marvellous beast born in the southern land that eats nothing but iron.

short_description.id: Kelinci bulan adalah tokoh mitos dalam cerita rakyat Asia Timur dan pribumi Amerika, berdasarkan tafsiran bercak gelap di Bulan sebagai kelinci atau hare.
short_description.en: The Moon rabbit is a mythical figure in East Asian and indigenous American folklore, based on reading the dark markings on the Moon as a rabbit or hare.

long_description.id: Kelinci bulan, juga disebut hare bulan atau kelinci giok, lahir dari tafsiran yang mengenali bercak gelap di sisi dekat Bulan sebagai kelinci atau hare. Di Asia Timur kelinci itu dilihat menumbuk dengan lesung dan alu, tetapi isinya berbeda: di Tiongkok eliksir kehidupan atau obat bagi manusia fana dan kadang kue bulan, sedangkan di Jepang dan Korea beras manis untuk mochi atau kue beras.
long_description.en: The Moon rabbit, also called the Moon hare or Jade rabbit, arises from seeing a rabbit or hare in the dark patches on the Moon's nearer face. In East Asia the rabbit is seen pounding with a mortar and pestle, but the contents differ: in China the elixir of life or medicine for mortals and sometimes mooncakes, in Japan and Korea sweet rice for mochi or rice cakes.

long_description.id: Sumber Tiongkok awal bernama Chu Ci mencatat seekor hare di Bulan yang terus menumbuk ramuan bagi para makhluk abadi, dan penyair dinasti Han menyebutnya "Hare Giok". Dalam kisah Jataka Buddhis, seekor kelinci yang hanya tahu mengumpulkan rumput menawarkan dirinya ke api bagi seorang lelaki tua yang ternyata Śakra; tersentuh oleh kebajikannya, Śakra menggambar rupa kelinci di Bulan. Legenda ini melahirkan beberapa festival di berbagai negara Asia.
long_description.en: An early Chinese source, the Chu Ci, records a hare on the Moon who ceaselessly pounds herbs for the immortals, and Han dynasty poets called it the "Jade Hare". In the Buddhist Jataka story a rabbit that knew only how to gather grass offered itself to the fire for an old man who was really Śakra; touched by its virtue, Śakra drew the rabbit's likeness on the Moon. The legend gave rise to several festivals in different Asian countries.

long_description.id: Cerita rakyat Amerindian Amerika Utara juga memuat tema kelinci bulan. Dalam legenda Aztec, Quetzalcoatl mengangkat seekor kelinci yang menawarkan diri sebagai makanan ke Bulan dan menorehkan rupanya di sana; dalam kisah lain, para dewa melemparkan seekor kelinci ke wajah Tecciztecatl agar cahaya Bulan lebih redup. Dalam legenda Cree seekor kelinci muda menunggangi Bulan bersama burung bangau.
long_description.en: Moon folklore of Amerindian cultures in North America also has rabbit themes. In an Aztec legend Quetzalcoatl raised a rabbit that offered itself as food to the Moon and imprinted her image there; in another story the gods threw a rabbit at Tecciztecatl's face so that the Moon would be dimmer. In a Cree legend a young rabbit wished to ride the Moon with the help of a crane.

cultural_context.id: Legenda ini melahirkan Festival Pertengahan Musim Gugur di Tiongkok, Tết Trung Thu di Vietnam, Tsukimi di Jepang, Chuseok di Korea, dan Bon Om Touk di Kamboja. Di Jepang dan Korea, hare yang menumbuk mochi dikaitkan dengan Tahun Baru, dan di Jepang hare ini bermakna simbolis kedermawanan dan umur panjang.
cultural_context.en: The legend gave rise to the Mid-Autumn Festival in China, Tết Trung Thu in Vietnam, Tsukimi in Japan, Chuseok in Korea, and Bon Om Touk in Cambodia. In Japan and Korea the mochi-pounding hare is linked with the New Year, and in Japan this hare carries the symbolic meanings of charity and longevity.

summary.id: Seekor monyet, berang-berang, jakal, dan kelinci bertekad berderma pada hari purnama. Kelinci yang hanya tahu mengumpulkan rumput menawarkan tubuhnya ke api; ia tidak terbakar, lelaki tua itu mengungkapkan dirinya Śakra, dan rupa sang kelinci digambar di Bulan.
summary.en: Four animals, a monkey, an otter, a jackal, and a rabbit, vowed to practice charity on the full-moon day. The rabbit, knowing only how to gather grass, offered its body to the fire; it was not burnt, the old man revealed himself as Śakra, and the rabbit's likeness was drawn on the Moon.

claims.quote: According to an Aztec legend, the god Quetzalcoatl, then living on Earth as a human, started on a journey ... a rabbit grazing nearby offered herself as food to save his life.
