statement.id: Menurut legenda Aztec, dewa Quetzalcoatl yang saat itu hidup di Bumi sebagai manusia memulai sebuah perjalanan ... seekor kelinci yang merumput di dekatnya menawarkan dirinya sebagai makanan untuk menyelamatkan nyawanya. Tergerak oleh persembahan mulia itu, Quetzalcoatl mengangkat sang kelinci ke Bulan sebelum mengembalikannya ke Bumi, dan menorehkan rupanya di Bulan.
statement.en: According to an Aztec legend, Quetzalcoatl, living on Earth as a human, started a journey; a rabbit grazing nearby offered herself as food to save his life, and moved by the offering he elevated her to the Moon before returning her to Earth, imprinting her image in the Moon.

claims.quote: In a Cree cultural legend, a young rabbit wished to ride the Moon, but only the crane was willing to take him there. The trip stretched the crane's legs, leaving them elongated.

statement.en: In a Cree cultural legend a young rabbit wished to ride the Moon, but only the crane was willing to take him there, and the trip stretched the crane's legs, leaving them elongated.

claims.quote: Due to Tecciztecatl's cowardice, the other deities believed that the Moon should not be as bright as the Sun and threw a rabbit at Tecciztecatl's face to diminish his light.

statement.en: Because of Tecciztecatl's cowardice, the other deities believed the Moon should not be as bright as the Sun and threw a rabbit at Tecciztecatl's face to diminish his light.

short_description.id: Nie Xiaoqian adalah hantu perempuan dalam kisah klasik Pu Songling.
short_description.en: Nie Xiaoqian is a female ghost in Pu Songling's classical tale.

long_description.id: Nie Xiaoqian adalah hantu perempuan dalam kisah klasik Pu Songling. Kisah menyebut ia meninggal pada usia delapan belas dan dikubur di kuil tua Jinhua.
long_description.en: Nie Xiaoqian is a female ghost in Pu Songling's classical tale. The tale says she dies at eighteen and is buried at an old temple in Jinhua.

long_description.id: Ia dipaksa membantu pembunuhan ritual oleh makhluk iblis. Sarjana Ning Caichen menolak godaannya dan membantu melepaskannya dari iblis. Dalam perkembangan cerita, ia tinggal bersama keluarga Ning dan kemudian menikah dengannya.
long_description.en: She is coerced into assisting ritual murders for a demon. The scholar Ning Caichen resists her temptation and helps free her from the demon. As the story develops, she lives with Ning's family and later marries him.

long_description.id: Dalam teks kisah itu, Nie Xiaoqian mengaku bermarga Nie, meninggal muda pada usia delapan belas, dimakamkan di dekat kuil, dan diancam makhluk jahat sehingga dipaksa mengerjakan tugas hina. Ia menjelaskan cara makhluk itu memikat korban, dan menurut kisah itu ia takut pada kantong pedang milik pendekar.
long_description.en: In the text of the tale, Nie Xiaoqian says her surname is Nie, that she died young at eighteen, was buried near the temple, and was threatened by monstrous beings into menial tasks. She explains how that being lures victims, and in the tale she fears the swordsman's leather bag.

long_description.id: Kisah menutup dengan kantong kulit yang menarik makhluk berwujud yasa ke dalamnya. Setelah tinggal di rumah Ning, pada awalnya Xiaoqian tidak makan atau minum, kemudian menyesap bubur encer; keluarga Ning merahasiakan bahwa ia hantu, dan para tamu pesta pernikahan mengira ia peri. Wikipedia mencatat bahwa kisah ini diadaptasi menjadi banyak film dan drama televisi, dan bahwa Pu menggambarkannya sebagai jelita bak gadis dalam lukisan.
long_description.en: The tale has the leather bag pull a yaksha-like being into itself. After she settled in Ning's house, Xiaoqian at first neither ate nor drank and later sipped thin gruel; the Ning family kept her ghost nature secret, and guests at the wedding took her for an immortal. Wikipedia notes the story has been adapted into numerous films and television dramas, and that Pu describes her as gorgeous, like a girl in paintings.

short_description.id: Nuppeppō adalah yōkai berupa gumpalan daging lembek berkerut yang muncul dalam emaki yōkai zaman Edo dan dikatakan berbau daging busuk.
short_description.en: The nuppeppō is a yōkai in the form of a wrinkled, flabby lump of flesh that appears in Edo-period yōkai emaki and is said to smell of rotten meat.

long_description.id: Nuppeppō adalah yōkai yang muncul dalam emaki yōkai zaman Edo seperti Gazu Hyakki Yagyō dan Hyakkai Zukan. Ia digambarkan dengan kerutan yang tak terbedakan di wajah dan tubuh sebagai gumpalan daging berkepala satu, dan dalam emaki itu ia hanya memiliki nama dan gambar. Mereka tampak seperti bongkahan daging besar yang lembek seukuran anak kecil, dengan tangan dan kaki yang benjol serta wajah yang samar.
long_description.en: The nuppeppō is a yōkai found in yōkai emaki of the Edo period, for example the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō and the Hyakkai Zukan. Its face and body show undifferentiated wrinkles, making it a one-headed lump of meat, and in the emaki it has only a name and a picture. They look like large, flabby chunks of flesh about the size of a child, with lumpy hands and feet and vague facial features.

long_description.id: Nuppeppō disebut berhabitat di pemakaman dan kuil tua, biasanya hanya muncul pada malam hari, dan mengeluarkan bau kuat daging busuk. Mereka tidak dikenal menimbulkan bahaya selain menjijikkan, tetapi dapat membuat kacau dengan berlari ke sana kemari dan mengungguli penduduk desa yang mengejarnya. Dalam Shingo Zade Hōdai Mōgyū, ia dikatakan menyedot lemak orang mati dan dahulu menyamar sebagai tabib.
long_description.en: The nuppeppō is said to live in graveyards and old temples, usually appears only at night, and gives off a strong odor of rotten meat. They are not known to cause harm beyond being disgusting, but can cause chaos by running about and outrunning villagers who chase them. In the Shingo Zade Hōdai Mōgyū, it is said to suck the fat of the dead and to have once disguised itself as a doctor.

long_description.id: Peneliti yōkai Katsumi Tada mencatat bahwa nopperabō kini dikenal sebagai yōkai tanpa mata dan hidung, tetapi dahulu bentuknya seperti nuppeppō ini. Asal-usulnya misterius: mungkin variasi nopperabō atau perubahan wujud yang gagal dari yōkai seperti mujina atau tanuki. Namanya berasal dari slang nupperi untuk perempuan yang berdandan terlalu tebal, dan pada 1609 di halaman Kastil Sunpu pernah muncul sosok yang mirip gumpalan daging berbentuk anak kecil.
long_description.en: The yōkai researcher Katsumi Tada notes that the nopperabō is now known as a yōkai with no eyes or nose, but in older times it was shaped like this nuppeppō. Its origin is mysterious: perhaps a variant of the nopperabō or a botched transformation by a yōkai such as a mujina or tanuki. The name comes from the slang nupperi for a woman wearing too much make-up, and in 1609 a figure resembling a child-shaped lump of flesh once appeared in the courtyard of Sunpu Castle.

statement.id: Shingo Zade Hōdai Mōgyū juga menulis bahwa ia menyedot lemak orang mati dan makan sepuasnya dengan jarum; dahulu ia datang menyamar sebagai tabib, tetapi kini datang apa adanya.
statement.en: The Shingo Zade Hōdai Mōgyū also writes that it sucks the fat of the dead and eats its fill with a needle; in the past it came disguised as a doctor, but now it comes as it is.

claims.quote: The name "nuppeppō" is a corruption of the derogatory slang nupperi ... used to describe a woman who applies too much make-up.

statement.id: Nama "nuppeppō" adalah perubahan dari slang merendahkan nupperi yang dipakai untuk perempuan yang berdandan terlalu tebal.
statement.en: The name "nuppeppō" is a corruption of the derogatory slang nupperi, used to describe a woman who applies too much make-up.

claims.quote: In 1609 (Keichō 14), at the courtyard of Sunpu Castle, someone that looked like a blob of meat appeared. It had the form of a young child, and it had hands but no fingers

statement.id: Pada 1609 (Keichō 14), di halaman Kastil Sunpu muncul sesuatu yang tampak seperti gumpalan daging berbentuk anak kecil, bertangan tetapi tanpa jari.
statement.en: In 1609 (Keichō 14), at the courtyard of Sunpu Castle, something that looked like a blob of meat appeared, with the form of a young child and hands but no fingers.

claims.quote: Nuppeppō’s origins are mysterious. They may be a variation of another famous yokai called nopperabō, a faceless spirit who likes to scare people. Or they may in fact be botched transformations of inexperienced shape-shifting yōkai, such as a mujina or tanuki.

statement.id: Asal-usul nuppeppō misterius; mungkin variasi nopperabō, roh tanpa wajah, atau hasil perubahan wujud yang gagal dari yōkai pengubah wujud yang belum berpengalaman seperti mujina atau tanuki.
statement.en: The origins of the nuppeppō are mysterious; they may be a variation of the nopperabō, a faceless spirit, or botched transformations of inexperienced shape-shifting yōkai such as a mujina or tanuki.

summary.id: Mungkin variasi nopperabō.
summary.en: Possibly a variation of the nopperabō.

summary.id: Mungkin hasil perubahan wujud yang gagal dari yōkai seperti mujina atau tanuki.
summary.en: Possibly botched transformations by yōkai such as the mujina or tanuki.

text.id: Kepercayaannya tercatat terkait pembangunan Bendungan Kariba
text.en: The belief is recorded in connection with the building of the Kariba dam

short_description.id: Nyami Nyami adalah dewa Sungai Zambezi yang dipuja orang Tonga, digambarkan sebagai ular berkepala ikan yang melindungi penduduk lembah dan menguasai perairan sungai.
short_description.en: Nyami Nyami is the Zambezi River god honoured by the Tonga, pictured as a fish-headed serpent who shields the valley's people and rules the river's waters.

long_description.id: Nyami Nyami, juga disebut dewa Sungai Zambezi atau roh ular Zambezi, adalah salah satu dewa terpenting orang Tonga yang tinggal di kedua tepi Zambezi, di Sambia dan Simbabwe. Ia diyakini bersemayam di Sungai Zambezi dan Bendungan Kariba, dan dipandang sebagai dewa yang menguasai perairan sungai itu.
long_description.en: Nyami Nyami, also known as the Zambezi River god or Zambezi snake spirit, is among the chief deities of the Tonga, who live on both banks of the Zambezi in Zambia and Zimbabwe. He is believed to dwell in the Zambezi River and the Kariba dam, and is regarded as the god who governs the river's waters.

long_description.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai sosok laki-laki berwujud ular berkepala ikan, yang melindungi orang Tonga dan menopang mereka di masa sulit. Ia menjamin cukup air untuk ladang dan cukup ikan di sungai. Bersama istrinya ia tinggal di dunia bawah di Ngarai Kariba, dan hubungan dengan keduanya dijalin melalui para tetua suku.
long_description.en: He is usually shown as a male, fish-headed serpent who guards the Tonga and carries them through hard times. He ensures enough water for the fields and enough fish in the river. With his wife he lives in the underworld of the Kariba Gorge, and the tribal elders act as the link to the pair.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan Tonga, pembangunan Bendungan Kariba membuat Nyami Nyami murka karena tempat tinggalnya diusik dan ia terpisah dari istrinya. Ketika sekelompok pekerja tenggelam dan jasadnya tak ditemukan, para kepala desa menyalahkan sang dewa; setelah ritual menghanyutkan kambing putih, jasad itu muncul keesokan harinya dan bangkai kambing lenyap. Legenda Kariba juga mengisahkan banjir besar yang menghancurkan sebagian bendungan.
long_description.en: In Tonga belief, building the Kariba dam enraged Nyami Nyami by disturbing his home and parting him from his wife. When a group of workers drowned and could not be found, village headmen blamed the god; after a ritual in which a white goat was set afloat, the bodies surfaced the next day and the goat's carcass vanished. The Kariba legend also tells of a great flood that wrecked part of the dam.

long_description.id: Saat dipindahkan, banyak orang Tonga ingin tetap dekat dengan Nyami Nyami. Kini mereka berpendapat sang dewa telah menarik diri dari dunia manusia, meski seorang kepala adat masih mengaitkan retakan Bendungan Kariba dengan kemarahannya. Liontin dan tongkat jalan bergambar dewa ini juga dijual kepada wisatawan.
long_description.en: When they were resettled, many Tonga wished to stay close to Nyami Nyami. Today they hold that the god has withdrawn from the world of men, although one chief still tied a crack in the Kariba dam to his anger. Pendants and walking sticks showing the god are also sold to tourists.

cultural_context.id: Bagi orang Tonga, Sungai Zambezi adalah tempat suci Nyami Nyami; saat dipindahkan, mereka ingin tetap dekat dengannya, dan penulis kajian menilai keyakinan ini tidak boleh diabaikan dalam pembangunan.
cultural_context.en: For the Tonga the Zambezi is Nyami Nyami's sacred place; when resettled they wished to stay near him, and the study's author argues this belief should not be ignored in development.

statement.en: Nyami Nyami, also called the Zambezi River god or Zambezi snake spirit, is one of the most important deities (Gottheiten) of the Tonga, who live in Zambia (Sambia) and Zimbabwe (Simbabwe) on both sides of the Zambezi.

claims.quote: Nyami Nyami wird gewöhnlich als männliche Figur dargestellt, die das Volk der Tonga beschützt und ihm Halt in schwierigen Zeiten gibt. Seine äußere Form ist eine Schlange, die den Kopf eines Fisches besitzt.

claims.quote: Nyami Nyami is a famous name given to the river god of the Tonga people; he is believed to be residing in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami adalah nama terkenal bagi dewa sungai (river god) orang Tonga, yang diyakini tinggal di Sungai Zambezi dan Bendungan Kariba.
statement.en: Nyami Nyami is the well-known name of the Tonga river god, believed to live in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.

claims.quote: During the construction of the dam the Tonga people believe that nyami nyami was angered by the constructors who not only disturbed his residence but separated him from his wife when they divided the waters to construct a dam.

statement.id: Orang Tonga percaya Nyami Nyami murka (angered) karena pembangun bendungan mengusik tempat tinggalnya dan memisahkannya dari istrinya.

claims.quote: During the construction of the Kariba dam in 1960s a group of white men who were involved in the construction drowned in the Zambezi River and their bodies could not be retrieved for a number of days.

statement.en: During construction of the Kariba dam in the 1960s, a group of workers drowned in the Zambezi River and their bodies could not be recovered for days.

claims.quote: Some of the village headmen stated that nyami nyami the river god was behind their disappearance.

statement.en: The locals said this could only be resolved by a ritual of slaughtering a white goat and letting it float on the Zambezi River.

claims.quote: The following day the bodies of the drowned men were found floating on the river and the body of the goat had disappeared.

statement.id: Keesokan harinya jasad para korban ditemukan mengapung dan bangkai kambing itu lenyap (goat had disappeared).
statement.en: The next day the drowned men's bodies were found floating and the goat's body had disappeared.

claims.quote: Nyami nyami the snake on the Zambezi river is seen as the river god respected by the community.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami, ular di Sungai Zambezi, dipandang sebagai dewa sungai (river god) yang dihormati masyarakat.
statement.en: Nyami Nyami, the snake of the Zambezi river, is seen as the river god respected by the community.

claims.quote: The nyami nyami on the other hand is seen as the god of the river in charge of the waters of the Zambezi river.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami dipandang sebagai dewa sungai yang menguasai perairan (in charge of the waters) Sungai Zambezi.

short_description.id: Osan kitsune adalah yōkai rubah dari cerita rakyat Jepang yang menyamar menjadi wanita cantik untuk menipu orang; salah satu dongengnya berasal dari Prefektur Hiroshima.
short_description.en: The Osan kitsune is a fox yōkai of Japanese folklore that disguises itself as a beautiful woman to deceive people; one of its tales comes from Hiroshima Prefecture.

long_description.id: Osan kitsune (おさん狐) adalah yōkai rubah yang menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyamar menjadi wanita cantik dan menggoda pria yang beristri atau punya kekasih. Kisahnya banyak tersebar di Jepang bagian barat, terutama di wilayah Chūgoku, dan Wikipedia bahasa Inggris mencatatnya sebagai dongeng dari Prefektur Hiroshima. Ia digambarkan suka pertengkaran sepasang kekasih dan cemburu, dan sebutan 女狐 untuk perempuan penggoda disebut berasal dari yōkai ini.
long_description.en: The Osan kitsune (おさん狐) is a fox yōkai that, according to Japanese Wikipedia, disguises itself as a beautiful woman and approaches men who are married or have lovers. Its tales are told widely in western Japan, especially in the Chūgoku region, and English Wikipedia records it as a folktale from Hiroshima Prefecture. It is said to like lovers’ quarrels and to be jealous, and the term 女狐 for a seductive woman is said to have originated from this yōkai.

long_description.id: Menurut dongeng yang dicatat Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, roh rubah ini muncul sebagai wanita yang menggendong bayi dan meminta bantuan orang yang lewat; setelah menyerahkan bayi itu ia menghilang, dan bayinya ternyata batu. Dalam kisah dari Kota Hiroshima, ia menakuti orang dengan api di ekornya dan menjelma menjadi singa; seorang pengrajin yang hendak membakarnya dipenggal setelah memuji arak-arakan daimyō yang ternyata sungguhan. Ada pula versi ketika Osan kitsune dan tanuki Yozaburō dari 伊像 saling menipu.
long_description.en: In the tale recorded by English Wikipedia, this fox spirit shows up as a woman holding a baby and begging passers-by for help; she vanishes once the baby has been handed over, and it turns out to be a stone. In a tale from Hiroshima City it frightens people with fire on its tail and by turning into a lion; a craftsman who tried to burn it was beheaded after praising a daimyō procession that proved real. There is also a version in which Osan kitsune and Yozaburō the tanuki of 伊像 trick each other.

long_description.id: Di kawasan Eba, Hiroshima, Osan kitsune yang tinggal di dekat Taman Sarayama disebut berusia 80 tahun, mengendalikan 500 pengikut, tidak pernah membunuh orang, dan dicintai warga. Beberapa tempat di Eba dikaitkan dengan legenda ini, sebuah jalan bernama Osan-dōri dinamai menurut sosok itu, kuil kecil dipuja di Marukoyama Fudō-in, dan patung rubah berdiri dekat halte trem Eba.
long_description.en: In the Eba district of Hiroshima, the Osan kitsune said to have lived near Sarayama Park was 80 years old, commanded 500 retainers, never killed people, and was beloved locally. Several places in Eba are associated with the legend, a road called Osan-dōri is named after the figure, a small shrine is enshrined at Marukoyama Fudō-in, and a fox statue stands near the Eba tram stop.

long_description.id: Dongeng "Rubah pencukur" yang dikumpulkan Museum Prefektur Tottori memperkenalkan Osan kitsune sebagai rubah yang sangat pandai menipu orang. Ia menjelma menjadi gadis cantik dengan ganggang hijau di kepalanya dan mengeluarkan kotoran kuda dari kotak bersusun sebagai ohagi. Di akhir kisah seorang pemuda mendapati dirinya tidur di padang rumput dan sadar telah tertipu, dan narator menyebut bahwa rubah ini konon sering membuat orang menjadi biksu. Menurut katalog Seki Keigo, kisah ini tergolong dongeng "Manusia dan rubah". Namanya ditulis 尾三 di Yuki-chō (Hiroshima), konon karena berekor tiga, dan お三狐 di Kadoma (Osaka), tempat ia dianggap berwatak pendendam.
long_description.en: The tale "Razor Fox" collected by the Tottori Prefectural Museum introduces the Osan kitsune as a fox that deceives people very well. It turns into a pretty girl with green algae on her head and takes horse dung out of a tiered box as ohagi. At the end a young man finds himself sleeping in an open field and realises he has been deceived, and the narrator remarks that this fox is said to often turn people into monks. According to Seki Keigo’s catalogue, the tale belongs to the "Man and Fox" type. The name is written 尾三 in Yuki-chō (Hiroshima), reportedly because of three tails, and お三狐 in Kadoma (Osaka), where it is regarded as vindictive.

claims.quote: Osan Kitsune (Japanese: おさん狐, おさんぎつね, romanized: Osan Fox) is a folktale from Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan.

statement.id: Osan Kitsune adalah dongeng roh rubah dari Hiroshima.
statement.en: Osan Kitsune is a fox-spirit folktale of Hiroshima.

claims.quote: It describes a fox spirit associated with deceptive encounters, often appearing in human form.

statement.id: Rubah itu menipu manusia sambil mengambil wujud manusia.
statement.en: The fox deceives people while taking human form.

claims.quote: In the tale, the fox spirit appears as a woman carrying an infant and asks passersby for help.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, dalam dongeng itu roh rubah muncul sebagai wanita yang menggendong bayi dan meminta bantuan orang yang lewat.
statement.en: According to English Wikipedia, in the tale the fox spirit appears as a woman carrying a baby and asking passersby for help.

claims.quote: After handing over the child, the figure disappears; the child is later revealed to be a stone.

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, setelah menyerahkan bayi itu, sosok tersebut menghilang, dan bayinya kemudian ternyata batu.
statement.en: According to English Wikipedia, after handing over the baby the figure disappears, and the baby is later revealed to be a stone.

claims.quote: Several locations in the Eba area of Hiroshima are associated with the Osan kitsune legend.

statement.id: Beberapa tempat di Eba terkait dengan legenda itu.
statement.en: Several places in Eba are associated with the legend.

claims.quote: A road known as Osan-dōri (おさん通り) is named after the figure.

statement.id: Jalan setempat memakai nama sosok itu.
statement.en: A local road bears the figure’s name.

claims.quote: おさん狐（おさんきつね）、またはおさんわ狐とは、美女に化けて妻帯者や恋人のいる男へ言い寄ってくる狐の妖怪。西日本、特に中国地方に多く伝わる。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menggambarkan Osan kitsune (おさん狐), juga disebut Osanwa kitsune (おさんわ狐), sebagai yōkai rubah yang menyamar menjadi wanita cantik dan menggoda pria yang beristri atau punya kekasih; kisahnya banyak tersebar di Jepang bagian barat, terutama di wilayah Chūgoku.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia describes the Osan kitsune (おさん狐), also called Osanwa kitsune (おさんわ狐), as a fox yōkai that disguises itself as a beautiful woman and approaches men who are married or have lovers; its tales are told widely in western Japan, especially in the Chūgoku region.

claims.quote: おさん狐は痴話喧嘩を好み、嫉妬深い一面がある。現代において、恋路を邪魔する女性や浮気相手の女性に対し、蔑称として女狐と呼ぶ場合があるが、このような呼称はこの妖怪が発祥とされている。

statement.id: Osan kitsune digambarkan suka pertengkaran sepasang kekasih dan cemburu; sebutan merendahkan 女狐 (rubah betina) untuk perempuan yang mengganggu hubungan asmara atau menjadi selingkuhan disebut berasal dari yōkai ini.
statement.en: The Osan kitsune is said to like lovers’ quarrels and to have a jealous side; the modern derogatory term 女狐 ("female fox") for a woman who interferes in a romance or is the other woman is said to have originated from this yōkai.

claims.quote: 広島県広島市では、おさん狐が尻尾に火を灯したりライオンに化けたりして人を脅かすので、職人が捕まえて火あぶりにしようとしたところ、翌晩に大名行列に化けて見せると言って許しを乞うた。翌晩に大名行列が現れたので職人は狐を褒めたところ、それは本物の大名行列で、職人は打ち首になったという。

statement.id: Dalam kisah dari Kota Hiroshima, Osan kitsune menakuti orang dengan menyalakan api di ekornya dan menjelma menjadi singa. Ketika seorang pengrajin menangkapnya untuk dibakar, ia memohon ampun dengan berjanji menjelma menjadi arak-arakan daimyō malam berikutnya. Arak-arakan muncul dan pengrajin memuji si rubah, tetapi itu arak-arakan daimyō yang sungguhan dan sang pengrajin dipenggal.
statement.en: In a tale from Hiroshima City, the Osan kitsune frightens people by lighting a fire on its tail and turning into a lion. When a craftsman caught it to burn it, it begged for mercy by promising to turn into a daimyō procession the next night. A procession appeared and the craftsman praised the fox, but it was a real daimyō procession and the craftsman was beheaded.

claims.quote: この話には類話があり、職人ではなく、お三キツネと伊像の与三郎タヌキが化かし合いをして、大名行列の殿様にお三キツネが斬られたという話もある。また、タヌキの方が斬られたという話も伝わっている。

statement.id: Kisah itu punya versi lain: bukan pengrajin, melainkan Osan kitsune dan tanuki Yozaburō dari 伊像 yang saling menipu, lalu Osan kitsune ditebas oleh tuan daimyō dalam arak-arakan. Ada juga versi di mana tanukilah yang ditebas.
statement.en: The tale has a related version in which, instead of a craftsman, Osan kitsune and Yozaburō the tanuki of 伊像 trick each other and Osan kitsune is cut down by the lord in a daimyō procession; a version in which the tanuki is cut down is also told.

claims.quote: 同じ広島でも、中区江波地区の皿山公園付近に棲んでいたおさん狐は年齢80歳、500匹の眷属を操り、京参りをしたり、伏見に位をもらいに行ったりと風格のある狐で、決して人を殺めることはなく、地元では愛される存在だったという。

statement.id: Di Hiroshima juga, Osan kitsune yang tinggal di dekat Taman Sarayama di kawasan Eba (Naka-ku) disebut berusia 80 tahun dan mengendalikan 500 pengikut, berziarah ke Kyoto dan pergi ke Fushimi untuk menerima pangkat; ia berwibawa, tidak pernah membunuh orang, dan dicintai warga setempat.
statement.en: Also in Hiroshima, the Osan kitsune said to have lived near Sarayama Park in the Eba district (Naka Ward) was 80 years old and commanded 500 retainers, made pilgrimages to Kyoto and went to Fushimi to receive rank; it was a dignified fox that never killed people and was beloved locally.

claims.quote: 現在では江波東2丁目の丸子山不動院に小さな祠が祀られており、江波車庫前の電停近くの中央分離帯に、立ち上がった姿の狐像がある。

statement.id: Kini sebuah kuil kecil dipuja di Marukoyama Fudō-in di Eba-higashi 2-chōme, dan sebuah patung rubah yang berdiri tegak ada di pembatas jalan dekat halte trem di depan Depo Eba.
statement.en: Today a small shrine is enshrined at Marukoyama Fudō-in in Eba-higashi 2-chōme, and a statue of a fox in a standing pose stands on the median strip near the tram stop in front of the Eba depot.

claims.quote: 広島県広島市佐伯郡湯来町では「尾三」と書かれるが、これは尾が3本あるからだという。

statement.id: Di Yuki-chō, Distrik Saeki, Hiroshima, namanya ditulis 尾三 karena konon ia berekor tiga.
statement.en: In Yuki-chō, Saeki District, Hiroshima, the name is written 尾三 because it is said to have three tails.

claims.quote: 大阪府北河内郡門真村（現・門真市）では「お三狐」という表記を当てており、執念深い性格とされている。

statement.id: Di Desa Kadoma di Distrik Kita-Kawachi, Osaka (sekarang Kota Kadoma), namanya ditulis お三狐 dan ia dianggap berwatak pendendam.
statement.en: In Kadoma Village, Kita-Kawachi District, Osaka (now Kadoma City), the name is written お三狐 and it is regarded as having a vindictive character.

claims.quote: 昭和60年(1985)8月15日、智頭町波多で採集 ... 昔、あるところになあ、おさん狐といってたいへんに人をよくだます狐がおったそうな。

statement.id: Dalam dongeng "Rubah pencukur" (かみそり狐) di situs Museum Prefektur Tottori, yang dikumpulkan di Hata, Chizu, pada 15 Agustus 1985, Osan kitsune diperkenalkan sebagai rubah yang sangat pandai menipu orang.
statement.en: In the tale "Razor Fox" (かみそり狐) on the Tottori Prefectural Museum site, collected at Hata, Chizu, on 15 August 1985, the Osan kitsune is introduced as a fox that deceives people very well.

claims.quote: おさん狐は頭にアオミドロを被ってよい娘になって、そうしてしゃあしゃあしゃあしゃあやって来て、その青年の前をとっととっととっととっと通って行った。

statement.id: Dalam dongeng itu, Osan kitsune menjelma menjadi gadis cantik dengan ganggang hijau (aomidoro) di kepalanya dan berjalan melewati seorang pemuda.
statement.en: In that tale the Osan kitsune turns into a pretty girl with green algae (aomidoro) on her head and walks past a young man.

claims.quote: その娘はちょっと重箱を出して、それの中へ馬糞をちょっと入れて、そうしてそれを風呂敷に包んで ... 「たいしたもんじゃないけど、おはぎにして持ってきたけえ。」と言って重箱のものを出すそうな。

statement.id: Dalam dongeng itu, si gadis memasukkan kotoran kuda ke dalam kotak bersusun (jūbako) dan membungkusnya dengan kain, lalu mengeluarkan isi kotak itu sambil berkata bahwa ia membawanya sebagai ohagi (kue beras).
statement.en: In that tale the girl puts horse dung into a tiered box (jūbako) and wraps it in a cloth, then takes out the contents saying she brought them as ohagi (rice cakes).

claims.quote: 若者は頭の毛を狐がずっと食いちぎって食いちぎって、めちゃくちゃに髪の毛を食いちぎられて、もう頭から血が出ているそうな。 おさん狐は人をよく坊主にするいうことだけれど、やっぱり今回も若者が坊主にされてしまったという話。

statement.id: Di akhir dongeng itu rambut si pemuda terkoyak digigit rubah sampai kepalanya berdarah, dan narator mengatakan bahwa Osan kitsune konon sering membuat orang menjadi biksu (gundul), dan kali ini pun si pemuda dijadikan biksu.
statement.en: At the end of that tale the young man’s hair has been bitten off by the fox until his head bleeds, and the narrator says that the Osan kitsune is said to often turn people into monks, and that this time too the young man was made a monk.

claims.quote: 「こりゃあまあ、お寺じゃあない、野原じゃ。野原へ寝とる。こりゃかなわん、はーあ、だまされん言うて来たけど、やっぱりだまされたじゃなあ。」と若者は思って

statement.id: Dalam dongeng itu, si pemuda mendapati bahwa tempat itu bukan kuil melainkan padang rumput tempat ia tidur, dan sadar bahwa ia tetap tertipu.
statement.en: In that tale the young man finds that the place is not a temple but an open field where he has been sleeping, and realises he has been deceived after all.

claims.quote: 関敬吾『日本昔話大成』によると、この話は本格昔話の「人と狐」の中に「剃刀狐」として位置づけられている。

statement.id: Menurut Nihon Mukashibanashi Taisei karya Seki Keigo, kisah ini digolongkan sebagai dongeng "Manusia dan rubah" dengan nama "Rubah pencukur" (剃刀狐).
statement.en: According to Seki Keigo’s Nihon Mukashibanashi Taisei, this tale is classified under the "Man and Fox" type of true folktales as "Razor Fox" (剃刀狐).

topic.en: Ending and opponent in the daimyō procession tale

summary.id: Seorang pengrajin menangkap rubah itu dan dipenggal setelah memuji arak-arakan daimyō yang sungguhan.
summary.en: A craftsman catches the fox and is beheaded after praising a real daimyō procession.

summary.id: Versi lain: Osan kitsune dan tanuki Yozaburō saling menipu dan rubahnya ditebas; versi lain lagi menyebut tanukinya yang ditebas.
summary.en: Another version: Osan kitsune and Yozaburō the tanuki trick each other and the fox is cut down; yet another says the tanuki was cut down.

short_description.id: Panlong adalah naga air mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai jiaolong dan juga menjadi motif seni.
short_description.en: Panlong is an aquatic Chinese mythological dragon resembling jiaolong and also serving as an artistic motif.

long_description.id: Panlong adalah naga air mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai jiaolong dan juga menjadi motif seni. Huainanzi mencatat Panlong sebagai gaya hiasan perunggu. Namanya secara harfiah berarti "naga melingkar".
long_description.en: Panlong is an aquatic Chinese mythological dragon resembling jiaolong and also serving as an artistic motif. The Huainanzi records Panlong as a bronze-decoration style. Its name literally means "coiled dragon".

long_description.id: Kamus Fangyan karya Yang Xiong mendefinisikan panlong sebagai naga yang belum naik ke langit. Komentar Shangshu dazhuan memadankannya dengan jiaoyu dan menyebutnya sangat dipercaya di sarangnya. Sebuah teks klasik lain menyebut motif 蟠龍 yang berangkai bersama badak tidur dan harimau mendekam pada hiasan lonceng besar dan bejana.
long_description.en: The Fangyan dictionary of Yang Xiong defines panlong as a dragon that has not yet ascended to heaven. The Shangshu dazhuan commentary pairs it with the jiaoyu and calls it greatly trusted in its lair. Another classical text lists the 蟠龍 motif linked together with the sleeping rhinoceros and crouching tiger in the decoration of great bells and vessels.

long_description.id: Biji manzhi karya Wang Zhuo menggambarkan pemakaian naga panlong dalam sihir simpatetik untuk hujan: cermin yang punggungnya dihiasi naga melingkar dikatakan dipuja, atau dipakai secara magis, untuk mendatangkan hujan.
long_description.en: The Biji manzhi by Wang Zhuo describes using panlong dragons in sympathetic magic for rain: a mirror adorned on its back with a coiled dragon is said to have been worshipped, or used magically, to cause rain.

cultural_context.id: Dalam Biji manzhi karya Wang Zhuo, cermin yang punggungnya dihiasi naga melingkar dikatakan dipuja atau dipakai secara magis untuk mendatangkan hujan.
cultural_context.en: In Wang Zhuo's Biji manzhi, a mirror adorned on its back with a coiled dragon is said to have been worshipped or used magically to cause rain.

description.id: Dalam sihir simpatetik, cermin berhias panlong dikatakan dipakai untuk mendatangkan hujan.
description.en: In sympathetic magic, a mirror adorned with a panlong is said to have been used to cause rain.

description.en: Chinese classic texts began using panlong in the Han dynasty, and the Huainanzi first records it as a decorative style on bronzes.

claims.quote: Panlong (simplified Chinese: 蟠龙; traditional Chinese: 蟠龍; pinyin: pánlóng; Wade–Giles: p'an-lung; lit. "coiled dragon") is an aquatic dragon resembling a jiaolong 蛟龍 "river dragon; crocodile" in Chinese mythology, an ancient motif in Chinese art, and a proper name.

statement.id: Panlong adalah naga air mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai jiaolong dan juga menjadi motif seni.
statement.en: Panlong is an aquatic Chinese mythological dragon resembling jiaolong and also serving as an artistic motif.

claims.quote: Chinese classic texts began using panlong in the Han dynasty (206 BCE – 220 CE). The (2nd century BCE) Huainanzi first records panlong as a decorative style on Chinese bronzes.

statement.id: Huainanzi mencatat Panlong sebagai gaya hiasan perunggu.
statement.en: The Huainanzi records Panlong as a bronze-decoration style.

claims.quote: The materialist philosopher Yang Xiong (53 BCE – 18 CE) used both panlong and longpan. His Fangyan 方言 "Regional Speech" dictionary defined panlong 蟠龍 "coiled/curled dragon", "Dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven [cf. tianlong "heavenly dragon"] are called p'an-lung."

statement.id: Kamus Fangyan (方言) karya Yang Xiong mendefinisikan panlong 蟠龍 sebagai "naga melingkar": naga yang belum naik ke langit disebut p'an-lung.
statement.en: The Fangyan (方言) dictionary of Yang Xiong defined panlong 蟠龍 as a "coiled dragon": dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven are called p'an-lung.

claims.quote: The (12th century CE) Song dynasty Biji manzhi 碧雞漫志 "Random Jottings from the Green Rooster Quarter" by Wang Zhuo 王灼 describes using panlong dragons in sympathetic magic for rainfall, "where a mirror, adorned on the backside with a "coiled dragon", p'an lung, 盤龍, is said to have been worshipped (rather used in a magical way) in order to cause rain."

statement.id: Biji manzhi (碧雞漫志) karya Wang Zhuo (王灼) menggambarkan pemakaian naga panlong dalam sihir simpatetik untuk hujan: cermin yang punggungnya dihiasi "naga melingkar" (盤龍) dikatakan dipuja, atau digunakan secara magis, untuk mendatangkan hujan.
statement.en: The Biji manzhi (碧雞漫志) by Wang Zhuo (王灼) describes using panlong dragons in sympathetic magic for rainfall: a mirror adorned on its back with a "coiled dragon" (盤龍) is said to have been worshipped, or used magically, to cause rain.

claims.quote: Shangshu dazhuan 尚書大傳 ... commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong and jiaoyu 鮫魚 ... was greatly trusted in its lair

statement.id: Komentar Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) atas Classic of History memadankan panlong dengan jiaoyu (鮫魚) dan menyebut "naga melingkar" itu sangat dipercaya di sarangnya.
statement.en: The Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong with jiaoyu (鮫魚) and says the "coiled dragon" was greatly trusted in its lair.

claims.quote: 大鐘鼎，美重器，華蟲疏鏤，以相繆紾，寢兕伏虎，蟠龍連組，焜昱錯眩，照耀輝煌

statement.id: Sebuah teks klasik yang menyebut hiasan lonceng besar, kuali tripod, dan bejana berharga mencantumkan motif 蟠龍 (naga melingkar) yang berangkai (連組) di samping badak tidur (寢兕) dan harimau mendekam (伏虎).
statement.en: A classical text describing the decoration of great bells, tripods, and precious vessels lists the 蟠龍 (coiled dragon) motif linked in a series (連組) alongside the sleeping rhinoceros (寢兕) and the crouching tiger (伏虎).

short_description.id: Peng adalah burung raksasa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang berubah dari ikan Kun.
short_description.en: Peng is a giant Chinese mythological bird transformed from the fish Kun.

long_description.id: Peng adalah burung raksasa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang berubah dari ikan Kun. Aksara peng memakai unsur burung, sedangkan kun memakai unsur ikan.
long_description.en: Peng is a giant Chinese mythological bird transformed from the fish Kun. The peng character uses a bird component, while kun uses a fish component.

long_description.id: Peng dahulu juga dipakai sebagai varian aksara feng dalam fenghuang. Dapeng dan Dapengniao termasuk sebutan lain yang berarti Peng besar atau burung Peng besar.
long_description.en: Peng was formerly used as a character variant for feng in fenghuang. Dapeng and Dapengniao are alternative names denoting the great Peng or great Peng bird.

long_description.id: Dalam bab Xiaoyao You dalam Zhuangzi, ikan Kun yang sangat besar di Lautan Utara berubah menjadi burung Peng, yang punggungnya luas ribuan li dan sayapnya bagai awan yang menggantung dari langit. Ketika laut bergolak, Peng berpindah ke Lautan Selatan yang disebut Telaga Langit. Teks itu juga memuat seekor burung puyuh kecil yang menertawakan perjalanannya.
long_description.en: In the Xiaoyao You chapter of the Zhuangzi, the immense fish Kun of the Northern Darkness transforms into the bird Peng, whose back spans thousands of li and whose wings are like clouds hanging from the sky. When the sea stirs, the Peng migrates to the Southern Darkness, called the Pool of Heaven. The text also features a small quail that laughs at its journey.

title.en: Kun becomes Peng in the Zhuangzi

claims.quote: A Peng (Chinese: 鵬; pinyin: péng) or Dapeng (大鵬; dàpéng) is a giant bird that transforms from a Kun (鯤; kūn), a giant fish, in Chinese mythology.

statement.id: Peng adalah burung raksasa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang berubah dari ikan Kun.
statement.en: Peng is a giant Chinese mythological bird transformed from the fish Kun.

claims.quote: The Chinese logograms for peng and kun exemplify common radical-phonetic characters. Peng (鵬) combines the "bird radical" (鳥) with a peng (朋; 'friend') phonetic, and kun (鲲; 鯤) combines the "fish radical" (魚) with a kun (昆; 'progeny', 'insect') phonetic.

statement.id: Aksara peng memakai unsur burung, sedangkan kun memakai unsur ikan.
statement.en: The peng character uses a bird component, while kun uses a fish component.

claims.quote: Both the mythic Chinese Peng and Kun names involve word play. Peng (鵬) was anciently a variant Chinese character for feng (鳳) in fenghuang (鳳凰; "Chinese phoenix"), as in the ca. 100 CE Shuowen Jiezi; Kun (鯤) originally meant "fish roe; fry; spawn" (ca. 200 BCE Erya).

statement.id: Peng dahulu juga dipakai sebagai varian aksara feng dalam fenghuang.
statement.en: Peng was formerly used as a character variant for feng in fenghuang.

claims.quote: Synonyms of Peng include Dapeng (大鵬; "Big Peng", "Great Peng") and Dapengniao (大鵬鳥; "Great Peng Bird"). Dapeng is also a place name for a few places in greater China, most notably in Shenzhen and Taiwan.

statement.id: Dapeng dan Dapengniao termasuk sebutan lain yang berarti Peng besar atau burung Peng besar.
statement.en: Dapeng and Dapengniao are alternative names denoting the great Peng or great Peng bird.

short_description.id: Penghou adalah roh pohon dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Tiongkok yang digambarkan seperti anjing hitam tanpa ekor.
short_description.en: Penghou is a tree spirit of Chinese mythology and folklore, described as a tailless black dog.

long_description.id: Penghou ("marquis genderang") adalah roh pohon dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Tiongkok. Dua kitab klasik Tiongkok mencatat versi serupa dari mitosnya. Satu teks menyebut makhluk yang berevolusi dari sari kayu bernama Penghou, berbentuk seperti anjing hitam tanpa ekor, dan dagingnya dapat diolah sebagai makanan.
long_description.en: Penghou ("drumbeat marquis") is a tree spirit of Chinese mythology and folklore. Two Chinese classics record similar versions of its myth. One text holds that what grows out of the essence of wood goes by the name Penghou; it resembles a tailless black dog and its flesh may be prepared as food.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah kisah, Lu Jingshu menyuruh orang menebang pohon kamper besar; darah keluar dan dari pohon itu keluar makhluk berwajah manusia dan bertubuh anjing, yang ia sebut Penghou lalu ia masak dan makan. Dagingnya disebut berasa manis dan asam, hangat, dan tidak beracun, dan memakannya menolak kejahatan dan menguatkan tekad. Dikatakan pula Penghou merasuki pohon yang telah tumbuh seribu tahun.
long_description.en: In one story, Lu Jingshu had a great camphor tree felled; blood came out and a creature with a human face and a dog's body emerged, which he named Penghou, then cooked and ate. Its meat is described as sweet, sour, warm and nontoxic, and eating it wards off evil and strengthens the will. Penghou is also said to possess trees that have grown for a thousand years.

long_description.id: Nama Penghou sampai ke Jepang zaman Edo dan diperkenalkan sebagai yōkai Tiongkok dalam beberapa karya, termasuk Konjaku Hyakki Shūi karya Toriyama Sekien. Karena gema pegunungan (yamabiko) dianggap ditimbulkan roh pohon, Penghou dahulu kadang disamakan dengan yamabiko.
long_description.en: The name Penghou reached Edo-period Japan and was introduced as a Chinese yōkai in several works, including Toriyama Sekien's Konjaku Hyakki Shūi. Because mountain echoes (yamabiko) were thought to be caused by a tree spirit, Penghou was at one time sometimes identified with yamabiko.

short_description.id: Pincoya adalah roh air perempuan dari laut Chiloé yang tariannya menentukan melimpah atau langkanya ikan [pincoya-c01, pincoya-c04].
short_description.en: The Pincoya is a female water spirit of the Chilotan seas whose dance decides whether fish are plentiful or scarce [pincoya-c01, pincoya-c04].

long_description.id: Pincoya adalah roh air perempuan dari laut Chiloé [pincoya-c01], berambut pirang panjang dan sangat cantik [pincoya-c02]. Ia melambangkan kesuburan makhluk laut [pincoya-c03]: jika menari menghadap laut, ikan melimpah; jika menghadap gunung, hasil laut langka [pincoya-c04].
long_description.en: The Pincoya is a female water spirit of the Chilotan seas [pincoya-c01], long-haired, blond and beautiful [pincoya-c02]. She personifies the fertility of sea life [pincoya-c03]: dancing toward the sea brings plenty of fish; toward the mountains, scarcity [pincoya-c04].

long_description.id: Ia putri Millalobo dan Huenchula [pincoya-c05], saudari Sirena chilota, dan istri sekaligus saudari Pincoy [pincoya-c06]. Ketiganya menuntun pelaut yang tenggelam ke kapal hantu Caleuche [pincoya-c07].
long_description.en: She is the daughter of Millalobo and Huenchula [pincoya-c05], sister of the Sirena chilota, and sister and wife of Pincoy [pincoya-c06]. The three guide drowned sailors to the phantom ship Caleuche [pincoya-c07].

long_description.id: Menurut satu kamus mitologi, Pincoya digambarkan bertubuh telanjang, berambut antara kemerahan dan pirang, dengan lekuk tubuh perempuan yang indah [pincoya-c08]. Ia pelindung kerang-kerangan dan ikan di pesisir [pincoya-c11], dan berbeda dengan Sirena, ia tidak berekor ikan [pincoya-c10]. Para encantadora dianggap mampu mengendalikannya lewat penaburan dan ritual lain sehingga ia menyuburkan pantai atau tempat menangkap ikan [pincoya-c09].
long_description.en: According to one mythology dictionary, the Pincoya is described with a naked body, hair between reddish and blond, and beautiful feminine lines [pincoya-c08]. She is a protective patroness of the shellfish and fish of the coast [pincoya-c11], and unlike the Sirena she has no fish tail [pincoya-c10]. The enchantresses were thought able to control her through sowings and other rituals so that she fertilized a beach or fishing site [pincoya-c09].

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Chiloé, Pincoya dipandang dengan penghargaan sebagai sosok yang baik, cantik, dan peduli pada manusia [pincoya-c12]. Kapal hantu Caleuche, tempat para pelaut tenggelam dipandu, tampak utuh sebentar dengan suara pesta lalu lenyap, dan menurut mitos orang mati di atasnya dapat hidup kembali seolah masih hidup [pincoya-c07, pincoya-c13].
long_description.en: In Chiloé mythology the Pincoya is regarded with appreciation as a good, beautiful and caring being [pincoya-c12]. The phantom ship Caleuche, to which drowned sailors are guided, appears briefly intact with sounds of a party and then vanishes, and myth has it that the dead on board can live again as if alive [pincoya-c07, pincoya-c13].

cultural_context.en: In academic terms the pop is described as a social process that rejects people alienated from society. Ancuta writes that creatures like the phi pop have been branded uncivilised superstition and ridiculed in oddball comedies.

short_description.en: Pop or Pob is a cannibalistic spirit of Thai folklore that likes to devour human viscera and is believed to live inside a sorceress.

long_description.id: Pop atau Pob adalah roh kanibal dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang gemar memakan isi perut manusia, dan berkerabat dengan roh Phi Fa. Kata Thai phi biasanya diterjemahkan "roh", tetapi dapat pula berarti hantu, iblis, atau monster. Menurut Ancuta, bagi sarjana asing pop sulit digambarkan karena menyalahi istilah Barat dan sekaligus menampilkan ciri hantu, roh, monster, dan iblis. Thai PBS menyebutnya hantu yang dikenal terutama di Isan dan memakan makanan mentah, dan kepercayaan padanya sering dibicarakan setiap kali terjadi kematian beruntun di desa-desa Isan.
long_description.en: The pop or pob is a cannibalistic spirit of Thai folklore that likes to devour human viscera, and is related to the Phi Fa spirit. The Thai word phi is usually translated "spirit" but can also mean ghost, demon or monster. According to Ancuta, the pop is hard for foreign scholars to describe because it defies Western terms and shows features of ghosts, spirits, monsters and demons alike. Thai PBS calls it a ghost known especially in Isan that eats raw food, and belief in it is often raised whenever deaths occur in succession in Isan villages.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda lama, seorang pelayan mencuri mantra untuk berpindah tubuh dan merebut tubuh pangeran; tubuh pelayan itu kemudian dihancurkan sehingga arwahnya tak bisa kembali dan berpindah dari satu tubuh ke tubuh lain sambil memakan ususnya. Legenda desa menyebut hantu ini hidup di dalam tubuh seorang penyihir dan keluar saat ia tidur, lalu berpindah ke tubuh baru yang menelan air liur si penyihir tua sebelum ia mati. Bila berhasil merasuki seseorang, pop memakan usus orang itu saat tidur.
long_description.en: In an old legend a servant overheard a prince's body-switching spell and took over the prince's body; his own body was then destroyed, so his spirit could not return and went from body to body eating intestines. Village legends say the ghost lives inside a sorceress and leaves her body during sleep, then passes to a new body that swallows the old sorceress's saliva before she dies. Once it has haunted someone, the pop eats that person's intestines as they sleep.

long_description.id: Thai PBS menyebut asal phi pop biasanya orang yang gemar bermain mantra tetapi tak dapat menjaganya atau melanggar pantangan, dan phi pop dapat berjenis perempuan maupun laki-laki. Ancuta menulis bahwa phi pop dikenal memasuki tubuh inang, umumnya perempuan yang bermain ilmu hitam, mewarisi "kutukan" dari leluhur, atau menelan air liur makhluk lain; ia berpindah ke anak-anak setelah inang meninggal karena usia tua, dan dapat berasal dari benda bertuah. Ia sering dianggap tak berbentuk dan dapat merasuki laki-laki maupun perempuan, dan khususnya di kalangan orang Isan dipercaya dapat berwujud hewan, sering anjing hitam. Ancuta juga menulis bahwa phi pop cenderung hidup sebagai manusia di siang hari dan melakukan kegiatan gaib di malam hari.
long_description.en: Thai PBS says the phi pop usually originates in someone fond of incantations who cannot keep them or who breaks a taboo, and that it can be female or male. Ancuta writes that the pop is known to enter a host's body, mostly a woman who dabbled in black magic, inherited the "curse" from ancestors or swallowed another creature's saliva; it moves to the children after the host dies of old age and can originate in auspicious objects. It is often thought shapeless and can possess men and women alike, and among the Isan in particular it is believed able to take animal forms, often a black dog. Ancuta also writes that phi pop tend to live as humans by day and engage in supernatural activities by night.

long_description.id: Folklor Thai membedakan beberapa jenis pop menurut Wikipedia: pop biasa (Pop Thammada) yang mati bersama inangnya, pop keturunan (Pop Chuea) yang diwariskan seperti garis darah, dan pop penukar wajah (Pop Laek Na) yang licik dan menuduh orang tak bersalah. Ha Gom dianggap penguasa semua pop yang tak takut sinar matahari dan tak terpengaruh benda suci.
long_description.en: Thai folklore distinguishes several kinds of pop according to Wikipedia: the ordinary pop (Pop Thammada) that dies with its host, the hereditary pop (Pop Chuea) passed on like a bloodline, and the face-switching pop (Pop Laek Na) that is cunning and accuses the innocent. Ha Gom is regarded as lord of all pops, unafraid of sunlight and unaffected by sacred objects.

long_description.id: Serangan pop tampak sebagai penyakit fisik atau mental pada inang. Cara mengusirnya antara lain memanggil penari penyembuh yang berputar, mantra, atau memukul pop keluar dengan tongkat sakti. Dalam tinjauan akademik, pop disebut proses sosial yang menyingkirkan orang yang terasing, dan yang dituduh diusir dari desa; di Ban Na Bong, Kalasin, pada November 2017, pintu desa ditutup sementara untuk upacara pengusiran, tanpa menunjuk siapa pun sebagai pop dan tanpa kekerasan.
long_description.en: A pop's attack shows as physical or mental illness in the host. Remedies include calling a spinning healing dancer, incantations, or beating the pop out with a magic rod. In academic terms the pop is called a social process that rejects people alienated from the community, and the accused is driven out of the village; at Ban Na Bong in Kalasin in November 2017 the village entrances were temporarily closed for an exorcism that named no one as the pop and used no violence.

claims.quote: Pop or Pob (Thai: ปอบ, pronounced [pɔːp̚]) is a cannibalistic spirit of Thai folklore. It manifests itself as a creature that likes to devour human viscera. Pop is related to the Phi Fa spirit.

statement.id: Pop atau Pob (ปอบ) adalah roh kanibal dalam cerita rakyat Thailand yang gemar memakan isi perut manusia dan berkerabat dengan roh Phi Fa.
statement.en: Pop or Pob (ปอบ) is a cannibalistic spirit of Thai folklore that likes to devour human viscera, related to the Phi Fa spirit.

claims.quote: The servant was unable to re-enter his body as it was destroyed. Henceforth, his revenant spirit goes from one body to another, eating its intestines.

statement.id: Dalam legenda lama, pelayan yang merebut tubuh pangeran tak bisa kembali ke tubuhnya yang telah dihancurkan, sehingga arwahnya berpindah dari tubuh ke tubuh sambil memakan ususnya.
statement.en: In the old legend, the servant who took the prince's body could not return to his destroyed body, so his spirit moves from body to body eating intestines.

claims.quote: Village legends say that this ghost lives inside a sorceress and leaves her body during sleep. Before the witch can die, the spirit has to find a body into which the Pop will be transmitted by consuming some saliva from the old sorceress.

statement.id: Legenda desa menyebut hantu ini hidup di dalam tubuh seorang penyihir dan keluar saat ia tidur; sebelum penyihir itu mati, roh itu harus menemukan tubuh yang menerimanya dengan menelan air liur si penyihir tua.
statement.en: Village legends say the ghost lives inside a sorceress and leaves her body during sleep; before the witch can die, the spirit must find a body into which it is transmitted by consuming some saliva from the old sorceress.

claims.quote: One rumored way to get rid of them is to call in a healing dancer, chasing away the Pop by spinning dance.

statement.id: Salah satu cara mengusir pop adalah memanggil penari penyembuh yang mengusirnya dengan tarian berputar.
statement.en: One rumoured way to get rid of a pop is to call a healing dancer who drives it out with a spinning dance.

claims.quote: In addition, especially among Isan people, it is believed that a Pop can take on the form of various animals. One of the most common is a black dog.

statement.id: Khususnya di kalangan orang Isan, dipercaya pop dapat berwujud berbagai hewan; salah satu yang paling umum adalah anjing hitam.
statement.en: Especially among the Isan people, a pop is believed to be able to take the form of various animals; one of the most common is a black dog.

claims.quote: One of the earliest known literary references to Pop appears in Ramphan Philap (รำพันพิลาป; 'Lament of Bewailment'), a poem written by Sunthorn Phu around 1842–1843.

statement.id: Salah satu rujukan sastra tertua tentang pop terdapat dalam Ramphan Philap, puisi karya Sunthorn Phu sekitar 1842–1843.
statement.en: One of the earliest literary references to pop is in Ramphan Philap, a poem by Sunthorn Phu around 1842–1843.

claims.quote: In November 1892, during the reign of King Rama V, a notable incident was recorded in what is now Uttaradit town. It concerned an old Laotian man of Phuan descent, known as Ta Puang

statement.id: Pada November 1892, di masa Raja Rama V, tercatat sebuah kejadian di wilayah yang kini menjadi kota Uttaradit, menyangkut seorang lelaki tua keturunan Phuan asal Laos bernama Ta Puang.
statement.en: In November 1892, during the reign of King Rama V, an incident was recorded in what is now Uttaradit town, concerning an old Laotian man of Phuan descent known as Ta Puang.

claims.quote: If these ghosts succeed in haunting someone, they will eat that person's intestines while sleeping.

statement.id: Bila hantu ini berhasil merasuki seseorang, ia memakan usus orang itu saat tidur.
statement.en: If these ghosts succeed in haunting someone, they eat that person's intestines while sleeping.

claims.quote: Pop Thammada (ปอบธรรมดา ; 'Ordinary Pop'): This is a person possessed by a Pop spirit. In this case, the person and the Pop are essentially one and the same. When the host dies, the Pop within them dies as well, and the curse does not continue.

statement.id: Pop Thammada ("pop biasa") adalah orang yang dirasuki roh pop; orang dan pop-nya satu dan sama, dan ketika inang mati, pop-nya ikut mati sehingga kutukan tidak berlanjut.
statement.en: Pop Thammada ("ordinary pop") is a person possessed by a pop spirit; the person and the pop are one and the same, and when the host dies the pop dies too, so the curse does not continue.

claims.quote: In some families, Pop is believed to be passed down from parent to child like a bloodline. If the parents are Pop, their children may inherit the spirit after the parents’ death.

statement.id: Pop Chuea ("pop keturunan"): di sebagian keluarga pop dipercaya diwariskan dari orang tua ke anak seperti garis darah, sehingga anak dapat mewarisi roh itu setelah orang tuanya meninggal.
statement.en: Pop Chuea ("hereditary pop"): in some families the pop is believed to pass from parent to child like a bloodline, so children may inherit the spirit after the parents die.

claims.quote: This is a deceitful and cunning variant. When it possesses someone, it refuses to reveal its true master if questioned—often falsely accusing an innocent person instead.

statement.id: Pop Laek Na ("pop penukar wajah") adalah varian licik: ketika merasuki seseorang ia menolak menyebut tuannya yang sebenarnya jika ditanya dan sering menuduh orang tak bersalah.
statement.en: Pop Laek Na ("face-switching pop") is a deceitful, cunning variant: when it possesses someone it refuses to reveal its true master if questioned and often falsely accuses an innocent person.

claims.quote: Ha Gom is considered the supreme entity, the lord of all Pops. It commands lesser Pop spirits and even other types of ghosts as its subordinates.

statement.id: Ha Gom dianggap sosok tertinggi, penguasa semua pop, yang memerintah pop lebih rendah bahkan jenis hantu lain sebagai bawahannya.
statement.en: Ha Gom is considered the supreme entity, lord of all pops, commanding lesser pop spirits and even other kinds of ghosts as subordinates.

claims.quote: Unlike ordinary Pop, Ha Gom is not afraid of sunlight. It can shapeshift into a human or an animal and blend in among people during the day without arousing suspicion. It is unaffected by sacred objects, monks, or holy amulets.

statement.id: Tidak seperti pop biasa, Ha Gom tidak takut sinar matahari, dapat berubah menjadi manusia atau hewan dan berbaur di siang hari, serta tidak terpengaruh benda suci, biksu, atau jimat.
statement.en: Unlike ordinary pops, Ha Gom is not afraid of sunlight, can shapeshift into a human or animal and blend in by day, and is unaffected by sacred objects, monks or holy amulets.

claims.quote: In the technical description, it is described that 'Pop is a social process'. That is to deny people who are alienated from society or the community. The accused is a Pop who will be expelled from the village community.

statement.id: Dalam deskripsi teknis, pop disebut sebagai proses sosial yang menyingkirkan orang yang terasing dari masyarakat; orang yang dituduh pop akan diusir dari komunitas desa.
statement.en: In the technical description, the pop is described as a social process that rejects people alienated from society; the accused pop is expelled from the village community.

claims.quote: Not long after his arrival, three young local women died under mysterious circumstances in quick succession. Rumors soon spread that Ta Puang was, in fact, a Pop in disguise.

statement.id: Tak lama setelah Ta Puang tiba, tiga perempuan muda setempat meninggal berturut-turut dalam keadaan misterius, dan desas-desus menyebarkan bahwa ia sebenarnya pop yang menyamar.
statement.en: Not long after Ta Puang arrived, three young local women died in quick succession under mysterious circumstances, and rumours spread that he was in fact a pop in disguise.

claims.quote: Another famous case occurred in 1908 at Ban Songyae, in what is now Yasothon province, home to St. Michael's Church, the largest wooden church in Thailand. It was said that Pop had possessed members of five families in the village. The situation was finally brought under control when two Catholic priests, Father Desaval and Father Ambrosio, performed an exorcism.

statement.id: Kasus terkenal lain terjadi pada 1908 di Ban Songyae (kini Provinsi Yasothon): pop disebut merasuki anggota lima keluarga, dan keadaan terkendali setelah dua pastor Katolik, Father Desaval dan Father Ambrosio, melakukan eksorsisme.
statement.en: Another famous case occurred in 1908 at Ban Songyae (now Yasothon province): pop was said to have possessed members of five families, and the situation was brought under control after two Catholic priests, Father Desaval and Father Ambrosio, performed an exorcism.

claims.quote: Although many villagers believed that the priests performed an exorcism, historical accounts clarify that the ceremony consisted only of prayers and blessings.

statement.id: Catatan Wikipedia: meski banyak warga mengira para pastor melakukan eksorsisme, catatan sejarah menjelaskan bahwa upacara itu hanya berupa doa dan pemberkatan.
statement.en: A Wikipedia note: although many villagers believed the priests performed an exorcism, historical accounts clarify that the ceremony consisted only of prayers and blessings.

claims.quote: When Thai Rath journalists investigated, they found that she was in fact only an elderly, stooped woman with limited mobility

statement.id: Pada 1996 wartawan Thai Rath menemukan bahwa Yai Sao, perempuan yang dicurigai warga Bang Sue sebagai pop, hanyalah perempuan tua yang bungkuk dengan mobilitas terbatas.
statement.en: In 1996 Thai Rath journalists found that Yai Sao, whom Bang Sue residents suspected of being a pop, was only an elderly, stooped woman with limited mobility.

claims.quote: In 2007, following the mysterious and sudden deaths of four villagers in Kalasin province's Sam Chai district, some 1000 residents raised some 35,000 baht for an exorcism of Pop

statement.id: Pada 2007, setelah empat warga Distrik Sam Chai, Provinsi Kalasin, meninggal mendadak, sekitar 1000 penduduk mengumpulkan sekitar 35.000 baht untuk eksorsisme pop.
statement.en: In 2007, after four villagers in Sam Chai district, Kalasin province, died suddenly, some 1000 residents raised some 35,000 baht for an exorcism of pop.

claims.quote: This event also caused the price of nard (หนาด), a medicinal plant that Thais believe its leaves can ward off ghosts

statement.id: Kehebohan pada 2002 membuat harga nard (หนาด), tanaman obat yang oleh orang Thai dipercaya daunnya menolak hantu, naik tajam.
statement.en: The 2002 scare caused the price of nard (หนาด), a medicinal plant whose leaves Thais believe ward off ghosts, to rise sharply.

claims.quote: Most movies about Pop are comedy horrors.

statement.id: Sebagian besar film tentang pop adalah horor komedi.
statement.en: Most movies about pop are comedy horrors.

claims.quote: Krasue Fat Pop Thai: กระสือฟัดปอบ (1990) with Chutima Naiyana, in which Krasue fights against Pop, judged to be a more malevolent spirit than Krasue by the villagers.

statement.id: Film Krasue Fat Pop (1990) dibintangi Chutima Naiyana; di dalamnya krasue melawan pop yang oleh warga dinilai lebih jahat daripada krasue.
statement.en: The 1990 film Krasue Fat Pop stars Chutima Naiyana; in it the krasue fights the pop, judged by villagers to be a more malevolent spirit than the krasue.

claims.quote: In 2023, Tee Yod, "Death Whisperer" became the fastest Thai film to gross 100 million baht of the year. And its seque, Tee Yod 2, the following year, it became the highest grossing Thai film of the year.

statement.id: Pada 2023 Tee Yod ("Death Whisperer") menjadi film Thai tercepat yang meraih 100 juta baht tahun itu, dan sekuelnya Tee Yod 2 tahun berikutnya menjadi film Thai terlaris tahun itu.
statement.en: In 2023 Tee Yod ("Death Whisperer") became the fastest Thai film of the year to gross 100 million baht, and its sequel Tee Yod 2 the following year became the highest-grossing Thai film of the year.

claims.quote: For foreign scholars, phi pop and phi krasue are notoriously difficult to describe. They certainly defy Western terminology of ghosts, spirits, monsters and demons, but at the same time, exhibit features characteristic of all the above.

statement.id: Menurut Ancuta, bagi sarjana asing phi pop dan phi krasue sulit dijelaskan; keduanya menyalahi istilah Barat tentang hantu, roh, monster, dan iblis, tetapi menampilkan ciri semuanya.
statement.en: According to Ancuta, phi pop and phi krasue are notoriously hard for foreign scholars to describe; they defy Western terms for ghosts, spirits, monsters and demons yet show features of all of them.

claims.quote: Both phi pop and phi krasue are known to enter the living body of a host, predominantly a woman who dabbled in black magic, inherited the “curse” from her ancestors, or became infected by swallowing another creature’s saliva, and reconstitute this body for its purposes.

statement.id: Phi pop dan phi krasue dikenal memasuki tubuh inang yang hidup, umumnya perempuan yang bermain ilmu hitam, mewarisi "kutukan" dari leluhur, atau tertular dengan menelan air liur makhluk lain, lalu membentuk ulang tubuh itu sesuai tujuannya.
statement.en: Phi pop and phi krasue are known to enter the living body of a host, predominantly a woman who dabbled in black magic, inherited the "curse" from ancestors or was infected by swallowing another creature's saliva, and reconstitute that body for their purposes.

claims.quote: They are both commonly identified as “evil spirits” a person gets possessed by, or turns into, as punishment for “the breaking of taboos associated with malevolent forms of magic”

statement.id: Keduanya lazim disebut "roh jahat" yang merasuki atau menjadi bagian dari seseorang sebagai hukuman karena melanggar pantangan yang terkait bentuk-bentuk sihir jahat.
statement.en: Both are commonly identified as "evil spirits" a person gets possessed by or turns into as punishment for breaking taboos associated with malevolent forms of magic.

claims.quote: phi pop moves on to inhabit the children (from father to son, from mother to daughter) after its original host dies of old age

statement.id: Menurut Ancuta, phi pop berpindah mendiami anak-anak (dari ayah ke putra, dari ibu ke putri) setelah inang aslinya meninggal karena usia tua.
statement.en: According to Ancuta, the phi pop moves on to inhabit the children (father to son, mother to daughter) after its original host dies of old age.

claims.quote: Phi pop can additionally originate in auspicious objects, from which they transfer to humans

statement.id: Phi pop juga dapat berasal dari benda-benda bertuah, lalu berpindah ke manusia.
statement.en: The phi pop can also originate in auspicious objects, from which it transfers to humans.

claims.quote: though phi pop is often thought to be shapeless and can possess men and women alike

statement.id: Phi pop sering dianggap tak berbentuk dan dapat merasuki laki-laki maupun perempuan.
statement.en: The phi pop is often thought to be shapeless and can possess men and women alike.

claims.quote: Phi pop’s consumption of its host from within similarly manifests itself as physical or mental illness.

statement.id: Pop yang memakan inangnya dari dalam tampak sebagai penyakit fisik atau mental.
statement.en: The pop's consumption of its host from within manifests as physical or mental illness.

claims.quote: just as it can be sent out with a deliberate intention to harm others

statement.id: Phi pop juga dapat sengaja dikirim untuk mencelakai orang lain.
statement.en: The phi pop can also be sent out deliberately to harm others.

claims.quote: phi pop can sometimes be exorcised by incantations or, more drastically, beaten out of the afflicted person with a magic rod, after which the person continues to live a regular life

statement.id: Phi pop kadang dapat diusir dengan mantra atau, lebih keras, dipukul keluar dari orang yang diserangnya dengan tongkat sakti, lalu orang itu hidup normal kembali; inang asalnya biasanya diasingkan.
statement.en: A phi pop can sometimes be exorcised by incantations or, more drastically, beaten out of the afflicted person with a magic rod, after which that person lives normally again; the originating hosts are usually driven into exile.

claims.quote: Like many Thai animistic beings, phi pop and phi krasue have traditionally been associated with the wilderness, from which they moved into the bordering villages to live among humans.

statement.id: Seperti banyak makhluk animistik Thai, phi pop secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan hutan belantara, lalu pindah ke desa-desa perbatasan untuk hidup di antara manusia.
statement.en: Like many Thai animistic beings, the phi pop has traditionally been associated with the wilderness, from which it moved into bordering villages to live among humans.

claims.quote: Phi pop and phi krasue tend to live as humans by day ... and engage in supernatural activities by night

statement.id: Phi pop cenderung hidup sebagai manusia di siang hari dan melakukan kegiatan gaib di malam hari.
statement.en: Phi pop tend to live as humans by day and engage in supernatural activities by night.

claims.quote: Most commonly translated as “spirits,” the Thai word phi can also refer to ghosts (i.e. dead humans), demons (i.e. evil immaterial spirits), or monsters (corporeal creatures).

statement.id: Kata Thai phi biasanya diterjemahkan "roh" tetapi dapat juga berarti hantu (manusia mati), iblis (roh jahat tak berjasad), atau monster (makhluk berjasad).
statement.en: The Thai word phi is most commonly translated as "spirits" but can also mean ghosts (dead humans), demons (evil immaterial spirits) or monsters (corporeal creatures).

claims.quote: In Lower Northeastern Thailand, these three terms are often used interchangeably to refer to the same creature that signifies a witch-like phi (2016, p. 154), while in other regions phi krasue, phi pop and phi thamop are distinct beings with unique characteristics.

statement.id: Di Thailand timur laut bagian bawah, phi pop, phi krasue, dan phi thamop sering dipakai bergantian untuk makhluk yang sama; di daerah lain ketiganya makhluk berbeda dengan ciri sendiri.
statement.en: In Lower Northeastern Thailand the terms phi pop, phi krasue and phi thamop are often used interchangeably for the same creature, while elsewhere they are distinct beings with their own characteristics.

claims.quote: This paper discusses two such cases, Paul Spurrier’s film P (2005), and Yuthlert Sippapak’s Krasue Valentine (2006), which portray phi pop and phi krasue’s adaptation to city life.

statement.id: Ancuta membahas film P (2005) karya Paul Spurrier, yang menampilkan adaptasi phi pop pada kehidupan kota.
statement.en: Ancuta discusses Paul Spurrier's film P (2005), which portrays the phi pop's adaptation to city life.

claims.quote: Creatures like phi pop and phi krasue have been branded as uncivilised superstition and ridiculed through their unflattering portrayals in oddball comedies.

statement.id: Makhluk seperti phi pop dicap takhayul tak beradab dan ditertawakan dalam komedi aneh.
statement.en: Creatures like the phi pop have been branded uncivilised superstition and ridiculed in oddball comedies.

claims.quote: ถอดรหัสความเชื่อเรื่อง "ผีปอบ" ซึ่งมักจะถูกหยิบขึ้นมาพูดถึงทุกครั้ง ที่มีปรากฏการณ์ตายติดต่อกัน ของคนในหมู่บ้านชนบทภาคอีสาน
claims.locator: สรุปประเด็นสำคัญ

statement.id: Thai PBS: kepercayaan pada "phi pop" sering dibicarakan setiap kali terjadi kematian beruntun di desa-desa pedesaan Isan.
statement.en: Thai PBS: belief in the "phi pop" is often raised whenever a series of deaths occurs in rural Isan villages.

claims.quote: ต้นเดือนพฤศจิกายน ทางเข้าออก "บ้านนาบง" ถูกปิดตายชั่วคราว เพื่อทำ "พิธีไล่ผีปอบ" ตามความเชื่อของคนอีสาน
claims.locator: สรุปประเด็นสำคัญ

short_description.id: Rantas adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Kashmir, berambut panjang dan berkaki terbalik, yang keluar pada malam bersalju lebat dan namanya dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak.
short_description.en: Rantas is a female creature of Kashmiri folklore, with long hair and reversed feet, who ventures out on heavily snowy nights and whose name is used to frighten children.

long_description.id: Rantas adalah makhluk mitos dari cerita rakyat Kashmir. Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan berambut panjang, bergigi runcing, berkuku panjang, dan berkaki terbalik, yang keluar pada malam bersalju lebat. Namanya dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak agar tetap aman di rumah selama musim dingin.
long_description.en: Rantas is a mythical creature of Kashmiri folklore, pictured as a woman with long hair, sharp teeth, long fingernails and backward-turned feet. She goes out on nights of heavy snowfall, and her name is used to scare children into staying indoors in winter.

long_description.id: Rantas dikatakan menculik laki-laki, menahan mereka sebagai tawanan, lalu menikahi mereka karena dukanya kehilangan kekasihnya. Ia mengembara dan meratap pada malam tanpa bulan dengan kaki yang menghadap ke belakang. Menurut legenda, ia memikat pelancong dengan kecantikannya yang memesona dan baru menunjukkan wujud menakutkannya setelah mereka terpikat.
long_description.en: Rantas is said to abduct men, hold them prisoner and later marry them, out of grief at losing her lover. On nights without a moon she roams and wails, her feet turned the wrong way round. Legend says she tempts unwary travellers with a bewitching beauty and shows her frightening shape only after they are spellbound.

long_description.id: Seorang penulis esai menyebut Raantas biasanya dianggap tinggal di kawasan hutan lebat dan sering mengunjungi desa terdekat pada musim dingin. Dalam cerita rakyat, ia dianggap perayu laki-laki yang licik dan perampas anak-anak. Ia dipercaya memiliki sihir dan dapat menyamar sebagai manusia mana pun; tubuhnya sangat berbulu dan ia murni makhluk malam.
long_description.en: An essay author says the Raantas is generally thought to live in thickly wooded areas and often comes to nearby villages in winter. In folklore she is regarded as a scheming seducer of men and a thief of children. She is believed to have some magic and to be able to pass as any human; her body is covered in thick hair and she is purely a creature of the night.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu kisah, seorang perempuan muda bernama Mokhtah membakar Raantas hidup-hidup dengan menjatuhkan kangri yang menyala ke atasnya. Kisah Lav Lone dan Rantas populer dalam legenda urban Kashmir, dengan lokasi yang masih diperdebatkan.
long_description.en: In one tale a young woman called Mokhtah burns the Raantas alive by dropping a burning kangri over her. The story of Lav Lone and Rantas is popular in Kashmiri urban legend, with its location still disputed.

short_description.id: Sasabonsam adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam cerita rakyat Akan di Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, dan Togo, digambarkan bergigi besi dan tinggal di pohon hutan sambil memangsa orang yang lewat.
short_description.en: The Sasabonsam is a vampire-like being of Akan folklore in Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Togo, pictured with iron teeth and living in forest trees, where it preys on passers-by.

long_description.id: Sasabonsam adalah makhluk mirip vampir dalam cerita rakyat orang Akan di Ghana selatan, serta di Côte d'Ivoire dan Togo; kisahnya juga terbawa ke Jamaika abad ke-18 oleh orang Akan yang diperbudak. Orang Asante di Ghana menyebutnya asasabonsam, sedangkan sumber lain mengenalnya sebagai Asanbosam dari cerita orang Aschanti. Dalam mitologi ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai raksasa pemakan manusia yang khas.
long_description.en: The Sasabonsam is a vampire-like figure told of by Akan communities in southern Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Togo, and its tales reached 18th century Jamaica with enslaved Akan. The Asante of Ghana knew it as the asasabonsam, and other accounts name it Asanbosam in the lore of the Aschanti. Mythology usually casts it as a typical man-eating ogre.

long_description.id: Ia digambarkan bergigi besi dan berambut panjang, hidup di pepohonan hutan, dan memangsa orang yang memasuki wilayahnya dengan menyerang dari atas. Ada yang menyebut matanya besar dan merah, kakinya panjang dengan telapak menghadap dua arah, dan ia suka menjuntaikan kaki dari dahan tinggi untuk menjerat pemburu. Versi lain memberinya kaki berpengait besi, enam lengan, atau ciri kelelawar dengan sayap selebar hampir 20 kaki.
long_description.en: It is pictured with teeth of iron and long hair, dwelling in forest trees and preying from above on anyone who enters its territory. Some accounts give it large red eyes and long legs with feet facing both ways, and say it likes to hang its legs from a high branch to snare hunters. Other versions add iron hooks for feet, six arms, or bat-like traits with wings almost 20 feet across.

long_description.id: Sebuah buku etnografi lama menggolongkan Sasabonsum sebagai satu jenis dewa. Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk mengerikan berwujud manusia, berwarna merah dan berambut panjang, sahabat para penyihir, yang menghadang dan melahap pengelana yang sendirian. Ia disebut dewa paling kejam, tidak dapat ditenangkan sekali marah, dan tinggal di hutan gelap bertanah merah; tanah merah itu dianggap berwarna karena darah korbannya.
long_description.en: An old ethnographic book treats Sasabonsum as a class of deity. It portrays him as a frightful red being of human form, a friend of wizards and witches, who ambushes and eats people travelling alone. He is called the cruellest of the gods, impossible to appease once angry, and lives in dark forest where the ground is red, a colour attributed to the blood of his victims.

long_description.id: Sasabonsum yang tinggal di dalam tanah dipandang sebagai dewa gempa, sedangkan yang tinggal dekat pohon randu dipercaya merobohkan pohon itu ke atas orang yang lewat. Penulis catatan itu berpendapat kepercayaan ini lahir dari seringnya korban jiwa akibat pohon tumbang. Ia juga mencatat bahwa pada 1881, ketika gempa kecil merobohkan sebagian dinding kediaman raja di Coomassie, para pendeta menyebut kerusakan itu perbuatan Sasabonsum.
long_description.en: A Sasabonsum living underground was regarded as an earthquake god, while one living by a silk-cotton tree was thought to topple it onto passers-by. The writer of that account believed such ideas grew from the many deaths caused by falling trees. He also recorded that in 1881, when a small tremor brought down part of the wall of the king's residence in Coomassie, the priests blamed Sasabonsum.

cultural_context.id: Penulis sebuah buku etnografi lama menafsirkan bahwa kepercayaan pada Sasabonsum penghuni pohon randu berasal dari banyaknya korban jiwa akibat pohon tumbang, sedangkan Sasabonsum bawah tanah dikaitkan dengan gempa.
cultural_context.en: The author of an old ethnographic book interpreted belief in the tree-dwelling Sasabonsum as arising from deaths caused by falling trees, while the underground Sasabonsum was linked to earthquakes.
